He’s expected to make his final MLB appearance against the Pirates this coming weekend, and we expect a heartwarming atmosphere around Comerica Park.
Should Detroit Tigers fans blame Scott Harris for the team’s disappointing 2026 season?
Objectively speaking, most of Harris’ notable moves haven’t entirely backfired. Kevin McGonigle fell to Detroit in the 2023 draft’s second round, and he’s widely expected to be the AL Rookie of the Year recipient. Veteran second baseman Gleyber Torres has been solid when he’s been healthy over the last two years, and we won't even hold the Verlander signing against Harris.
We must also reiterate that Harris inherited Javier Báez, who has indisputably been one of the worst free agent signings in Tigers history. And although he drew significant pushback for the seemingly underwhelming return for Tarik Skubal, the early returns haven’t been awful on the Tigers’ end.
Top outfield prospect Zyhir Hope has an .822 OPS in nearly 150 plate appearances at Double-A Erie, and we’ll see whether he contends for an Opening Day spot next spring. River Ryan will make his Tigers debut when he starts against the Nationals on Monday night, though Brady Scott has missed much of the last month-plus with an arm injury.
We’ve seen far worse performances by lead baseball executives this year, and Harris shouldn’t warrant being the scapegoat. But you know what they say about deserving…
Framber Valdez, SP
The most significant black mark against Valdez is his three-year, $115 million contract. Had he been a veteran who’d signed a two-year deal worth $30 million, it’d have been easy for the Tigers to accept his 4.06 ERA and diminished strikeout rate. By no means would they have been encouraged heading into 2027, but the context of someone’s salary matters.
Valdez is due nearly $43 million next season and has a $35 million player option for 2028. We'd be shocked if he doesn't opt into the latter year, but could the Tigers possibly dump his salary elsewhere? Probably not, seeing as he also has a $40 million mutual option for 2029.
When you factor in Valdez’s suspension for allegedly throwing at Red Sox shortstop Trevor Story and the subsequent accusations of immaturity, we’re not exactly optimistic about how he’ll fare next year.
Javier Báez, SS/CF
How bad has Báez been in a Tigers uniform, you ask? He's managed just 0.8 bWAR since the start of 2023, and he has a .606 OPS in that time. Across a full 162-game season, the three-time All-Star would have averaged 12 home runs, 69 RBIs, a .262 on-base percentage, and 0.3 bWAR.
This year has been a complete disaster, with an ankle problem costing Báez several months on the injured list. He’s provided Detroit with -0.8 bWAR in nearly 200 plate appearances, and his five walks against 38 strikeouts aren’t exactly encouraging about what lies ahead.
If Báez still has any diehard fans, please step up to the podium. He has one year left on his contract, and his $24 million salary might guarantee he remains in Detroit for the foreseeable future.
Matt Vierling, CF
Vierling lacks the kind of lucrative contract that Valdez and Báez signed, but he’s right alongside the latter among the team’s lowest bWAR scores. The 30-year-old center fielder managed -0.9 bWAR and a .590 OPS in 291 plate appearances before groin and heel injuries prematurely ended his season.
At this point, we’re not sure why Harris — or his potential replacement — would keep Vierling around. He's been worth -1.1 bWAR in only 122 games since the start of last year, so claiming that he lacks value is the understatement of the month.
Zach McKinstry, RF/SS
Of the four players on our list, McKinstry leads the pack with 1.5 bWAR through 124 games. It's too bad that he's managed only 26 RBIs and a .584 OPS across 366 plate appearances. How do you have such a low RBI total with that many plate appearances? Even the argument about him usually hitting no higher than sixth doesn’t work, because we’ve seen plenty of No. 7 hitters have at least 60 RBIs.
Assuming that the Tigers plan to upgrade their outfield this winter, keep your eye on the Yankees’ Trent Grisham; the two-time Gold Glove winner played this year on the qualifying offer, and Detroit might be desperate enough in hoping he can replicate his 34 homers from last season.

title: Roki Sasaki to return to Dodgers this week with a twist
author: Dylan Hernandez
body:
Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs?
The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week.
Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on Tuesday.
The Dodgers had refrained from turning Sasaki into a reliever up to this point because of concerns over their starting rotation. Blake Snell departed from his most recent start after one inning because of a tight groin, but the two-time Cy Young Award winner has since not experienced any problems in that area.
The team believes it has four healthy starters in Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Emmet Sheehan figures to be the rotation’s new insurance policy, as Sheehan has allowed only one run in 17 innings pitched this month.
Roberts said he doesn’t plan to use Sasaki as a quasi-starter who pitches four or five innings following an opener.
Asked if Sasaki would be used in late-inning, high-leverage situations, Roberts replied, “I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably start a clean inning, but, yeah.”
Could he close?
“It won’t be the ninth inning the first time,” Roberts said.
But Roberts acknowledged there was a chance Sasaki could end up in that role.
Sasaki became the Dodgers’ closer last year by default, as the team didn’t have any other options. He saved three games in the postseason.
His move to the bullpen last year came after he missed 4 ½ months because of shoulder problems. He agreed to try pitching in relief under the condition the Dodgers let him start again the next season.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.70 earned-run average this year, but was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in the seven starts he made after the All-Star break.
The Dodgers started this season counting on $69-million free agent addition Edwin Diaz to be their closer, but the three-time All-Star has endured a nightmare of a season that has included two IL stints. In Diaz’s absence, Tanner Scott has served as the team’s primary ninth-inning option and has performed well. However, Scott has posted a 4.97 ERA over his last 14 games.

title: Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
author: Eric Stephen
body:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.
Week 26 results
6-1 record
39 runs scored (5.57 per game)
16 runs allowed (2.29 per game)
.836 pythagorean win percentage
Year to date
96-60 record
780 runs scored (5.00 per game)
587 runs allowed (3.76 per game)
.627 pythagorean win percentage (98-58)
Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

rss_title: Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
rss_body:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.

Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Josue De Paula Shares Honest Message Amid Defensive Criticism
author: TJ French
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula recently made his MLB debut with LA.
He’s had a few very solid moments at the plate, and he’s showcased his impressive plate discipline with an ability to put the ball in play and drive it to the opposite side of the field.
De Paula is still very young, so there’s plenty of time to develop in the coming years, but it’s been a welcome sign thus far in his first handful of MLB action.
Recently, Josue De Paula shared an honest message about dealing with critics to Dodgers reporter Fabian Ardaya.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
Josue De Paula Shares Honest Message
Per Ardaya, here is what Josue De Paula had to say about critics calling out his defense:
“I know that’s a big area of improvement for me,” said De Paula. “I know I got a lot of hate on it. I’m that type: if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. So I’m gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon. It’s gonna take some time.”
Even manager Dave Roberts said that De Paula still has a lot of development to do in the outfield, but it’s been clear De Paula’s defense isn’t the reason he’s in the show.
Ardaya notes that De Paula could have a full-time role with the Dodgers if he shores up his defensive ability:
“The list of helpful voices kept growing over the first 10 days of De Paula’s big-league career. His bat could be special, but De Paula’s path to impacting the 2027 Dodgers becomes a lot easier if he proves he can handle the corner outfield. Mookie Betts, a six-time Gold Glove winner in right field, gave him pointers on how to shag fly balls. Manager Dave Roberts, who spent 10 years patrolling big-league outfields, goes out of his way to ensure De Paula emphasizes the details.”
With all the stars on the Dodgers roster, De Paula’s development is in good hands.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Trade Pitch Offloads Mark Vientos to Pirates
Josue De Paula’s Rookie Campaign Thus Far
Josue De Paula has played in just 10 games for LA, and across his first 38 MLB plate appearances, he’s batted .286 with 10 walks, eight hits, six runs, one home run, and 3 doubles.
Those are very solid numbers to start your MLB career, and especially as a top prospect.
Here is some of De Paula’s prospect bio, per MiLB.com:
“De Paula draws comparisons to a slightly smaller but more athletic version of Yordan Alvarez, thanks to his precocious combination of swing decisions and exit velocities. He offered at just 14 percent of pitches outside the strike zone last season — by comparison, Juan Soto led the Majors with a 16 percent rate — and is supremely comfortable working deep counts in order to find pitches he can punish.”
Yordan Alvarez? The frontrunner for 2026 AL MVP? Not a bad comparison. The future looks bright for Josue De Paula thus far.

title: Josue De Paula responds to criticism about defense with bold prediction
author: Blake Williams
body:
Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut.
Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level.
But his defense in the outfield is a major area of concern, and it’s part of the reason the Dodgers did not call De Paula up until needing a regular DH. As they look ahead to the postseason, De Paula is likely to be limited to being a bat off the bench, given his defensive struggles and the uptick of production from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker.
However, De Paula knows he needs to improve in the outfield, and he’s made it a focus during his first stint at the MLB level.
“Every day. I know that’s a big area of improvement for me, and I know I’ve got a lot of hate on it,” De Paula said. “I’m the type that if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. I’m going to shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.”
De Paula has spent time before every game practicing his defense, working with Dodgers coaches to become more of a usable option in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has taken notice of that, and issued a challenge to De Paula.
“Well, it’s clear he needs to improve on his defense,” Roberts said. “How do you shut people up? You perform better. You practice hard, and that’s how you do it. My challenge to him is to be a complete baseball player, and not just to be a hitter. So he’s putting a lot of good work with Dino every day, and so I welcome that.”
Josue De Paula praises Dodgers teammates
De Paula became the first position player promoted from Double-A by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, creating lofty expectations for himself.
The 21-year-old has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head-on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” De Paula said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”

title: 'Wouldn’t Have Won the World Series': Shohei Ohtani’s Impact on Dodgers Runs Deeper Than Expected as Dave Roberts Reveals Why
author: Srijanee Chakraborty
body:
Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score.
It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for the entire team. It did not go unnoticed by the players.
Roberts recalled on the611podcast that Dodgers veteran Mookie Betts also felt the same.
“Mookie told me a couple of years ago, ‘Doc, we wouldn’t have won the World Series if it wasn’t for Shohei and Yamamoto’. And his point was the discipline that they had every single day,” said Roberts on the podcast.
“How they work with intention every single day, because what that made, it raised the level even higher for our guys. Yamamoto’s day-to-day is three to four hours of intentionality to prepare to throw a bullpen. Shohei is the same way. Roki is getting there, but his culture- that’s what they do.”
The Dodgers signed Ohtani and Yamamoto ahead of the 2024 season.
Ohtani signed the historic 10-year, $700 million contract, while Yamamoto agreed to a massive 12-year, $325 million deal. They proved that every million spent was worth it, as the Dodgers became the World Series champion in 2024 and again in 2025.
Ohtani’s three-homer, 10-strikeout performance in Game 4 of the NLCS, leading to the World Series, is one for the history books. In Game 2 of the 2024 World Series, Ohtani suffered a partial dislocation in his left shoulder while trying to steal a base. But showing incredible toughness, he returned in Game 3 to play against the New York Yankees.
It does not happen without intentionality, and Ohtani’s whole regimen is driven by it. Shotime runs by the clock; from sleeping to bullpen sessions, everything has a fixed schedule. He is Roberts’ “easiest player to manage.”
Last season, Ohtani finished Game 3 of the World Series by reaching base a record-setting 9 times, hitting 2 doubles and 2 homers. The two-way phenom ended the championship batting .333, with 3 homers and 5 RBIs.
Yamamoto was equally impressive.
During the 2024 Fall Classic, Yamamoto threw a one-hit, one-run game, pitching for six innings. In the following edition, he threw in three games and gave up 2 runs to the Toronto Blue Jays, logging a 1.02 ERA.
“When you’re talking about winning 11 games in October, I couldn’t believe more [that] it’s about people, and players you can bet on,” Roberts said on the podcast.
Ohtani and Yamamoto are the players Roberts bet on. Their success is defined by the discipline they rigorously maintain.
When Yamamoto arrived at the Dodgers clubhouse, he brought his own regimen that influenced others.
He relies on flexibility to generate momentum rather than brute strength. Apart from taking bullpen sessions like clockwork, Yamamoto also practices javelin throwing.
He follows a routine designed by his personal trainer and guru, Osamu Yada. Yamamoto also famously keeps a notebook in the dugout to jot down observations from the game. All these habits work together to make him successful.
Roberts also revealed how the presence of these Japanese players influenced the Americans.
“So now, when you get younger players that we have, or even American players that are veterans, they’re like, they’re doing it this intentional, this precise, and that’s the thing that, as a manager, I love,” noted Roberts.
“Because you don’t know where games are gonna go. Games are gonna get hot, and the pressure’s gonna get there. But you have to be able to default to kind of what you know. And that’s what, again, in baseball, can kind of default to doing things the right way.”
And to the Dodgers’ credit, they did not try to ignore the vastly unfamiliar culture. Rather, they chose to learn from it. Perhaps that mentality is what makes them champions.

It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for the entire team. It did not go unnoticed by the players.
Roberts recalled on the611podcast that Dodgers veteran Mookie Betts also felt the same.
“Mookie told me a couple of years ago, ‘Doc, we wouldn’t have won the World Series if it wasn’t for Shohei and Yamamoto’. And his point was the discipline that they had every single day,” said Roberts on the podcast.
“How they work with intention every single day, because what that made, it raised the level even higher for our guys. Yamamoto’s day-to-day is three to four hours of intentionality to prepare to throw a bullpen. Shohei is the same way. Roki is getting there, but his culture- that’s what they do.”
The Dodgers signed Ohtani and Yamamoto ahead of the 2024 season.
Ohtani signed the historic 10-year, $700 million contract, while Yamamoto agreed to a massive 12-year, $325 million deal. They proved that every million spent was worth it, as the Dodgers became the World Series champion in 2024 and again in 2025.
Ohtani’s three-homer, 10-strikeout performance in Game 4 of the NLCS, leading to the World Series, is one for the history books. In Game 2 of the 2024 World Series, Ohtani suffered a partial dislocation in his left shoulder while trying to steal a base. But showing incredible toughness, he returned in Game 3 to play against the New York Yankees.
It does not happen without intentionality, and Ohtani’s whole regimen is driven by it. Shotime runs by the clock; from sleeping to bullpen sessions, everything has a fixed schedule. He is Roberts’ “easiest player to manage.”
Last season, Ohtani finished Game 3 of the World Series by reaching base a record-setting 9 times, hitting 2 doubles and 2 homers. The two-way phenom ended the championship batting .333, with 3 homers and 5 RBIs.
Yamamoto was equally impressive.
During the 2024 Fall Classic, Yamamoto threw a one-hit, one-run game, pitching for six innings. In the following edition, he threw in three games and gave up 2 runs to the Toronto Blue Jays, logging a 1.02 ERA.
“When you’re talking about winning 11 games in October, I couldn’t believe more [that] it’s about people, and players you can bet on,” Roberts said on the podcast.
Ohtani and Yamamoto are the players Roberts bet on. Their success is defined by the discipline they rigorously maintain.
When Yamamoto arrived at the Dodgers clubhouse, he brought his own regimen that influenced others.
He relies on flexibility to generate momentum rather than brute strength. Apart from taking bullpen sessions like clockwork, Yamamoto also practices javelin throwing.
He follows a routine designed by his personal trainer and guru, Osamu Yada. Yamamoto also famously keeps a notebook in the dugout to jot down observations from the game. All these habits work together to make him successful.
Roberts also revealed how the presence of these Japanese players influenced the Americans.
“So now, when you get younger players that we have, or even American players that are veterans, they’re like, they’re doing it this intentional, this precise, and that’s the thing that, as a manager, I love,” noted Roberts.
“Because you don’t know where games are gonna go. Games are gonna get hot, and the pressure’s gonna get there. But you have to be able to default to kind of what you know. And that’s what, again, in baseball, can kind of default to doing things the right way.”
And to the Dodgers’ credit, they did not try to ignore the vastly unfamiliar culture. Rather, they chose to learn from it. Perhaps that mentality is what makes them champions.

title: The Source |SOURCE SPORTS: Air Jordan 4 “Jackie Robinson” Reportedly Set For Historic 80th Anniversary Release
author: Sha Be Allah
body:
Jordan Brand is reportedly preparing to honor one of the most important athletes in American history with a special Air Jordan 4 dedicated to baseball and civil rights icon Jackie Robinson.
The Air Jordan 4 “Jackie Robinson” is expected to be released on April 15, 2027—Jackie Robinson Day and exactly 80 years after Robinson broke Major League Baseball’s modern color barrier when he took the field for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947. The sneakers are expected to retail for $230, with the reported style code JJ9189-101. Jordan Brand has not yet officially announced the release.
According to early reports, the sneaker will arrive in a Sail and Multi-Color scheme heavily inspired by Robinson’s Brooklyn Dodgers roots. The design reportedly takes some cues from the classic “White Cement” Air Jordan 4, combining a light-colored upper with cement detailing and Dodgers blue accents across the eyelets, midsole and branding. Red Jumpman detailing provides another hit of color.
The most significant elements, however, are expected to be the direct tributes to Robinson.
Early information indicates that one heel will feature Nike Air branding while the other will carry Robinson’s universally retired No. 42. “ROBINSON” is also expected to replace the traditional “JORDAN” wording on the interior tongue tag, connecting one of Michael Jordan’s most recognizable silhouettes directly to the baseball pioneer. Images circulating thus far are mock-ups, so the final appearance remains subject to change.
The timing of the reported release carries considerably more meaning than a standard sneaker drop. Robinson debuted for the Brooklyn Dodgers on April 15, 1947, becoming the first Black player of the modern Major League Baseball era. He went on to win the inaugural Rookie of the Year Award in 1947, the National League MVP Award in 1949 and helped Brooklyn capture its first and only World Series championship in 1955.
His No. 42 was retired throughout Major League Baseball in 1997, and every April 15, players, coaches and managers across MLB wear 42 in his honor.
Nike has previously celebrated Robinson through several footwear releases, most notably the highly sought-after Nike Dunk Low “Jackie Robinson” in 2022. The reported 2027 project, however, would bring Robinson’s legacy to the Air Jordan line at retail for the first time, with sneaker reports describing the project as a collaboration involving Robinson’s estate.
And Jordan Brand apparently isn’t stopping with a lifestyle sneaker.
An Air Jordan 4 MCS “Jackie Robinson” baseball cleat is also reportedly planned. The cleated version is expected to feature a predominantly Dodgers-inspired blue colorway along with Robinson’s signature, No. 42 branding and translucent heel tabs incorporating an image of Robinson. Current release calendars list the cleat at $225.
That makes the collection a natural intersection between two athletes whose impact went well beyond their respective playing surfaces.
Michael Jordan transformed basketball, sneaker culture and athlete marketing on a global level. Robinson’s significance reaches even deeper into American history, with his Major League debut challenging baseball’s segregation and helping open doors for generations of Black athletes who followed.
Eight decades after Robinson made his historic Major League debut at Ebbets Field in Brooklyn, breaking baseball’s modern color barrier in a Dodgers uniform, one of sneaker culture’s most recognizable silhouettes is reportedly being used to tell his story to another generation.
The Air Jordan 4 “Jackie Robinson” is currently expected to arrive April 15, 2027, for $230, with the matching baseball cleat also appearing on current release calendars for Jackie Robinson Day. Official images and release information from Jordan Brand are still forthcoming.

title: How Dodgers can fit Josue De Paula onto playoff roster for Corey Seager-like debut
author: Anthony Ranaudo
body:
With Shohei Ohtani landing on the injured list with knee and biceps issues, the Dodgers called Josue De Paula straight up from Double-A Tulsa to the major leagues.
The move meant he was skipping Triple-A entirely, making him the first position player prospect promoted directly from Double-A under Andrew Friedman's tenure and the first Dodgers hitter to skip Triple-A since Yasiel Puig.
The numbers that got him to the big leagues are absurd. De Paula hit .303 with 27 home runs, 104 RBI, and 29 stolen bases at Double-A this season, an .966 OPS, and MLB had him as the No. 6 overall prospect in the game before the promotion.
An advanced hit tool forcing a September call-up before anyone expected it is exactly what makes a Corey Seager comparison worth investigating. Seager got the call in September 2015, made his debut with a two-hit, two-RBI performance, and then hit .337 with four homers and 17 RBI over his final 27 games of the season. That was enough for the Dodgers to name him the starting shortstop job over veteran Jimmy Rollins heading into October.
Seager and the Dodgers didn't make much noise that year, losing to the New York Mets in the NLDS, but it signaled to the team and fanbase they were willing to give the keys to the kid. Seager wound up leading the Dodgers to the 2017 World Series, and again in 2020, finally winning it all. He was World Series MVP and the NLCS MVP the series before, so LA can only hope this move for De Paula follows somewhat similarly.
Where Josue De Paula fits on the Dodgers' playoff roster
So where does De Paula actually fit for October? With Ohtani out, the DH spot is wide open, and De Paula is expected to see the bulk of his early opportunities there, with some reps in the corner outfield mixed in. Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic mentioned, of his first 37 MLB pitches he has seen that were outside the zone, De Paula has only swung at five, and didn't strike out until his 17th big league at-bat.
If he keeps hitting anywhere close to the way he has in his minor league career and glimpses in these first few games, there's a path to him being a useful bat off the bench or a semi-regular DH option on the postseason roster. That combo would be adding thump, energy and speed the Dodgers don't currently have without sacrificing anything on defense, since he'd be playing a spot that doesn't ask much of his glove yet.
None of that matters unless the Dodgers can legally get him on a postseason roster, and that's going to be a bit of a hurdle. Since De Paula wasn't on the 40-man as of September 1, per MLB's rules regarding postseason roster requirements, the Dodgers need to petition the Commissioner's Office, which requires him to have been in the organization by August 31 and to be replacing an injured player who's already served his minimum IL time.
De Paula clears the first requirement, but the second gets a little trickier. Andy Pages, is one of the options for De Paula to replace, but is also inching closer toward a return around the end of September and likely will be reclaiming his everyday outfield job, not sitting out for procedural reasons.
Dalton Rushing is the more interesting case, since he's already been ruled out from catching this season, and if the front office likes what it's seen from De Paula, shifting Rushing to the 60-day IL cleanly, locks in his unavailability. It opens the exact spot the Dodgers would petition around. In that case, Pages plays center and De Paula takes the roster spot Rushing leaves behind.
It's a real procedural step, not a guarantee, and it depends on the front office actually preferring De Paula's over Rushing. It also assumes the Dodgers have no other injuries before then, which is always a roll of the dice. But if the front office wants De Paula's bat and energy in October, this is the door they'll need to walk through.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Get Major Andy Pages Update Ahead of Padres Series
author: TJ French
body:
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 21: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts between Dave Roberts #30 and Rafael Flores Jr. #43 of the Pittsburgh Pirates, after he was hit by a pitch, during the third inning at Dodger Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
The Los Angeles Dodgers are coming off a three-game sweep of the San Francisco Padres this past weekend.
LA, after clinching the NL West, is still looking to secure the NL’s No.2 seed with just six games left on the schedule. Next up for LA is a series with the San Diego Padres, who are rolling right now in MLB. The Dodgers have Monday off after a long stretch of games.
As the Dodgers gear up for a playoff run, they recently received a great piece of news regarding outfielder Andy Pages.
“Andy Pages will be activated before Tuesday’s game vs. SD, Dave Roberts said, with Shohei Ohtani “shortly” after. Roki Sasaki will be available out of the bullpen as Dodgers begin to plot out their October relief roles. Big week for a lot of guys, including Edwin Díaz.”
The MLB regular season has just one week left until the playoffs begin starting next week.
Getting Andy Pages back will be a huge boost for the Dodgers lineup, as he’s been enjoying a solid campaign and contributing heavily to the team’s offense.
GettyLOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – AUGUST 15: Andy Pages #44 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts at the plate during the game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
Andy Pages injured his hand after being hit by a pitch about a month ago, which landed him on the IL.
LA obviously wants to take things slow with Pages to avoid further injury, but the consensus is that he is good to go after doing a lot of off-field hitting work.
A first-time MLB All-Star this season, Pages is batting .272 with 21 home runs, 25 doubles, 80 RBI, and an OPS+ of 117.
TJ French covers the MLB for Heavy. TJ is a graduate of the University of Georgia. He has 2+ years of writing experience.

title: Dodgers pick latest recipients for Tommy Lasorda Award
author: Matthew Moreno
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers presented the fifth annual Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award to Charlie Hough and Joe Amalfitano on Sunday.
The honor is bestowed every season to members of the Dodgers community who embodies the passion, enthusiasm and love for the team that former Hall of Fame manager Tommy Lasorda possessed.
Hough and Amalfitano were recognized during an on-field ceremony before the series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Laura Lasorda, Tommy’s daughter, presented the awards with the ceremony taking place two days before what would have been her father’s 99th birthday.
Charlie Hough
Hough has now spent 46 years in the Dodgers organization as a player, coach or special assistant in the baseball operations department. The Dodgers drafted Hough in the eighth round of the 1966 MLB Draft.
Hough went on to make his MLB debut with the team in 1970, and pitched for the Dodgers in 11 of his astounding 25 seasons. While with L.A., the right-hander went 47-46 with a 3.50 ERA and 60 saves over 401 games (16 starts).
Hough retired after making 21 starts for the then-Florida Marlins in 1994. He was 46 years old at the time.
Overall in his career, Hough finished with a 216-216 record and a 3.75 ERA in 858 games (440 starts).
Joe Amalfitano
Amalfitano, 92, served 14 seasons as third base coach on Lasorda’s Dodgers staff from 1983-96. He also was a senior adviser in baseball operations from 2002-04. Overall, Amalfitano amassed 67 seasons in professional baseball as a Major League player with the New York/San Francisco Giants, Houston Colt .45s and Chicago Cubs (1954-67).
Amalfitano’s baseball career also included serving as manager with the Cubs (1979-81) and a front office executive. As a player, Amalfitano collected 418 hits across 10 seasons in the Majors.
Tommy Lasorda Bleed Dodger Blue Award history
The inaugural Tommy Lasorda Award went to Rosalind Wyman, who was the key figure in bringing the Dodgers to Los Angeles from Brooklyn in 1958.
She additionally was influential in helping the Giants relocate from New York while also helping the Lakers move to Los Angeles from Minneapolis.
The second annual Tommy Lasorda Bleed Dodger Blue Award went to John Shoemaker in 2023, and Steve Yeager was the recipient in 2024.
For 2025, the Dodgers presented the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award to longtime public relations executive Steve Brener and Hall of Fame broadcaster Jaime Jarrín (2025). Coincidentally, Hough joined Laura for the on-field ceremony to celebrate Brener and Jarrín.

title: Dodgers Notes: Tarik Skubal Away From Team, Dave Roberts' Surprise Admission, LA Demotes Pitcher
author: Gabe Smallson
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, on Sunday and improved to 96-60 on the year. They completed the series sweep of the divisional rivals and notched their fourth-straight win (and 14th of the last 17).
After Jack Dreyer took the start and allowed an earned run in the first inning, Emmet Sheehan pitched the next 5.1 frames and stole the show on the mound. He struck out nine, allowed one hit, one walk and no earned runs.
Offensively, Teoscar Hernndez, Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy and Josue De Paula each had a two-hit game. De Paula was 5-for-10 over the course of the series, just the first of hopefully many more at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the eventual victory, southpaw Tarik Skubal unfortunately had to be placed on the bereavement list. As he deals with his personal matter, it is likely that he will still make one more start (he is next scheduled for Sept. 26) before the postseason.
In other news, manager Dave Roberts made a somewhat surprising admission regarding superstar Mookie Betts. After hitting just .235 before the All-Star break, Betts has completely turned things around and looks like a more familiar version of himself, hitting .322 in his last 30 games.
"I couldn't tell you that I saw this," Roberts said on Saturday regarding Betts' turnaround. "But I just felt that he was stronger. He's worked hard on that. He looks great. He's not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great."
Finally, a Dodgers pitcher was demoted as part of the four-player roster move made on Sunday. The right-hander has an impressive 1.32 ERA across 26 games (27.1 innings) at the Triple-A level, but in 11 appearances with the Dodgers this season, he has an 8.10 ERA across 10 innings of work.
Here's all the latest Dodgers news and stories (click the headline for the full article):

"I'm here to help the team, whatever it is."
Josue De Paula (2-4, 2B) talks with the media after the #Dodgers 3-1 win over the Giants. pic.twitter.com/KcZhvCNugk
Josue De Paula had an impressive showing in his first series at home 
The 21-year-old collected 5 hits in the Dodgers SWEEP of the Giants! https://t.co/N7pNMY7uWv pic.twitter.com/acAwN5mGzu
"I feel like I'm in a much better spot now... Whatever role they want me to do, going forward I'm ready to do it."
Emmet Sheehan (5.1 IP, H, 0 ER, BB, 9 K, 93 P) talks with the media after the #Dodgers 3-1 win over the Giants. pic.twitter.com/F3EwvZ3H9l
Discipline is contagious 
Dave Roberts explains how the Japanese players' work ethic has shaped the Dodgers clubhouse #The611Podcast | @FanDuel pic.twitter.com/pqi0c3g9Tc
Miguel Rojas has more reasons than his teammates to hope #Dodgers get first-round bye. He is scheduled to take the test to become a US citizen on Oct 1. If LAD is playing Wild Card Series would complicate his travel to take test

title: Kyle Tucker rests after fouling ball off right knee
author: Eric Stephen
body:
LOS ANGELES — Kyle Tucker didn’t start on Sunday, one day after fouling a ball off his right knee, but the Dodgers right fielder insisted that he felt fine. This was more of a chance to pair a rest day for Tucker with Monday’s scheduled off day for the team.
“[The off day] wasn’t planned. I just felt that after he took one off the knee, this would have been 10 in a row for him,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s playing well, played a lot. It’s a chance to give him two days, then six in a row to finish the season.”
The injury was in a much higher spot on his leg than the right shin fracture that cost him two months on the injured list during the 2024 season while with the Houston Astros.
Tucker did pinch-hit in the eighth inning on Sunday, and he’s second on the Dodgers in games played (148), starts (141), and plate appearances (602), trailing only Freddie Freeman in all three categories. Tucker is playing the best baseball of his season at the moment with five home runs in his last 10 starts, hitting .417/.500/.972 since September 9.
Notes
Speaking of playing in the outfield on Tuesday, the Dodgers will likely activate center fielder Andy Pages off the injured list to play in the series opener against the San Diego Padres, after he missed the last 27 games after a fastball broke his left hand on August 21.
Pages at the end of this season will have two years, 155 days of major league service time and will be eligible for salary arbitration for the first time as a Super Two player, among the top 70 percent in service time among major leaguers with two years but not yet three years of service time. MLB Trade Rumors last week projected the cutoff for Super Two players this offseason to be two years, 134 days.
Longtime Dodgers third base coach Joey Amalfitano and knuckleballer Charlie Hough were honored on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Sunday’s game as the 2026 winners of the the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award. This is the fifth year of the award, timed close to Lasorda’s birthday, which is Tuesday.

title: Tigers return home to host Nationals in penultimate series of 2026
author: Adam Dubbin
body:
The Detroit Tigers wrapped up their seven-game road trip with an 8-1 loss to the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field, dropping the four-game series to the home team, three games to one. The end of the regular season is mercifully near as the Olde English D returns home to wrap things up.
Next up, the Motor City Kitties head home to welcome the Washington Nationals to Comerica Park for the penultimate series of the summer starting on Monday. The three-game set is one of two in which the Tigers will host National League opponents — a strange way to end the schedule.
Making his Detroit debut in the opener is right-hander River Ryan, who was acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade at the deadline. In the 28-year-old’s two appearances for the Triple-A Toledo Mud Hens, he posted a solid 3.86 ERA but a disturbingly high 1.71 WHIP over just 4 2/3 innings, allowing seven hits (one home run) and a walk while striking out four of the 20 batters he faced.

title: Dodgers get notable update on Shohei Ohtani
author: Renzo Pocholo Salao
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers may be getting Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup before the MLB calendar turns to October.
The Dodgers placed Ohtani on the 15-day IL on Sept. 8 as he continues to deal with lingering knee and bicep injuries. The Japanese slugger began hitting balls off a tee last week in preparation for a return to the lineup.
The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya reported Saturday that Ohtani will come off the injured list on Wednesday. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters that there’s “a good chance” Ohtani gets activated for a return either on Wednesday or Thursday.
Ohtani reportedly swung off a Trajekt Arc machine, which is expected to be the closest he’ll get to facing live pitching before returning to the Dodgers’ lineup. He also managed “between 30 to 40 swings” in the batting cage during L.A.’s win over the San Francisco Giants.
If Ohtani returns on Wednesday, the four-time MVP would have only five regular-season games to get his bat going again before the playoffs. He has only had three at-bats since going 0-for-4 in the Dodgers’ Sept. 2 loss to the St. Louis Cardinals.
Ohtani has all but abandoned any hopes of him pitching again this season, which means the Dodgers likely won’t be benefiting from any ridiculous two-way performances as Shohei had last year.
How quickly Shohei begins to look like himself again at the plate make the difference in October as the Dodgers go for a historic three-peat.

title: MLB roundup: Braves clinch NL East with win over Astros
body:
Field Level Media
                
21 Sep 2026, 11:49 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Erik Williams)
Mike Yastrzemski capped a four-run sixth inning with a three-run homer, and the visiting Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East with a 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
The Braves swept the three-game interleague series and claimed their seventh division pennant over the last nine seasons. Yastrzemski was the last of four batters to reach safely against Astros left-handed reliever Bryan King (3-6), who didn't record a single out and exited after allowing Yastrzemski's 12th homer of the season.
Jose Altuve and Yainer Diaz homered for the spiraling Astros, who will enter the final week of the regular season one game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West.
Astros starter Hunter Brown allowed just three singles and two walks over five shutout innings. Braves starter Martin Perez navigated traffic, allowing just one run on six hits and two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
Rays 5, Red Sox 1
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in two runs apiece during a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays defeated visiting Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
With the win, the Rays completed their final regular-season homestand with an 8-1 record and wrapped their home schedule with a major league-best 55-26 mark.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4 for the Red Sox, who managed just six hits while losing their second straight game.
Pirates 4, Royals 3
Rafael Flores Jr. belted a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning to cap Pittsburgh's three-game sweep over visiting Kansas City. With the win, the Pirates improved to 14-6 in their last 20 games.
Oneil Cruz went deep to lead off the fourth inning and Spencer Horwitz had an RBI single in the sixth for Pittsburgh. Carmen Mlodzinski earned the win after allowing two runs on three hits in three innings.
Vinnie Pasquantino had a pinch-hit two-run homer for the Royals, who have lost four in a row and seven of their past eight games.
Phillies 7, Mets 2
Cristopher Sanchez tossed 6 1/3 solid innings and earned the victory for visiting Philadelphia, which earned a much-needed win over New York.
Luis Arraez was 1-for-4 with two RBIs for the Phillies. Justin Crawford provided insurance in the eighth with a bases-clearing triple off Kodai Senga. Sanchez (18-6) gave up two runs on six hits. Philadelphia sits four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks in the race for the final National League wild card.
Bo Bichette homered for the Mets, who dropped their home finale for the third time in four years, while Brett Baty had a pinch-hit run-scoring single in the seventh. Francisco Alvarez and A.J. Ewing each singled twice.
Cubs 9, Reds 1
Pete Crow-Armstrong tied the major league lead with his 45th home run, and David Peterson held host Cincinnati to one run on three hits in six innings in Chicago's win.
Crow-Armstrong was 3-for-5 with two RBIs, three runs, his 30th double and his 38th stolen base. He matched Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber at 45 homers, and he became the first center fielder in history with 40 home runs, 30 doubles and 30 steals in a season.
Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered for the Cubs. JJ Bleday hit a home run for the Reds, who have dropped three of four.
Cardinals 5, Nationals 3
Leo Bernal's two-run home run capped a three-run eighth inning, and St. Louis rallied for a win against visiting Washington to salvage the finale of the three-game series.
Ivan Herrera tied it 3-3 with one out when he hit his second solo homer of the day. Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless inning for the win. Jose Fermin had two hits for the Cardinals, who had lost four straight.
CJ Abrams homered, and Daylen Lile had a double and a single for Washington, which had won six of seven.
Mariners 2, Rockies 1
Kade Anderson threw seven scoreless innings, allowing just three hits in the longest outing of his rookie season, and visiting Seattle stayed alive in the postseason race with a win over Colorado in Denver.
Dominic Canzone had two hits and two RBIs for Seattle, which gained a game on the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Closer Andres Munoz left the game in the ninth with an apparent right arm injury.
Hunter Goodman's 39th home run of the season couldn't prevent Colorado from moving within one loss of its fourth consecutive 100-loss season.
Blue Jays 7, Rangers 2
Nathan Lukes and Charles McAdoo each had two RBIs to lead Toronto to a win over Texas in Arlington, Texas.
Kazuma Okamoto broke a 2-2 deadlock with an RBI single in the fifth and gave the Blue Jays a lead they would never relinquish as they remained three games back of the final AL wild-card spot. Spencer Arrighetti (9-9) picked up the win, allowing two runs in 2 1/3 innings during a bullpen game.
Jake Burger delivered the Rangers' lone runs on a game-tying two-run homer in the fourth. Jacob deGrom (11-10) had a shaky outing, giving up three runs with five hits in 4 1/3 innings for Texas, which maintained its one-game lead in the AL West despite the defeat.
Brewers 3, Orioles 0
Jacob Misiorowski set the tone with three shutout innings and Milwaukee blanked host Baltimore for the second game in a row to complete a three-game sweep and set a franchise record for regular-season victories.
William Contreras homered, and Cooper Pratt provided two run-scoring singles with two outs. Milwaukee is two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the National League. Misiorowski's ERA dipped to 1.86.
The Orioles further damaged their fading playoff hopes, losing the first three games of the homestand to fall five games back of the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot. Colton Cowser had two of Baltimore's four hits. Orioles starter Brandon Young (9-5) was charged with two runs in six innings.
Diamondbacks 8, Yankees 4
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and Arizona kept its slim National League wild-card chances alive with a victory over New York in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1/3 scoreless innings. The D-backs remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies with six to play.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Twins 8, Angels 0
Dean Kremer allowed one hit over six innings and Alan Roden went 3-for-5 with a home run and four RBIs as Minnesota earned a split of its four-game series with Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Josh Bell had three hits, a walk, two RBIs and a run while Brooks Lee also had three hits and scored three times for Minnesota, which finished with 13 hits. Kremer (4-5) allowed just a fourth-inning leadoff single to Vaughn Grissom.
Ryan Johnson (5-9) suffered the loss for Los Angeles, which finished the 2026 season with a 34-47 home record.
Guardians 1, Athletics 0
Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings to lift Cleveland past the visiting Athletics.
Williams (14-8) gave up only three hits while throwing 63 of 89 pitches for strikes. Steven Kwan had three hits and Cade Smith earned his 39th save as the Guardians swept the series and remain atop the American League Central.
A's starter Jack Perkins (3-12) gave up five hits and one run in six innings. Zack Gelof had two of the team's six hits as the Athletics suffered their sixth straight loss
Dodgers 3, Giants 1
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and Los Angeles completed a three-game sweep of visiting San Francisco.
Tommy Edman homered for the Dodgers, who trailed 1-0 after one inning before Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit with nine strikeouts over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings.
Jung Hoo Lee and Victor Bericoto singled for the only hits for the Giants, who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record. Sam Hentges (1-7) allowed a pair of one-out singles in the seventh before Hernandez's double for a 2-1 edge.
Padres 7, Marlins 3
Jake Cronenworth homered twice and knocked in a season-high five runs while Fernando Tatis Jr. also homered as host San Diego polished off a three-game sweep and finished 6-0 against Miami this season.
The Padres won their fifth straight game and are 13-1 in their last 14 games. Walker Buehler (9-6) worked 6 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and three runs.
Sandy Alcantara (13-11) absorbed the loss for the Marlins after permitting eight hits and four runs over six innings. Alcantara is winless in his last eight starts.
White Sox 8, Tigers 1
Chase Meidroth hit a two-run homer for Chicago and Sam Antonacci's two-run double highlighted a 2-for-4 performance as the White Sox waited through a rain delay of nearly four hours and played in wet, blustery conditions to beat Detroit.
Five pitchers held the Tigers to six hits and five walks as Detroit was limited to a single run for the third time in the series. Huascar Brazoban (6-2), reinstated prior to the game from the 15-day injured list (left lat strain), pitched for the first time since Aug. 24. He allowed a hit in one inning to get his first victory with the White Sox.
Tigers starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed four runs in 3 2/3 innings, giving up four hits before exiting with a trainer. Detroit pitchers allowed eight walks, with White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas (1-for-2) drawing three of them. Eduardo Valencia went 3-for-4 for the Tigers, who were eliminated from postseason contention.
--Field Level Media

rss_body:
Field Level Media
                
21 Sep 2026, 11:49 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Erik Williams)
Mike Yastrzemski capped a four-run sixth inning with a three-run homer, and the visiting Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East with a 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
The Braves swept the three-game interleague series and claimed their seventh division pennant over the last nine seasons. Yastrzemski was the last of four batters to reach safely against Astros left-handed reliever Bryan King (3-6), who didn't record a single out and exited after allowing Yastrzemski's 12th homer of the season.
Jose Altuve and Yainer Diaz homered for the spiraling Astros, who will enter the final week of the regular season one game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West.
Astros starter Hunter Brown allowed just three singles and two walks over five shutout innings. Braves starter Martin Perez navigated traffic, allowing just one run on six hits and two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
Rays 5, Red Sox 1
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in two runs apiece during a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays defeated visiting Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
With the win, the Rays completed their final regular-season homestand with an 8-1 record and wrapped their home schedule with a major league-best 55-26 mark.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4 for the Red Sox, who managed just six hits while losing their second straight game.
Pirates 4, Royals 3
Rafael Flores Jr. belted a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning to cap Pittsburgh's three-game sweep over visiting Kansas City. With the win, the Pirates improved to 14-6 in their last 20 games.

title: Purple Row After Dark: If the Rockies could steal one player
author: James Riggenbach
body:
The Colorado Rockies are 57–99.
Purple Row After Dark: If the Rockies could steal one player
An absurd rule for absurd times: if the worst team in baseball could steal one player from a playoff club, who should the Rockies take?
One more loss will give them their fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they are almost certainly going to finish with the worst record in baseball.
These are absurd times for the Rockies, so I have devised an appropriately absurd rule to help them out.
The team with the worst record in baseball gets to steal one player from a playoff team.
There are, naturally, some restrictions. We’re freezing the playoff field as it stood before games on Sunday, September 20. The player has to come from one of those 12 teams, cannot be a pending free agent, and you cannot take the player who leads his team in FanGraphs WAR. The Rockies also inherit the player’s existing contract.
No, one player is not suddenly turning the Rockies into a contender. But could one poached superstar at least keep this thing from becoming five consecutive 100-loss seasons?
Here’s the board:
| Team | Off limits: fWAR leader | Highest available fWAR | Other players worth considering | 
| Rays | Junior Caminero (5.2) | Drew Rasmussen (4.7) | Jonathan Aranda (3) | 
| Guardians | Parker Messick (4.6) | Steven Kwan (3.4) | Gavin Williams (3.4), Brayan Rocchio (3.3), José Ramírez (2.2) | 
| Rangers | Ezequiel Duran (4.6) | Jacob deGrom (4.2) | Josh Jung (2.9), Wyatt Langford (2.8) | 
| Yankees | Cam Schlittler (6.1) | Ben Rice (4) | Cody Bellinger (3.9), Aaron Judge (2) | 
| Red Sox | Willson Contreras (4.1) | Payton Tolle (4) | Ceddanne Rafaela (3.9), Ranger Suárez (3.7) | 
| White Sox | Miguel Vargas (5) | Chase Meidroth (4) | Tristan Peters (3.9), Sean Burke (3.1) | 
| Brewers | Jacob Misiorowski (6.3) | Brice Turang (5.4) | Jackson Chourio (4), Jake Bauers (3.6) | 
| Dodgers | Shohei Ohtani (6.7) | Yoshinobu Yamamoto (4.7) | Max Muncy (4.3), Andy Pages (3.9) | 
| Braves | Chris Sale (5.7) | Michael Harris II (4) | Matt Olson (4), Drake Baldwin (3.1) | 
| Cubs | Pete Crow-Armstrong (10.2) | Alex Bregman (5) | Dansby Swanson (3.6) | 
| Padres | Fernando Tatis Jr. (5) | Jackson Merrill (4) | Ty France (3.8), Mason Miller (3.7) | 
| Phillies | Cristopher Sánchez (5.8) | Jesús Luzardo (5.6) | Zack Wheeler (3.5), Bryce Harper (3.4) | 
For me, the choice comes down to Brice Turang, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Aaron Judge.
Turang is probably the sensible choice.
At 5.4 fWAR, he would easily lead the Rockies, giving them a legitimate top-end player while immediately solving second base for the foreseeable future. He’s 26, hitting .266/.367/.441 with an .808 OPS, and brings value on both sides of the ball with elite range, strong baserunning and a 95th-percentile walk rate.
It would be a very easy way to make the roster better.
But the Rockies really need starting pitching.
Enter Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He’s 14–8 with a 2.51 ERA, 178 strikeouts and a 0.87 WHIP over 179 innings. His Statcast profile is just as impressive: 100th-percentile pitching run value, 99th-percentile fastball run value, 95th-percentile offspeed run value and a 91st-percentile xERA.
Pitchers are risky, and Yamamoto comes with a lot of money attached. But it’s hard to argue with either the profile or the results, and the addition of the Penner family makes absorbing that contract a lot easier to imagine.
Speaking of high-priced items...
Aaron Judge.
Judge being available is basically a loophole created by our own stupid rule. Injuries have limited him to just 285 plate appearances, which is why he sits at only 2 fWAR, but he’s still hitting .241/.360/.511 with 15 home runs.
And the underlying numbers are still very much Judge: a .396 xwOBA, .569 xSLG, 94.0 mph average exit velocity and a 57.5% hard-hit rate.
It is very hard to look at that and say, “No thanks.”
After all, Aaron Judge is the type of hitter that, if he were playing 81 games a year at Coors Field, I might take out a small loan for season tickets.
So who are you stealing?

Judge being available is basically a loophole created by our own stupid rule. Injuries have limited him to just 285 plate appearances, which is why he sits at only 2 fWAR, but he’s still hitting .241/.360/.511 with 15 home runs.
And the underlying numbers are still very much Judge: a .396 xwOBA, .569 xSLG, 94.0 mph average exit velocity and a 57.5% hard-hit rate.
It is very hard to look at that and say, “No thanks.”
After all, Aaron Judge is the type of hitter that, if he were playing 81 games a year at Coors Field, I might take out a small loan for season tickets.
So who are you stealing?

title: Emmet Sheehan strengthens postseason case as Dodgers sweep Giants
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

title: Gran noticia para los Dodgers: Shohei Ohtani podría volver pronto
author: FOX Deportes
body:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Gran noticia para los Dodgers: Shohei Ohtani podría volver pronto
La recuperación del japonés va por buen camino y está por salir de la lista de lesionados
El regreso de Shohei Ohtani a la parte alta del orden al bat de Los Angeles Dodgers parece estar cada vez más cerca. Tras completar otro día favorable en su rutina de bateo, el estelar pelotero se mantiene firme en su camino para salir de la lista de lesionados. Dave Roberts, manager del equipo angelino, confirmó la alta probabilidad de verlo activo durante la próxima serie frente a los San Diego Padres.
La molestia en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda obligó a aumentar su descanso de quince días. La directiva confía en tenerlo de vuelta este miércoles, justo en el segundo juego de la serie como locales. Sin embargo, su retorno será exclusivo como bateador designado, manteniendo pausada su labor sobre la loma de los disparos.
Su proceso de recuperación dio un salto de calidad tras enfrentar los lanzamientos simulados de la máquina Trajekt. El propio estratega aseguró que el japonés se sintió bastante cómodo luego de tomar entre treinta y cuarenta turnos. Complementando el trabajo físico, el jugador también realizó corridas de bases mientras sus compañeros entrenaban.
El optimismo reina en la plantilla tras la holgada victoria de diez carreras a cuatro frente a San Francisco Giants. La afición angelina ya aguarda con ansias el choque del martes ante San Diego para reencontrarse con su estrella. El bat del fenómeno japonés promete encender la recta final de la temporada regular.
LO MÁS VISTO

title: Dodgers considering Emmet Sheehan for playoff role after gem in win over Giants
author: Dylan Hernandez
body:
Emmet Sheehan’s next start will be in the minor leagues.
The right-hander might be out of sight, but that doesn’t mean he will be out of mind.
His scheduled start Saturday for triple-A Oklahoma City in a Pacific Coast League playoff game is part of a design to prepare him to pitch for the Dodgers in October.
Sheehan has pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
His quote-unquote demotion came after he pitched 5 ⅓ scoreless innings in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ sweep-sealing 3–1 victory over the San Francisco Giants Sunday.
The game was the third Sheehan pitched this month for the Dodgers. His numbers in those three games: 17 innings pitched, one run allowed, 24 strikeouts, three walks.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sent down to Oklahoma City in early August, Sheehan returned to the major leagues earlier this month with a slightly modified arsenal that has significantly improved his results. He’s thrown his curveball more, and his increased inability to change speeds has made his fastball play up even when he’s not touching 97 mph with it.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94–95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said. “So I think that’s something that, that’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it, 85 pitches.”
With the Dodgers expecting to start Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow in the postseason, the team has started the process of moving Sheehan into a relief role by having Jack Dreyer pitch an inning as opener Sunday. Sheehan was down in triple-A over the last week but a roster spot for him was opened up because Skubal went on the bereavement list.
Sheehan entered the game in the second inning and pitched into the seventh. He gave up only one hit and one walk; he struck out nine.
He said he has made it a point to feel “free and easy” with his delivery.

title: Dodgers superan al bullpen de Gigantes en triunfo 3-1 y barren la serie de 3 juegos
author: Associated Press Spanish
body:
Por DAN GREENSPAN
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Kiké Hernández conectó un doble productor que puso a su equipo por delante en la séptima entrada, Emmet Sheehan no permitió carreras en 5 1/3 innings, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 3-1 a los Gigantes de San Francisco el domingo para completar una barrida de tres juegos.
El boricua Hernández atacó el primer lanzamiento que vio de Sam Hentges (1-7) e impulsó a Max Muncy para poner a los Dodgers arriba 2-1. Muncy añadió una carrera de seguridad con un sencillo en la octava.
Kris Bubic (4-2) lanzó 2/3 de inning para llevarse la victoria, y Tanner Scott se encargó de la novena entrada para su 23er salvamento.
Sheehan aprovechó al máximo un juego de bullpen para reforzar sus credenciales de cara a integrar el roster de postemporada de los Dodgers como relevista largo. Ponchó a nueve, permitió un hit y otorgó una base por bolas después de relevar a Jack Dreyer en la segunda entrada.
Matt Wilkinson permitió tres hits y no dio bases por bolas, además de ponchar a seis en cinco episodios sin permitir carreras, pero el bullpen de los Gigantes se vino abajo. El zurdo de 23 años fue adquirido como parte del canje que envió al receptor Patrick Bailey a Cleveland en mayo.
Tommy Edman conectó un jonrón hacia el jardín derecho en la sexta entrada para empatar el juego 1-1, castigando al relevista Carson Seymour con un batazo de 400 pies.
Jonah Cox recibió una base por bolas abriendo la entrada para ayudar a que los Gigantes tomaran ventaja 1-0. Cox llegó a segunda por un mal intento de sorprenderlo en la inicial por parte de Dreyer antes de robarse la tercera, y un sencillo de Victor Bericoto lo remolcó.
___
