Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire Pitchers
Emmet Sheehan - SP, LAD (53% rostered)
Blake Snell was removed from his start on Wednesday after one inning with left groin tightness. So, the recently optioned Sheehan might get another chance in the Dodgers’ rotation next week. Shuttled up and down a couple times recently, Sheehan returned to the big leagues for two starts after spending most of August in Triple-A and struck out 15 batters over two starts spanning 11 2/3 innings with just one earned run. He showed a renewed confidence in his fastball and that pitch was missing bats. Again, this is more speculative as Snell’s removal from his start appeared to be at least partially precautionary, but Sheehan could start at home against the Padres next week.
Justin Wrobleski - SP/RP LAD (41% rostered)
A pitcher’s upcoming schedule can be more important than their skill this time of year and Wrobleski is scheduled to face the Rafael Devers-less Giants twice to close the season. Bailey Ober and Zebby Matthews are also streaming options against the Giants. Overall, these are not a trio of pitchers we’d be running to recommend besides for this particular matchup.
Ryan Johnson - SP/RP, LAA (22% rostered)
As the Angels have overhauled their organizational pitching structure, many of their arms have made key adjustments over the last month. Johnson is part of that group, mostly trashing his sinker starting on August 11th. Since then, he has a 2.04 ERA across 39 2/3 innings. It’s still not a great profile – he’s a sidearming righty who doesn’t miss many bats and rarely throws a pitch over 90 mph besides that sinker – but he has a strong cutter, sweeper, and splitter. He’s scheduled to close the season with outings against the Twins and Mariners as a risky streaming option with good results lately.
Andrew Alvarez - SP/RP, WSN (22% rostered)
Alvarez is coming off a gem against the Angels last Saturday with a career-high seven scoreless innings, eight strikeouts, and just one hit allowed. He also walked four batters. In that game, the Angels ran out a lineup with nine right-handed hitters against the left-handed Alvarez and he tore through them with his curveball. His best pitch, it forced 10 of his 15 total whiffs and set up his auxiliary fastball and slider to get called strikes because hitters were so keyed in on the hook. His fastball leaves plenty to be desired at 92 mph with a suboptimal shape, but his curve and slider have a uniquely symbiotic relationship. David Laurila wrote about this on FanGraphs a few months back in an interview with Alvarez. Those two pitches have practically the same velocity and spin axis while the curveball has significantly more depth making hitters struggle to decipher between the two. He’s mildly trustworthy on Saturday against the Cardinals and again against the Mets next weekend.
Jonah Tong - SP, NYM (14% rostered)
Tong turned in another solid start on Monday against the Orioles going six strong with six strikeouts, one walk, and one unearned run. He pushed up his fastball usage heavily in this outing compared to his last, jumping up from 31% to 55% as he found a little bit of extra life on it. That could’ve been weather related as there was a brisk headwind in Citi Field that night – which can help pitchers add a bit of induced vertical break on their fastballs – but it was still the out-pitch Tong had envisioned. Off that dominant fastball, he was able to sequence his changeup, cutter, and curveball more effectively than he has otherwise against major league hitters and looked good overall. He has a huge test against the Phillies this Sunday to try and keep the momentum going before facing the Nationals next week to close the season.
Anthony Molina - RP/SP, SFG (5% rostered)
After being ripped for seven runs by the Padres last week, Molina bounced back well with 5 2/3 scoreless innings and six strikeouts on Tuesday against the Cardinals. He had much better command of his fastball in that more recent outing and that’s important for Molina because while that pitch has plus velocity around 96 mph, its shape is mediocre. So, it needs to be commanded in order to be consistently effective. Otherwise, that pitch is flanked by a quality curveball that’s effective against hitters from both sides of the plate, a solid slider, and a changeup that can miss bats against lefties. He’s scheduled to face the Twins at home next week to close his season.

title: Sasaki to make one more start for Dodgers before regular season concludes
author: Sonja Chen
body:
CINCINNATI -- Heralded by the thumping beat of "Bailalo Rocky," Roki Sasaki opened eyes and electrified Chavez Ravine as the postseason closer during the Dodgers' run to back-to-back championships. The 24-year-old could be poised for a return to the 'pen for L.A.'s three-peat bid -- but he'll make at least one more start before the end of the regular season.
Sasaki has been sidelined since exiting his Aug. 26 start in Atlanta due to a blister on his right middle finger, and he should be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers' final homestand, likely in next week's series against the Padres.
The Dodgers had been considering getting Sasaki reacclimated to the bullpen before the postseason, but they kept the option of him starting open. Sasaki has remained stretched out during his time on the IL, most recently throwing four simulated innings on 48 pitches on Wednesday afternoon in Cincinnati.
"There's benefits both ways," manager Dave Roberts said. "One can argue it's best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up. Because if something does happen, he's built up. The other side is you can assimilate him into the 'pen and get comfortable in that role -- if that is the role. And so again, that's why we have to be really thoughtful with that."
On Wednesday night, the benefit of having additional rotation depth in Sasaki became clear when Blake Snell exited his start against the Reds after just one inning due to left groin tightness. Removing him from the game was seen as more of a precautionary move, but it exposed the somewhat tenuous state of the Dodgers' starting pitching at present.
If the projected postseason rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Snell and Tyler Glasnow remain healthy, then the Dodgers will be in a great place. But there are question marks behind the Big Four. Shohei Ohtani will not pitch again this season. Justin Wrobleski moved to the bullpen and has been much shakier in the second half. Emmet Sheehan, who's currently with Triple-A Oklahoma City, is trending upward after his two most recent starts in the Majors -- but has been inconsistent overall.
Yamamoto is the only member of L.A.'s rotation who has not missed a start this season. Both Skubal and Snell had surgery to remove loose bodies from their left elbows. Glasnow spent more than three months on the IL due to lower back spasms, a recurring issue for him. The Dodgers have been proactive with managing Glasnow's back, as Roberts said he flew back to L.A. early to cut out an additional flight segment in between last Saturday's start in Miami and his next scheduled start on Friday.
Should anything happen to those four, Sasaki would figure to be the next arm up in the rotation. Sasaki has broken out in his second Major League season, even though his 5-5 record and 4.60 ERA may seem underwhelming at first glance. After a shaky start to the campaign, Sasaki introduced a new splitter and began to consistently throw his fastball harder, helping him achieve sustainable success as a starter. He posted a 2.63 ERA in seven starts before the blister issue arose.
Because Sasaki is returning from an injury, there may be some rust for him to knock off. He is still pitching with the blister, but Roberts said he felt good after covering it with Dermabond in his most recent bullpen session and simulated game.
"It's playable," Roberts said. "Given the Dermabond, the time that he'll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it's dang near close to being healed."
The Dodgers expect Sasaki to play an important role on their postseason pitching staff, even though they're not sure which role he'll fulfill -- but it is easier to shorten him up to pitch in relief rather than have to build him back up to start. After the latest injury concern, opting to keep starting on the table for Sasaki has already proven wise.

title: Tarik Skubal luce en la loma y Dodgers superan 3-2 a Rojos para hilvanar 6ta victoria
author: Por BETH HARRIS
body:
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Tarik Skubal lanzó hasta la octava entrada, Teoscar Hernández conectó un sencillo que impulsó la carrera de la ventaja en la quinta y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles resistieron ante los Rojos de Cincinnati para imponerse el martes 3-2 e hilar su sexto triunfo.
El dominicano Hernández se fue de 3-3 con una base por bolas y batea para .484 en sus últimos nueve juegos. Will Smith conectó un jonrón temprano por los líderes del Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
El astro de los Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani, tuvo la noche libre para descansar por persistentes molestias en la rodilla y el bíceps. Freddie Freeman se fue de 4-0 con tres ponches como bateador designado en lugar de Ohtani.
Skubal (9-7) permitió dos carreras y cuatro hits en 7 1/3 entradas. Ponchó a cinco y dio dos bases por bolas.
Los Dodgers han ganado en cada una de sus últimas cuatro aperturas.
Desde que se unió al club justo antes de la fecha límite de canjes del 3 de agosto, el pitcher ganador en dos ocasiones del Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana tiene marca de 2-2 con efectividad de 2,84 y 48 ponches contra 10 bases por bolas en siete aperturas.
Tanner Scott lanzó la novena para acreditarse su 22º salvamento.

title: Andrew Friedman Comments on Shohei Ohtani’s Injury Recovery Ahead of MLB Playoffs
author: Miracle Dimwesh
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers received an encouraging update on Shohei Ohtani as they prepare for the postseason.
Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Ohtani is "progressing well" after recently resuming light baseball activities. Friedman also said he expects the two-way star to return during the regular season.
Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling. The move was backdated to Sept. 8, making him eligible to return Sept. 23.
#Dodgers Andrew Friedman said Shohei Ohtani is “progressing well” since starting to swing a bat earlier this week. Ohtani will be eligible to come off IL on Wednesday.
Friedman: “I expect him back in the regular season.”
How many ABs? Friedman shrugged
Ohtani took his first swings off a tee earlier this week without discomfort. The next steps in his progression are expected to include tracking pitches and eventually facing live pitching as he works to regain his timing.
The Dodgers have reason to be cautious with the veteran as they prepare for October. Ohtani has already made 14 starts as a pitcher this season, going 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA and 95 strikeouts in 85.2 innings.
He has also remained a major part of Los Angeles' lineup when healthy. Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 11 stolen bases and a .380 on-base percentage through 130 games.
His absence has come at an important point in the season, but the Dodgers now have some flexibility after clinching the National League West with an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
That gives Los Angeles an opportunity to prioritize Ohtani's recovery rather than rushing him back. Friedman did not provide a specific number of at-bats Ohtani will receive before the postseason.
For now, the Dodgers will continue monitoring his progress while gradually increasing his baseball activities. Ohtani's potential return before October gives the club another important storyline to follow during the final days of the regular season.

rss_title: Andrew Friedman Comments on Shohei Ohtani’s Injury Recovery Ahead of MLB Playoffs
rss_body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers received an encouraging update on Shohei Ohtani as they prepare for the postseason.
Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Ohtani is "progressing well" after recently resuming light baseball activities. Friedman also said he expects the two-way star to return during the regular season.
Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling. The move was backdated to Sept. 8, making him eligible to return Sept. 23.
#Dodgers Andrew Friedman said Shohei Ohtani is “progressing well” since starting to swing a bat earlier this week. Ohtani will be eligible to come off IL on Wednesday.
Friedman: “I expect him back in the regular season.”
How many ABs? Friedman shrugged
Ohtani took his first swings off a tee earlier this week without discomfort. The next steps in his progression are expected to include tracking pitches and eventually facing live pitching as he works to regain his timing.

title: Mookie Betts sends message that should excite Dodgers fans for playoffs
author: Matthew Moreno
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are National League West champions for the 13th time in the last 14 seasons, and the fifth consecutive year.
More than half of their reign over the division has coincided with Mookie Betts’ tenure with the franchise. Betts now has been part of six Dodgers teams that have won the NL West, and of course three World Series championships as well.
“It’s amazing,” Betts told David Vassegh on SportsNet LA when discussing the 2026 NL West title. “Obviously it’s not just me. We’ve got a great group of guys. It’s fun. Step one. We’ve got a long way to go, but winning is always fun.”
Mookie Betts makes promise
Part of the Dodgers’ success this year, especially over the past several weeks, has come because of Betts improving on season-long struggles.
“Thank you for sticking with me,” Betts said when asked if he had a message for Dodgers fans. “I know it was hard. I make it hard sometimes, but thank you for sticking by my side, by our side. We’ve got something special coming.”
With a 14th consecutive postseason berth on the horizon, the Dodgers are still playing for seeding in the NL bracket. Scenarios still open to them range from the No. 1 seed to being third. They enter play Friday trailing the Milwaukee Brewers by two games for the best record in baseball.
At No. 2 in the NL, the Dodgers are four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves for the all-important bye in the first round of the postseason. L.A. does not hold the tiebreaker over the Brewers or Braves.
With respect to Atlanta, the Dodgers missed out on an opportunity to clinch the tiebreaker due to getting swept at Truist Park from Aug. 25-27. Though, the implications and potential playoff preview did not resonate with Betts.
“We’ve won two Wild Card Series, we’ve won with the bye. So I don’t think it really matters,” Betts said of NL seeding during that series. “I mean, if you want to make it matter, sure. But it doesn’t matter when you play. You’re going to have to get timely hits and pitch. There’s no secret or magic formula to it. It’s just about playing good ball.”

title: Rival executive underscores why Edwin Diaz belongs nowhere near Dodgers and how to fix him
author: Pat Ragazzo
body:
It's no secret that Edwin Diaz has had a nightmare first season with the Los Angeles Dodgers. Diaz was brought in on a three-year, $69 million deal in the offseason to be an elite closer for the Dodgers, but things haven't gone according to plan.
He got off to a rough start to the season before undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies from his elbow in late April. This knocked him out for a little over three months, but upon his return, Diaz's performance didn't improve. Just three weeks after being activated, he landed back on the IL with neck inflammation on August 18.
On the season, Diaz has an abysmal 11.85 ERA and four blown saves in 11 chances across 13⅔ innings. He has also struggled on his most recent minor league rehab assignment, allowing five runs, three walks and a hit by pitch in just 0.2 innings two outings ago. As a result, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated that the team could leave Diaz off their postseason roster.
What has gone wrong for Dodgers' closer Edwin Diaz?
One National League executive who spoke with FanSided gave his take on Diaz. The NL executive believes Diaz's lower arm angle has impacted his stuff. Diaz's arm angle has dropped each year since 2022 when it was 23 degrees. It lowered to 20 degrees in 2024 to 19 degrees in 2025 to just 15 degrees this year. This is something Diaz and the Dodgers are actively working to fix.
Diaz's fastball velocity is also down this season. He's averaging 96.3 mph on his four seamer as opposed to 97.2 mph in 2025. Opponents are hitting .441 with a .735 slugging percentage against his fastball. His slider velocity is normal, but hitters have a .323 average with a .516 slugging percentage against it. Last season, batters hit .179 with a .269 slugging percentage versus Diaz's slider.
In addition to his lower arm slot, the executive thinks that Diaz's struggles may have become partly mental after the mechanical/stuff issues. The executive compared Diaz to Tanner Scott, who had a poor first season with the Dodgers last season, and believes an offseason reset might do the trick like it did with Scott.
Scott is not having a good September (7.71 ERA), but has bounced back this season overall to post a 2.87 ERA, 1.02 WHIP, 76 strikeouts and 22 saves in 59.2 innings. He will likely be the Dodgers' closer in the postseason unless Diaz somehow miraculously turns his campaign around -- and fast.
Given the injuries, mechanical woes and mental aspect that comes with all of this, it appears that 2026 will be a lost one for Diaz. The three-time All-Star and three-time Reliever of the Year, has had a disastrous year and the most realistic hope is that he can return to form in 2027.

title: Dodgers Reverse Roki Sasaki Return Plan After Blake Snell Injury
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki is set to return as a starter, though his postseason role remains unclear.
The Dodgers’ plan changed after Blake Snell suffered an injury on Wednesday, September 16th, during his start against the Cincinnati Reds.
Why the Dodgers changed plans
Snell had a sore left groin and left after one inning. The southpaw was optimistic he avoided the worst of the injury, but the Dodgers still face uncertainty about his status.
As a result, if Snell cannot pitch to finish the season or even the start of the postseason, the Dodgers will need to build up Sasaki as a starter to cover themselves.
Sasaki isn’t at his best right now — the Japanese righty is on the injured list with a blister on his middle finger.
He is eligible to be activated, and he just threw a 48-pitch live batting practice that went well, but the organization is waiting to see how they want to roll him out, either throw him in the bullpen now or have him make starts.
“One can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts said. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Will Roki Sasaki make a start?
After Snell’s injury, Roberts was asked again about Sasaki’s likelihood of returning as a starter rather than a reliever, and the skipper said that, to rest everyone properly and for build-up reasons, Sasaki will get a start at some point in the closing days of the season.
“You know, just trying to make sure that guys have ample rest,” Roberts said. “I think his next outing will be as a starter.”
While many fans thought it was a foregone conclusion that Sasaki would move into a reliever role, he could make his first-ever postseason start after a breakout campaign this year.
In his last seven games, he has a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts, 15 walks, and a 1.28 WHIP.
His splitter is a nasty putaway pitch that he throws for strikes, while the slider is coming along as a nice complement.
More importantly than his two offspeed pitches, his fastball sits in the high 90s and has more movement. With that profile, Sasaki would be a devastating postseason reliever, but now he may be called upon for a role no one expects.

title: Dodgers share updated projection for Andy Pages' return from injured list
author: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are returning for their final homestand of the 2026 regular season as National League West champions and on the verge of getting reinforcements back from the injured list.
Edwin Díaz is expected to be activated on Friday, and Andy Pages may not be far behind. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not specify a date for his All-Star outfielder but said Pages was “very likely” to return during the homestand.
Pages has been on the injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fracture. He underwent a procedure that involved inserting a screw into his left hand to accelerate the recovery process without extending the recovery timeline.
Thus, the expectation remained Pages would be back with the Dodgers in four to five weeks from the time of suffering the injury. An additional note is that Pages will forego a rehab assignment prior to getting activated.
The 25-year-old has been swinging a bat over the past several days and took a step forward on Tuesday by hitting off a pitching machine. He then advanced to taking at-bats against the Trajekt machine.
Tommy Edman stepped up in place of Andy Pages
Alek Thomas initially received the bulk of starts in center field but was removed from the roster on Sept. 1 as part of multiple moves.
Since then Tommy Edman has been an effective replacement in center field, but getting Pages back lets the Dodgers get their best nine players in the lineup just in time for the postseason.
Edman’s ability to play all over the field has long been valued by the Dodgers. It was a strong motivation for his acquisition from the St. Louis Cardinals at the 2024 trade deadline and a subsequent contract extension that offseason.
But Edman’s versatility has been even more so valuable lately with Shohei Ohtani and Pages sidelined. Roberts lauded Edman for his ability to impact a game with his glove and bat.
The 31-year-old said he takes pride in doing his best to fill the void left by Pages’ absence.
Now with Pages on the verge of returning, the Dodgers will likely move Edman back to second base but also have the option of further leveraging his positional versatility if needed.

Happy Friday, everyone. The Tigers will be doing their best to topple their division rivals this weekend as we head towards the final week of the season (what? How did that happen??) We have a few little tidbits to get you started for your Friday, including a look at our former ace Tarik Skubal, and our other former ace Justin Verlander who is making headway towards coming back for one final start next weekend.
We also check in on some injured Tigers, some injured superstars, and see which MLB managers might want to freshen up their resumes.
So let's just get right into it.
Detroit Tigers News
- A little roster update.
The Tigers today placed RHP Kyle Finnegan on the 15-day injured list (retroactive to September 16) with left groin inflammation. RHP Ty Madden was recalled from Triple-A Toledo.

And a more general medical update on what's going on with injured Tigers. Looks like Justin Verlander did a bullpen session this week, making it more and more likely we'll see him pitch over Verlander weekend next week.
MLB News
- What would the divisions look like if they were grouped by payroll?
- Cutest first pitch of all time.
- It's not Miggy stealing nachos, but this is pretty delightful.

title: Freddie Freeman’s wife Chelsea Freeman steps beyond Los Angeles Dodgers spotlight with a story of family, style and purpose
author: Global Sports Desk
body:
Freddie Freeman’s wife Chelsea Freeman has built a life that reaches well beyond the baseball field. A recent social media appearance brought fresh attention to her style, but the moment also offered a glimpse into the world she has created away from the Los Angeles Dodgers spotlight. Chelsea Freeman is a mother, businesswoman and familiar presence around Major League Baseball through her husband’s career. From raising three sons with Freddie Freeman to appearing at MLB events and developing her own business interests, her story has continued to grow alongside one of baseball’s biggest names.
Chelsea Freeman’s latest moment showed the personal style she has made her own
Chelsea Freeman recently shared a series of photos wearing a bright yellow mini dress while promoting FashionPass, a US-based clothing and accessories rental service. Her look included summer sandals, a colorful bag, rings and a diamond bracelet, while her makeup remained light and natural.
The photos were taken at a luxury property overlooking the sea. Three images showed Chelsea Freeman outside in the sunlight, while another offered an indoor view of the elegant setting.
The post carried a simple message that matched the mood of the photos.
“A little sunshine in dress form,” Chelsea Freeman captioned her IG post.
The FashionPass collaboration also reflected another side of Chelsea Freeman’s public presence. She has developed a strong social media following by sharing fashion, family moments, travel memories and glimpses of everyday life.
That has allowed her identity to extend beyond being known simply as Freddie Freeman’s wife. Her online presence often gives fans a closer look at the person supporting one of baseball’s most recognizable players while also maintaining interests of her own.
Chelsea Freeman has also remained connected to the wider MLB community. During the 2026 All-Star Game red carpet, she took on an interviewer role and spoke with several baseball stars’ wives and girlfriends.
Family and business have shaped Chelsea Freeman’s life away from the Dodgers
Chelsea Freeman and Freddie Freeman began dating in June 2011 after meeting while Chelsea Freeman was attending the University of Central Florida. The couple became engaged in January 2014 and married on November 22, 2014, at the St. Regis Bal Harbour in Miami Beach, Florida.
The couple have three sons. Frederick Charles Freeman II, known as Charlie, was born in September 2016. Brandon John Freeman was born in December 2020, while Maximus Turner Freeman was born in February 2021.
Motherhood has remained an important part of Chelsea Freeman’s life. She frequently shares family moments online, while her children have also been seen supporting Freddie Freeman during his baseball career.
Her connection to baseball became particularly visible during the 2026 All-Star Game. Chelsea Freeman interviewed Olivia Dunne, the girlfriend of Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes, during a lighthearted Q&A. Olivia Dunne revealed that she carries her identification in her purse so she can get a drink, prompting a laugh from Chelsea Freeman.
Chelsea Freeman also spoke with Kate Upton, wife of Justin Verlander. Their conversation included questions about fashion at home and what Justin Verlander might have done if he had not become a professional baseball player.
Away from those MLB appearances, Chelsea Freeman has pursued her own business path. She founded the Chelsea Freeman Collection, an online boutique offering game-day clothing and merchandise connected to Los Angeles and Atlanta.
Before that, Chelsea Freeman worked as a real estate agent with Keller Williams. She had also worked as a model during her college years.
Her journey has therefore taken several directions. She has experienced the demands of being married to a professional baseball player, built a family with Freddie Freeman and developed interests that belong to her alone.
The latest social media moment may have brought Chelsea Freeman back into the spotlight, but her story is much bigger than one post. Her family, business ventures, public appearances and personal style have helped shape an identity that continues to stand alongside, rather than simply behind, Freddie Freeman’s MLB career.

title: Dodgers notes: Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal
author: Jacob Macofsky
body:
The NL West continues to run through Los Angeles, as the Dodgers clinched their 13th division title over the last 14 seasons with an 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday.
The Dodgers secured their 93rd win— matching their regular season total from last year— thanks in large part to a huge game from Kyle Tucker. Tucker launched his second home run of the four-game set in Cincinnati and collected four hits in five at-bats, finishing just a triple shy of the cycle. For what has undoubtedly been a disappointing first year with his new team, Tucker gave fans a prelude for what they can potentially see from him in October.
Tucker spoke with David Vassegh of SportsNet LA while celebrating their division-clinching win about settling for a double in his final at-bat, noting he wouldn’t have made it safely to third base in his cycle pursuit.
“I tried my best. I don’t think I was going to get there. I probably would’ve been thrown out halfway, but it’s all good.”
Tucker also spoke about the challenges and hurdles he faced repeatedly this season, expressing gratitude for his teammates continuing to stick with him throughout the highs and lows.
“This group is awesome. Everyone supports each other through the ups and downs. We all know where we want to be at the end of the year, and we all just try to help each other out to get there. This is a great group to play with, to play behind, so everyone is super supportive. Everyone knows what we gotta get done.”
With only nine games left for the Dodgers in the regular season, team president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman gave an optimistic update on Shohei Ohtani, noting that they expect him to return from the injured list before their season finale, per Jack Harris of the California Post.
“He’s doing well,” Friedman said, as the team celebrated another National League West title around him at Great American Ball Park. “He’s progressing well.”
“I expect him back in the regular season,” Friedman declared.
Two months ago, Tarik Skubal was still the ace of a Detroit Tigers team on a downward trajectory. On Thursday, Skubal was celebrating the opportunity to pitch in the postseason for a third consecutive season, this time for the reigning two-time World Series champions.
Skubal hopes that the celebrations from Thursday were the first of many more to come as the march for the three-peat is officially in motion, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“First of many,” he said. “… This is checking a box, and once we get to postseason baseball and doing all that stuff, I think it’s going to be a ton of fun.”
Skubal also reflected on the resiliency of this year’s Dodgers, noting their ability to bounce back after a rough month of August with a current record of 11-5 in the month of September, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
“I think there was no panic from this group,” Skubal said. “I think that’s why in big moments, pressure doesn’t really get to these guys.”

title: MLB News: Dodgers clinch, Tarik Skubal, Shohei Ohtani, Aaron Judge, Cade Cavalli, Pete Alonso
author: Ashley MacLennan
body:
Happy Friday, everyone! Lots of little news bites to keep you busy this morning while you’re pretending to do work, or just enjoying your coffee. We look at some of the Mets’ woes, from terrible offseason choices, to their fanbase missing Pete Alonso, to a new and rough-looking injury. We also check in on some injured superstars, as Shohei Ohtani is feeling a little closer to normal, while Aaron Judge was pulled from a game. Uh oh.
We’ll also see which MLB managers might want to start refreshing their resumes, update you on the WPBL postseason, and share the cutest first pitch ever.
Let’s just get right into it.
- Davy Andrews has a fun article that aims to help the TV action character Reacher find better baseball aliases to use at shady motels. Fans of the show will get a kick out of this.
- Tom Verducci spotlights Tarik Skubal and how he’s going to be a difference-maker for the Dodgers this postseason.
- Verducci also looks at a change the Dodgers made to Skubal’s approach on the mound.
- It’s not time to start worrying about Jesus Luzardo’s arm… yet. Story by Michael Baumann.
- The Dodgers have clinched their 13th NL West title in 14 years. Story by Sonja Chen.
- Jessica Camerato reports that the Nationals are in extension talks with Cade Cavalli.
- Fabian Ardaya shares that Shohei Ohtani is feeling “normal…ish”. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- Karl Rasmussen breaks down seven terrible offseason moves the Mets made that could ruin their future.
- Food for thought, what if divisions were arranged by payroll?
- The return of Pete Alonso to Citi Field has Mets fans turning against their own team. Story by Jay Jaffe.
- Kiri Oler keeps us up to date on the advancing WPBL postseason.
- Keith Law admits which prospects he was wrong about. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- The Phillies have claimed Jose Urquidy off waivers from the White Sox. (MLB)
- Brian Murphy looks at six numbers that have defined the Rays’ tremendous season.
- Karl Rasmussen looks at the 10 biggest breakout stars of the 2026 season.
- The Yankees pulled Aaron Judge in the sixth inning of Thursday’s game against the Twins due to lower leg tightness. (ESPN)
- Ken Rosenthal thinks these six managerial positions are the ones most at risk right now. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- Most adorable first pitch EVER.
- Jared Greenspan shares that A’s prospect Ryan Lasko, who was paralyzed in an outfield collision, has been released from his rehab facility, receiving a standing ovation from the clinic’s staff.
- Davy Andrews explains why we won’t be seeing a pitcher join the 120 club this season.
- Ben Clemens tries to make sense of Fernando Tatis Jr’s up and down season.
- Keegan Matheson looks at the personal connection behind George Springer’s Clemente Award nomination.
- How Tommy Pham made a literal elevator pitch to get activated by the White Sox and then immediately made it worth their while. Story by Karl Rasmussen.
- Mets’ Jared Young was carted off the field last night following a collision with one of his teammates. (ESPN)
- Brittany Ghiroli and Sam Blum explain why the sale of the Angels will be unlike anything else we ever see again. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- This is tremendous.
And tomorrow will be a better day than today, Buster. Make it so.

title: 【ＭＬＢ】大谷翔平のＭＶＰが完全消滅…ＥＳＰＮアナリスト「ＭＶＰ争いは終わった」ＰＣＡに確定マーク | 東スポWEB
author: 東スポWeb
body:
ドジャース大谷翔平投手（３２）のＭＶＰの可能性は完全に消滅したようだ。
米スポーツ専門局「ＥＳＰＮ」のアナリスト、ブラッドフォード・ドゥーリトル氏は１８日、「２０２６年のナ・リーグＭＶＰ争いは終わり、今やＰＣＡは歴史との戦いを強いられている」と記した。
ＰＣＡことカブスのピート・クローアームストロング外野手（２４）は４４本塁打を放ち３７盗塁をマークと「４０―４０」も視野に入れた。負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）入りした大谷翔平はもちろんミジオロウスキー（ブルワーズ）、デラクルーズ（レッズ）、サンチェス（フィリーズ）らナ・リーグのライバル達も相手にならないと断じた。
米メディア「スポーティングニュース」も「カブスは今シーズン、ナショナルリーグ中地区で優勝こそ逃したものの、ワイルドカード獲得に向けて順調に進んでおり、ホームアドバンテージとなるワイルドカード上位の座もほぼ確実に手にするだろう。不安定な投手陣にもかかわらず、今シーズンが成功を収めている主な理由はＰＣＡの存在に尽きる。彼は今シーズン、目覚ましい活躍を見せ、メジャーリーグ史上最高のシーズンを送りつつある」とＰＣＡの活躍を詳報した。
続けて「８月上旬まではＭＶＰ争いは大谷とどちらが勝つか不透明だったが、大谷がケガで登板も打撃もできない状況では、ＰＣＡの受賞を阻む者は誰もいない」と〝確定〟を打った。

body:

title: Dodgers news: Yoshinobu Yamamoto caught off guard by Kike Hernandez's wild act
author: Jedd Pagaduan; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Yoshinobu Yamamoto caught off guard by Kike Hernandez's wild act appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers remain the cream of the crop in MLB, as their consistency year after year is something to behold. On Thursday, the Dodgers sealed the inevitable, winning their 13th NL West title in 14 seasons, with an 8-2 victory on the road against the Cincinnati Reds, giving them a 93-60 record on the season thus far.
LA has won everything there is to win over the past decade or so, but winning a division title is never easy even though they've made it look like it, making it a cause for celebration every single time. But the Dodgers, having won so much already, have to spice up their celebrations from time to time the way utility man Kike Hernandez did on Thursday.
Hernandez, during the Dodgers' champagne-popping celebration in the locker room, was caught on camera pouring a bottle of champagne down the shorts of ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Yamamoto appeared to be caught off guard by this wild act from his teammate, and he tried his best afterwards to remove the bottle that Hernandez put inside his shorts.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
It appears Kiké Hernández shoved a bottle of champagne down Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s shorts during the Dodgers division title celebration 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/zE3vycFEaj
— Dodgers Nation (@DodgersNation) September 17, 2026
Hernandez has already won three World Series titles with the Dodgers, so he certainly is no stranger to some out of pocket scenes in the locker room during this sort of celebration. But it's a testament to how close this team is and how comfortable they are with each other that Hernandez can get away with such a wild act that is, of course, all in jest.
Both Hernandez and Yamamoto have been postseason heroes for the Dodgers, with the former starring for them in 2024 and latter pitching his heart out last year. They have already shown that they have the clutch gene, so when the dust settles on this celebration, fans can be certain that both of them will lock in as well as they proceed in their quest to win three consecutive World Series titles.

title: 'Something Special': Dave Roberts’ Clear Message After Dodgers Secure 5th Straight Title
author: Sourav Kumar Ghatak
body:
“Before this season started, they said the Dodgers were ruining baseball. Let’s get four more wins and really ruin baseball!” Dave Roberts set the tone after the Dodgers won the 2025 NLCS to enter the World Series. This time, Roberts didn’t ask to ruin baseball but hoped for something that, incidentally, would be a first in franchise history.
The New York Yankees and the Oakland Athletics are the only two teams in MLB to have a three-peat record. Despite recent dominance of the Dodgers, including winning the NL West title for five straight seasons, a three-peat record is what they still manifest. Winning the World Series in 2026 would thus get the last two seasons’ winners into the exclusive club, and Roberts may just have communicated the same emotion.
“To win 11 games in October, you never know who is gonna be the guy, what that moment is gonna fall to, and many people have lived it in this clubhouse. So my ask is, be ready to be that guy. And like I said, we’re the most talented, we’re the smartest players, we’re the toughest players, and we’re the most hungry. Again, we have something to do unprecedented, and again, 2026 is gonna be something special. So let’s keep the blinders on and celebrate this,” FOX Sports: MLB quoted Roberts after the win over the Reds on Thursday.
The Dodgers secured the 2026 NL West title on Thursday, which was incidentally their 13th in the last 14 seasons. No wonder the team had a champagne bath to celebrate their achievement, but not before their manager took the stage to set the tone for their playoff run.
Achieving a three-peat was what the Dodgers targeted before entering the 2026 season. The 2024 and 2025 World Series winners had no other motivation than to win their third straight. Hence, achieving what would be a first in franchise history would understandably make this season special.
The Dodgers ended their 2025 regular season with a 93-69 record compared to a 93-60 record this season. So, the team is already dominating much better than last season, and what makes it even more special is how the struggling stars were performing in clutch time.
Since the Dodgers splashed $240 million to sign Kyle Tucker in 2026, criticisms have followed him. A .232 season was not what was expected from him in white and blue. However, the former Astros star is surging just at the right time. On Thursday, his four-hit performance helped the Dodgers get over the Reds and clinch their NL West title. Tucker is now 12-for-29 (.414) with four homers over his last eight games.
Furthermore, after a positive update about Shohei Ohtani’s injury, the Dodgers couldn’t ask for more.
“He is back to progress today,” Roberts said Thursday. “He should be getting some coach pitch this week. He’s progressing well; there’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do. I still don’t know when he’ll return, but everything that I hear is really positive.”
The Dodgers fans thus have all the reasons to hope for a three-peat record in 2026.

Winning the World Series in 2026 would thus get the last two seasons’ winners into the exclusive club, and Roberts may just have communicated the same emotion.
“To win 11 games in October, you never know who is gonna be the guy, what that moment is gonna fall to, and many people have lived it in this clubhouse. So my ask is, be ready to be that guy. And like I said, we’re the most talented, we’re the smartest players, we’re the toughest players, and we’re the most hungry. Again, we have something to do unprecedented, and again, 2026 is gonna be something special. So let’s keep the blinders on and celebrate this,” FOX Sports: MLB quoted Roberts after the win over the Reds on Thursday.
The Dodgers secured the 2026 NL West title on Thursday, which was incidentally their 13th in the last 14 seasons. No wonder the team had a champagne bath to celebrate their achievement, but not before their manager took the stage to set the tone for their playoff run.
Achieving a three-peat was what the Dodgers targeted before entering the 2026 season. The 2024 and 2025 World Series winners had no other motivation than to win their third straight. Hence, achieving what would be a first in franchise history would understandably make this season special.
The Dodgers ended their 2025 regular season with a 93-69 record compared to a 93-60 record this season. So, the team is already dominating much better than last season, and what makes it even more special is how the struggling stars were performing in clutch time.
Since the Dodgers splashed $240 million to sign Kyle Tucker in 2026, criticisms have followed him. A .232 season was not what was expected from him in white and blue. However, the former Astros star is surging just at the right time. On Thursday, his four-hit performance helped the Dodgers get over the Reds and clinch their NL West title. Tucker is now 12-for-29 (.414) with four homers over his last eight games.
Furthermore, after a positive update about Shohei Ohtani’s injury, the Dodgers couldn’t ask for more.
“He is back to progress today,” Roberts said Thursday. “He should be getting some coach pitch this week. He’s progressing well; there’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do. I still don’t know when he’ll return, but everything that I hear is really positive.”
The Dodgers fans thus have all the reasons to hope for a three-peat record in 2026.

title: Edwin Díaz regresa a Dodgers y pone en duda el rol de cerrador en 2026
author: Mike
body:
Edwin Díaz está de vuelta en el bullpen de los Dodgers y la noticia trae algo más que alivio: trae una pregunta que el equipo tendrá que responder antes del postemporada. El cerrador puertorriqueño, uno de los más dominantes del circuito cuando está encendido, regresa a Los Ángeles en septiembre de 2026, pero el rol de cerrador ya estaba repartido. Ahora el bullpen más profundo de la Liga Nacional tiene un problema de lujos: demasiado talento para una sola posición.
El regreso que nadie sabe cómo acomodar
Díaz no llega como una pieza de relleno. Llega como el mismo pitcher que alguna vez fue el relevista más emocionante de las Grandes Ligas, el hombre de las trompetas, el que hacía temblar el Citi Field con su entrada. El problema es que los Dodgers construyeron su bullpen asumiendo que él no estaría, y lo hicieron bien. Demasiado bien.
La jerarquía en el cierre de Los Ángeles ya tenía dueño. [DATO PENDIENTE: nombre del cerrador titular de los Dodgers en la temporada 2026 y estadísticas de ERA/saves antes de la llegada de Díaz.] Meter a Díaz en esa ecuación no es sumarle un refuerzo al equipo; es pedirle a alguien que baje un escalón, y en béisbol, los cerradores no bajan escalones fácilmente. El ego va junto con el rol.
Lo que hace interesante la situación no es solo quién cierra, sino cómo responde Díaz. En sus mejores años con los Mets — antes de la lesión de rodilla en el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol 2023 y la reconstrucción que vino después — era el tipo de pitcher que define innings. Ahora firma con un equipo donde nadie lo esperaba para ser el número uno y tendrá que demostrar que puede funcionar en otro papel, o convencer a la dirección de que merece el suyo de vuelta. cómo el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol 2023 marcó a los peloteros latinos
Por qué los Dodgers siguen siendo los favoritos, con o sin esta duda
El talento sobrante es un buen problema. Muy pocas franquicias en la historia reciente de la MLB han podido decir que tienen demasiados buenos relevistas para una sola posición, y los Dodgers de 2026 están en ese punto. La profundidad del bullpen angelino no depende de resolver quién cierra; depende de que todas las piezas ejecuten cuando llegue octubre.
Díaz en roles de séptimo u octavo inning sigue siendo Díaz: su slider sigue siendo uno de sus pitcheos más difíciles de conectar, y su velocidad no ha caído a niveles preocupantes según los reportes de su llegada. [DATO PENDIENTE: velocidad promedio de Díaz en apariciones recientes o spring training 2026 para contrastar con pico de carrera.] El riesgo real no es el físico; es la cabeza. Los cerradores que pasan a roles de preparación tienden a rendir menos no porque les falte talento, sino porque les falta el disparador mental del noveno inning.
Los Dodgers han navegado tensiones de roster más complicadas que esta y han salido campeones. Si alguien puede gestionar el ego del bullpen, es esa organización. Pero Díaz no es un nombre cualquiera — es una figura, un personaje, una marca — y lo que pase con él en estas últimas semanas de temporada regular va a decir mucho sobre cómo Los Ángeles llega al postemporada.
- Edwin Díaz carrera y trayectoria en los Mets

title: ド軍地区V直後、笑顔の大谷翔平が“登場” 由伸やフリーマンらと並び…MLB公式の投稿に反響（THE ANSWER）｜ｄメニューニュース
author: THE ANSWER
body:
敵地レッズ戦に快勝
大リーグのドジャースは17日（日本時間18日）、敵地レッズ戦に8-2で勝利し、5年連続となるナ・リーグ西地区優勝を決めた。負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている大谷翔平投手は歓喜の輪には不在だったが、意外な場所に登場していた。
5年連続の美酒。歓喜の光景に大谷の姿はなかった。上腕二頭筋を痛めてIL入り。今は復帰を目指して回復に努めている。
試合終了直後にMLBは公式Xを更新。最近14シーズンで13度目の地区優勝となったドジャースを称える画像を投稿した。
中央にフリーマンが陣取り、周りを山本由伸、マンシー、ベッツが固める中、大谷も右上で笑みを浮かべていた。
　X上のファンの視線も集中。「大谷翔平さんはポストシーズン、ワールドシリーズで大暴れしてもらいましょう」「大谷翔平　10月は暴れるぜ」「ポストシーズン楽しみにしています」などの声が上がっていた。
（THE ANSWER編集部）

title: MLB 山本由伸、「丁寧な生活」がもたらす抜群の安定感 WBC派遣に慎重姿勢だった球団 先発陣唯一の〝完走〟で米国でも真価証明（SANSPO）｜ｄメニューニュース
body:
【シンシナティ（米オハイオ州）17日（日本時間18日）＝横山尚杜】ドジャース・山本由伸投手（28）は今季もエースの活躍で、移籍初年から3年連続の地区優勝に貢献。ワールドシリーズ3連覇を狙うポストシーズンが迫り、「やっと始まるなという気持ち。あと3、4回できるように頑張りたい」とシャンパンを浴びた。
大車輪の奮闘を見せた昨季から右肩上がりで成績を伸ばした。シーズンの登板を1度残した現時点でチームトップで自己最多の14勝、179回を消化。先発陣でただ一人、開幕からローテーションを守った。
今年3月にはワールド・ベースボール・クラシック（WBC）に出場。球団は前年にワールドシリーズ含むポストシーズンでフル回転した影響を懸念し、派遣に慎重姿勢を見せていたが、「丁寧な生活」を信条とする右腕のコンディションは一度も揺らがず、米国でも真価を証明した。
強豪ド軍で確固たる地位を築き、チームを代表する存在となった。「チーム全体が勝つためにできることを全てやっている。選手も編成も含め、その気持ちでやれていることがチームの強さ」と胸を張った。

title: Tucker's near-cycle clinches LA's 5th straight NL West title, 13th in 14 years
author: Sonja Chen
body:
CINCINNATI -- Try as they might to view 2026 as its own season, everything the Dodgers have done this year is impossible to separate from the larger context of what they have accomplished in more than a decade of excellence.
The Dodgers hit another key milestone in their title defense by reclaiming the NL West crown with an 8-2 victory over the Reds on Thursday afternoon at Great American Ball Park. Three days after their traditional champagne toast in honor of clinching a postseason berth, winning the West brought on a wild clubhouse celebration -- which they hope will be the first of many over the next several weeks.
"You get so mired in each year, it’s hard to have any perspective," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said. "We’ve had our share of troubles this year. Things where we had to work harder than we expected on a couple of fronts. But the important thing is how we finish and how we go into October."
In their record-tying 14 consecutive postseason appearances, the Dodgers have 13 division titles. The only team to unseat them was the 2021 Giants, who edged them in one of the most highly contested NL West races in recent memory.
Since divisional play began in 1969, the Dodgers lead all big league teams with 24 division titles, one more than the Braves -- currently in line to win the NL East -- and three more than the Yankees. Each year's achievements raise the bar for every ensuing year. The expectations facing the Dodgers have become nearly impossible to meet. But they've embraced them gladly.
"There is certainly a higher expectation when, if you don't win the World Series, you fail," manager Dave Roberts said. "But that's kind of part of what you signed up with the Dodgers.”
The Dodgers' offense, whose inconsistency has been a perpetual concern over the course of the season, provided plenty of early support to back a scheduled bullpen game. Kyle Tucker led the way with a four-hit, three-RBI showing, finishing a triple shy of the Dodgers’ first cycle since 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula and Miguel Rojas also knocked in runs.
Justin Wrobleski opened the bullpen game with three perfect innings, and while Blake Treinen surrendered a solo home run in the fourth, Landon Knack pitched four scoreless frames before Seth Halvorsen allowed a run in the ninth.
With nine games remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are far from full strength. Their best hitter, Shohei Ohtani, is on the 15-day IL, as is first-time All-Star Andy Pages. The six-man rotation they carried for most of the season has been reduced to four fully stretched-out starters on the active roster, necessitating Thursday's bullpen game.
"It's been the same thing the last couple years," Muncy said. "We've had guys go down. We've had guys step up in their place. … That's all that we ask, and we've been able to survive a lot."

title: 大谷翔平の“東京開幕ユニ”が競売に 漢字サイン、黄金パッチ付き…数億円規模で落札か
author: Full-Count編集部
body:
大谷翔平の“東京開幕ユニ”が競売に 漢字サイン、黄金パッチ付き…数億円規模で落札か
漢字サイン、「ゴールドMLBロゴマン」のパッチ付き
米オークション会社「ザ・リアレスト」は17日、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手が2025年3月18日に東京ドームで行われた東京シリーズ開幕戦で着用したユニホームをオークションに出品すると発表した。大谷にとって日本でプレーした初のメジャー公式戦の実使用品で、近代の野球ユニホームとして史上最高額、数億円規模での落札が見込まれている。
ユニホームには、前年のMVP受賞者らにのみ着用が許される公式戦初の「ゴールドMLBロゴマン」パッチが付いているほか、背番号付近には直筆の漢字サイン（大谷翔平）や「Opening Day Tokyo Series」「NL MVP」などの手書きの添え書きが施されている。
同社によると、入札は専用サイトですでに開始されており、10月17日に締め切られる。大谷に関連するメモラビリアを巡っては、同試合で着用したスパイクが約44万ドル（約6500万円）で落札されるなど、世界的な高値取引が続いている。
（Full-Count編集部）

title: Edwin Díaz to return to Dodgers on Friday, but not as closer
author: Jack Baer
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made Edwin Díaz the highest-paid reliever in MLB history last offseason. Their return so far has been an 11.85 ERA and two injured list stints.
Díaz's season is set to resume Friday, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters Thursday morning before the team clinched its 13th National League West title in 14 years. When asked what role Díaz will occupy upon returning, Roberts had two words ready.
"Low leverage."
Instead of serving as closer, Díaz will be trying to earn any sort of bullpen role as his team figures out its playoff roster. Roberts made clear that the Dodgers won't just be plugging him into the late innings this time around:
"I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy. You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we're at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That's what he's about."
Díaz has appeared in only 16 games this season. He pitched for three weeks in March and April before hitting the IL with loose bodies in his throwing elbow, then returned in July with even more disastrous results. The Dodgers tried to stick with him as closer, but a stretch of 11 earned runs allowed in nine appearances ended with another trip to the IL on Aug. 18, this time with neck inflammation cited as the reason.
Díaz has been on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City since early September, but the results have been hardly encouraging. He walked seven batters and allowed six runs across five appearances.
His most recent appearance was a scoreless inning, though, with his lone baserunner coming on a two-out double from Miguel Andujar in a 12-0 win over the El Paso Chihuahuas.
That performance was apparently good enough for the Dodgers to decide he was ready for a return to the big leagues, with Roberts saying it was "really good" and "his best one yet."
As far as what the Dodgers are looking for when Díaz returns, Roberts said "Quality strike-throwing and get guys out."
With Díaz scuffling all season, Tanner Scott — who himself had a rough first season in 2025 after signing a big contract with the Dodgers — has primarily stepped in as closer and performed well enough, with a 2.87 ERA and 22 saves in 65 appearances. Amazingly, the Dodgers' current relief struggles are nothing compared to what the team went through last season before winning its second straight World Series.

title: Josue De Paula Makes Honest Dodgers Statement After NL West Clinch
author: TJ French
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West on Thursday afternoon.
With their 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds, the Dodgers captured their 13th division title in the past 14 seasons. LA won the series over the Reds and is now 93-60.
Up next for LA? October baseball.
Following the victory over the Reds on Thursday, rookie prospect Josue De Paula made an honest statement about the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: Mookie Betts Drops Heartfelt Message After Dodgers-Reds Game
Jose De Paula's Message to Dodgers After NL West Clinch
In Thursday's game, Josue De Paula went 1-for-4 with 1 RBI and a walk.
Here was his message following winning the NL West:
"Being on a winning team, I live for those special moments. I can't wait until we start winning in the playoffs. It's going to be cool."
De Paula hasn't played much with LA this season, as he's been busy tearing up the minors, but it's good he can't start wait until the team starts winning in October.
It also has to be a pretty cool moment for De Paula, who has been up with the Dodgers for all of a week and a half, and is already experiencing a division celebration champagne shower.
More MLB on Heavy: Tarik Skubal Sends Hilarious Message to Blake Snell After Reds Win
Josue De Paula's Early Showings in MLB
So far, De Paula has played in just six games for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Across 14 at-bats, he has two hits, including a home run, two runs scored, six walks, and an OPS of .829.
It's not a huge sample size, and De Paula still has plenty of time to develop with the Dodgers.
He is still the Dodgers' #1 prospect.
In 501 ABs in AA this season, he hit 27 home runs, 37 doubles, and 31 stolen bases.

title: Wrobleski fires three perfect innings in start
author: Eric Samulski; Justin Wrobleski
body:
Justin Wrobleski threw three shutout innings, allowing no hits and striking out three against the Reds on Thursday.

title: Dodgers darán más miedo: dos pilares en ofensiva y defensiva se acercan al regreso
author: Pascual Escandón
body:
Dodgers darán más miedo: dos pilares en ofensiva y defensiva se acercan al regreso
Edwin Díaz será activado este viernes ante San Francisco, mientras Andy Pages está cerca de volver tras superar una fractura en la mano izquierda
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles afinan los últimos detalles de su roster mientras se preparan para la postemporada. Con el boleto a octubre ya asegurado, la organización trabaja en recuperar a dos elementos que pueden tener un papel importante: Edwin Díaz y Andy Pages.
La situación de ambos es diferente. Díaz regresará este viernes para el inicio de la serie ante los Gigantes de San Francisco, aunque el mánager Dave Roberts adelantó que el relevista será utilizado inicialmente en situaciones de baja presión. Pages, por su parte, también se perfila para volver durante la actual estancia de los Dodgers en casa, pero todavía no tiene una fecha exacta de activación.
DÍAZ REGRESA, PERO TENDRÁ QUE RECUPERAR LA CONFIANZA
El regreso del puertorriqueño representa uno de los principales temas para el bullpen angelino. Díaz tiene efectividad de 11.85 en 16 apariciones, con 13.2 entradas lanzadas, 19 ponches y un WHIP de 2.56, números que explican la cautela del cuerpo técnico.
El escenario es muy diferente al que se esperaba cuando los Dodgers contrataron al tres veces All-Star durante el invierno para asumir el papel de cerrador.
Roberts ha sido directo al hablar de la situación del relevista y dejó claro que deberá demostrar nuevamente que puede ser una opción confiable en los momentos de mayor presión. Díaz no tiene garantizado recuperar inmediatamente el puesto de cerrador, especialmente con otros relevistas que han asumido responsabilidades importantes durante su ausencia.
La última salida de rehabilitación del boricua fue más alentadora: trabajó una entrada sin permitir carreras en Triple-A, antes de recibir la confirmación de que regresaría al equipo grande.
Sin embargo, sus actuaciones anteriores en las menores habían generado preocupación. Los Dodgers quieren verlo recuperar ritmo y control antes de volver a colocarlo en situaciones de alta exigencia.
PAGES, EL REFUERZO QUE NECESITA LA OFENSIVA
Mientras Díaz deberá reconstruir su lugar dentro del bullpen, Andy Pages representa una alternativa importante para fortalecer la alineación.
El cubano se encuentra en la lista de lesionados debido a una fractura en la mano izquierda y ha estado trabajando progresivamente en su swing. Los Dodgers planean activarlo durante la actual estancia en casa sin enviarlo a una asignación de rehabilitación en las ligas menores.
Antes de la lesión, Pages había establecido números importantes en su segunda temporada completa en Grandes Ligas. En 128 juegos bateó para .272, conectó 21 cuadrangulares, produjo 80 carreras, anotó 72 y robó 12 bases, además de registrar un OPS de .796.
Esos números convierten su regreso en una noticia relevante para una ofensiva que busca llegar completa a octubre.
La intención es que Pages vuelva a ocupar el jardín central, mientras Tommy Edman regresaría a la segunda base cuando el cubano esté disponible.
DOS REGRESOS CON OBJETIVOS MUY DISTINTOS
Los caminos de Díaz y Pages hacia la postemporada serán diferentes.
Díaz tendrá que demostrar que puede volver a ser una alternativa confiable para los innings de mayor presión, mientras que Pages buscará recuperar rápidamente el ritmo ofensivo que tenía antes de sufrir la fractura.
Para los Dodgers, ambos movimientos llegan en un momento particularmente importante. La organización ya consiguió el campeonato de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y aseguró su presencia en la postemporada, pero ahora debe definir qué jugadores llegarán en mejores condiciones al mes de octubre.
El regreso de Pages puede darle mayor profundidad al lineup, mientras que la recuperación de Díaz podría ampliar las alternativas de Roberts en el bullpen.
La serie contra San Francisco marcará el primer paso del regreso de Díaz, mientras Pages espera recibir el alta durante los próximos días. Los dos tendrán poco tiempo para demostrar que están listos para afrontar el escenario de mayor presión de la temporada.

title: Mookie Betts Sends Heartfelt Statement After Dodgers-Reds Game
author: TJ French
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West on Thursday afternoon after an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds. LA ended up winning the series, and its the 13th time over the past 14 seasons that the Dodgers are NL West champs, including five straight division titles.
Dodgers star infielder Mookie Betts has been part of the last 5 division titles.
Following the Reds game on Thursday, Mookie Betts sent a very heartfelt message to the fans for sticking with him throughout the season.
More MLB on Heavy: BREAKING: Los Angeles Dodgers Clinch NL West Vs. Reds on Thursday Afternoon
Mookie Betts Thanks Fans for Sticking With Him
If you've watched/followed the Los Angeles Dodgers throughout the season, you know some of their All-Star players have endured some lengthy slumps.
Mookie Betts was one of them after he dealt with an oblique injury.
Per Dodgers reporter David Vassegh, here is what Mookie had to say after the game:
"Thank you for sticking with me. I know it was hard. I make it hard sometimes, but thank you for sticking by my side. By our side. We've got something special coming."
That 'something special coming' would be a third straight World Series victory.
More MLB on Heavy: Former Los Angeles Dodgers Pitcher Suddenly Released by New MLB Team
Taking a Look at Mookie Betts' 2026 Season
Mookie Betts has caught fire over the past month and a half, which has really helped with his season-long marks.
He's batting .250 now with 20 home runs, 20 doubles, and an OPS+ of 103.
Mookie has also added 64 runs, 111 hits, and 62 RBI in 114 games played.
As the Dodgers march toward October, they are looking very formidable, and they will hope all their players stay healthy for the next week and a half until the regular season is over.

title: Tarik Skubal Leaves Door Open on Dodgers Future During NL West Celebration
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers future free agent Tarik Skubal, pending his move to the team, joined the celebration of the team’s division win and made an interesting comment about his future.
With champagne pouring and running down his face, Skubal was asked about his outlook on the upcoming postseason push amid the current celebration.
“It’s a ton of fun to celebrate these moments with these guys. It’s gonna be special. It’s gonna be the first of many,” Skubal said.
The statement has multiple layers: if the Dodgers win more postseason series, they’ll have many more celebrations down the road this year.
The Dodgers will pop bottles at each stop, following the NLDS, NLCS, and the World Series.
However, his lingering free-agent status also hangs in the background of his entire Dodgers tenure. LA is getting a shot to show Skubal what the team and organization can do for him.
Over the offseason, likely before the lockout, Skubal has the chance to sign a deal that keeps the champagne flowing with his “best friend” Blake Snell for years to come.
Odds are, Skubal still isn’t thinking too far ahead; he was speaking about this season, but as the Dodgers keep winning, things are moving in their favor in the Skubal sweepstakes.
Also, this hasn’t stopped fan speculation that the comments mean more.
Dodgers fans think Skubal is staying
“I’m holding on to Skubal saying ‘this is the first of many’ which would lead me to believe he’s gonna resign with the Dodgers!!!,” @PokieNFace said on X.
“He dropped a hint I think,” @topherbutler6 wrote.
“Yea he’s not leaving ?,” @ItsGeorgyBruh added.
“Skubal in La next year,” @YoPr0digy also replied in the comments

title: Dodgers take down Reds to capture fifth consecutive NL West crown, 13th in past 14 seasons
author: Andy Backstrom
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers were already playoff-bound for the 14th straight season. But after taking down the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, they're winners of the NL West for the 13th time in that span and for the fifth season in a row.
Of course, the streak LA cares about most will be at stake in the postseason. The Dodgers are aiming to become the first team to three-peat as World Series champions since the fabled New York Yankees of 1998-2000.
With the victory Thursday, the Dodgers (93-60) have the second-best record in the NL, behind only the Milwaukee Brewers (95-58), who clinched the NL Central earlier this week but dropped their series finale to the Pirates on Thursday. The Dodgers and Brewers will jockey for the NL's top seed over the final week of the regular season.
Meanwhile, LA will do its best to sort out an injury-riddled roster before the calendar flips to October. Most notably, the status of Shohei Ohtani will be acutely monitored, as the two-way star has been juggling issues with his biceps, left knee and neck.
Then there's lefty starting pitcher Blake Snell, who's dealing with a groin injury that ended his start Wednesday versus the Reds after just one inning.
Andy Pages is expected back in the Dodgers' outfield soon. However, only time will tell how quickly he returns to form after healing from a fractured left hand.
A bullpen game and a flurry of early scoring sealed the NL West in Cincy
LA didn't need one of its aces to secure the division title on Thursday. Manager Dave Roberts, who has overseen 10 of the Dodgers' NL West crowns amid this memorable run, opted for a bullpen game.
Lefty Justin Wrobleski spun three innings of shutout ball. He was the first to punch out Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who clocked out with three Ks on the day. Cincinnati's lone run came in the fourth, when Sal Stewart homered off Dodgers right-handed hurler Blake Treinen.
Then righty Landon Knack registered four scoreless innings while allowing four hits. Seth Halvorsen finished the game while allowing one more Reds run to score in the ninth.
That merely made a dent in LA's commanding lead. The Dodgers built that in large part thanks to a trio of extra-base hits. Kyle Tucker went yard in the first inning, depositing a two-run dinger. He also hit an RBI double in the second. In the fourth, Max Muncy drove home a pair of runs with a two-bagger.
The Reds and Dodgers traded runs in the ninth, with Miguel Rojas taking one deep to put the exclamation point on LA's division-clinching victory.

The Dodgers and Brewers will jockey for the NL's top seed over the final week of the regular season.
Meanwhile, LA will do its best to sort out an injury-riddled roster before the calendar flips to October. Most notably, the status of Shohei Ohtani will be acutely monitored, as the two-way star has been juggling issues with his biceps, left knee and neck.
Then there's lefty starting pitcher Blake Snell, who's dealing with a groin injury that ended his start Wednesday versus the Reds after just one inning.
Andy Pages is expected back in the Dodgers' outfield soon. However, only time will tell how quickly he returns to form after healing from a fractured left hand.
A bullpen game and a flurry of early scoring sealed the NL West in Cincy
LA didn't need one of its aces to secure the division title on Thursday. Manager Dave Roberts, who has overseen 10 of the Dodgers' NL West crowns amid this memorable run, opted for a bullpen game.
Lefty Justin Wrobleski spun three innings of shutout ball. He was the first to punch out Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who clocked out with three Ks on the day. Cincinnati's lone run came in the fourth, when Sal Stewart homered off Dodgers right-handed hurler Blake Treinen.
Then righty Landon Knack registered four scoreless innings while allowing four hits. Seth Halvorsen finished the game while allowing one more Reds run to score in the ninth.
That merely made a dent in LA's commanding lead. The Dodgers built that in large part thanks to a trio of extra-base hits. Kyle Tucker went yard in the first inning, depositing a two-run dinger. He also hit an RBI double in the second. In the fourth, Max Muncy drove home a pair of runs with a two-bagger.
The Reds and Dodgers traded runs in the ninth, with Miguel Rojas taking one deep to put the exclamation point on LA's division-clinching victory.

title: Es hora de que Shohei Ohtani renuncie al pitcheo de manera definitiva
author: Ryan Phillips
body:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.
Durante años, Ohtani ha maravillado al beisbol con sus enormes home runs, velocidades de salida de otro mundo y actuaciones ofensivas que el juego nunca había visto antes. Su capacidad para lanzar lo hizo único, pero ya no vale la pena correr el riesgo. Su experimento de dos vías fue una de las hazañas más impresionantes en la historia del deporte. Continuarlo no vale la pena si eso significa perder la magia que puede crear con un bat en las manos.
En el plato, Ohtani es un superhéroe. En el montículo, es frágil. Ya no tiene sentido arriesgar al Ohtani bateador por tener la posibilidad de contar con el Ohtani pitcher.
Ohtani podría ser el Ícaro del beisbol. Aquello que lo hizo milagroso podría terminar siendo lo que lo haga volver a tocar tierra.
La diferencia es que Ohtani puede alejarse de su defecto fatal antes de que se convierta en su caída.
Publicado originalmente en www.sportsillustrated.com el 15/09/2026, traducido al español para SI México.

title: Kyle Tucker's recent Dodgers surge is smokescreen fans shouldn't fall for
author: Katrina Stebbins
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West for the 14th time in their last 15 seasons with an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday. Justin Wrobleski pitched three perfect innings, Freddie Freeman continued to heat up, Miguel Rojas hit just his fourth homer of the year, but the Dodgers' top performer, not just in the series finale, but over the Dodgers' last 10 games was Kyle Tucker.
He homered in his first at-bat on Thursday to give the Dodgers an early 2-0 lead. By the end of the game, he'd gone 4-for-5 with the homer, two doubles, three RBI, and ended up a triple shy of the cycle.
After a long season of struggles and fans and writers alike wondering aloud if the Dodgers made a huge mistake signing him to his absurd four-year, $240 million contract, Tucker seems to have turned back into his old self at just the right time.
The Dodgers, while still heavy favorites to win the World Series, have a whole host of weaknesses their upcoming postseason opponents can (and will) identify and exploit. But Tucker earning back his old King Tuck moniker in LA would add an extra bite the lineup expected but hasn't seen most of this season.
However, there's a caveat to all of this that Dodgers fans shouldn't ignore. LA has played seven of their last 10 games against the Reds, one of the worst teams in the National League.
Kyle Tucker's newfound success for the Dodgers has to be tempered by one unavoidable fact
Before coming into this nine-game stretch, Tucker hit .143 with a .628 OPS against the Detroit Tigers, St. Louis Cardinals, and Washington Nationals. All are inferior opponents to the Dodgers and some even had worse records than the Reds by the time they saw the Dodgers. But none had the NL or AL's second-worst run differential like Cincinnati.
Going into this series, Cincinnati had a staggering -148 run differential. Their pitching staff's collective ERA is 4.87 and WHIP is 1.45, the third-worst in baseball in both categories. Of the four starters the Dodgers faced during this series, only Andrew Abbott had an ERA under 5.00 (4.78).
The Dodgers' last nine games should be a greater test of Tucker's mettle, and will prove whether or not this hot streak was purely incidental. Six inter-division games against the San Francisco Giants and three against the San Diego Padres are surely going to give the Dodgers more grief, as games against those teams often do, and may expose this recent surge as being nothing more than a flash in the pan.

title: When is Shohei Ohtani coming back? Dodgers reveal injury update
author: Gabe Lacques; USA TODAY
body:
Andrew Friedman, the Los Angeles Dodgers' president of baseball operations, told reporters in Cincinnati that he expects Shohei Ohtani will return during the club's final nine games of the regular season.
Speaking after the champagne celebration that followed the club's 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds that clinched the National League West, Friedman said of Ohtani, "I expect him back in the regular season."
The four-time MVP and two-way superstar will not pitch this season due to right biceps and left knee injuries, and he has not been in the Dodgers lineup since Sept. 7, after which he was placed on the 15-day injured list. Ohtani sat out five games before giving that one a go, and he had just six hits in 49 at-bats (.122) with no home runs in his final 61 plate appearances.
Much of that span was spent trying to also return as a pitcher, before a bullpen session on Aug. 28 was cut short. The club is hoping his focus on playing one side of the ball enables his body not only to heal, but hold up as the Dodgers aim for a third consecutive World Series title.
For the season, Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs and a .902 OPS, and will likely cede his two-year reign as NL MVP to the Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: When is Shohei Ohtani coming back? Dodgers reveal injury update
