title: Dave Roberts: First-round bye would be more ‘beneficial’ than ever for injury-riddled Dodgers
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
CINCINNATI — A few days off sounds pretty good right about now.
“I do think this team, as much as any team we’ve had, that week off is probably most beneficial,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of locking down one of the top two seeds in the National League in order to get a first-round bye and five days off before starting the postseason.
Going into Thursday’s game, the Dodgers held a 3 ½-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the second seed in the NL with a magic number of seven to clinch that first-round bye. The Dodgers trail the Milwaukee Brewers by three games for the top seed.
“It’s always helpful in the sense of giving your guys a break to reset,” Roberts said. “But given all the tax and where our guys are health-wise, to get that week would be huge.”
Blake Snell joined the long list of players with injury concerns when he left his start Wednesday after just one inning due to left groin tightness. The Dodgers also have questions about Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps), Freddie Freeman (knee), Edgardo Henriquez (back), Andy Pages (hand), Roki Sasaki (blister) and Dalton Rushing (elbow).
Pages has been swinging a bat and hitting off the Trajekt machine this week, and it is “very likely” he will be activated from the IL during the homestand starting Friday, according to Roberts.
Ohtani has been “progressing” this week and is feeling “normal-ish” with no pain in his right arm or left knee, Roberts said.
“He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when (his) time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Snell could undergo an MRI to determine the severity of his groin injury. But he was optimistic after the game Wednesday that he had pulled back and left the game soon enough that it won’t be a serious issue and he might be able to make one more start before the end of the regular season.
“It’s all contingent on how he feels and potential imaging,” Roberts said. “It doesn’t make sense to just shut him down until the postseason if he can pitch. But again, if he’s not 100 percent to pitch, then we have no problem kicking the can.”
DIAZ RETURN
Right-hander Edwin Diaz completed his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday and will join the Dodgers in Los Angeles this weekend with the expectation that he will be activated from the Injured List.
Diaz will be used in “low-leverage” situations, Roberts said, with a need to prove he can pitch well enough to assume a bigger role if he is on the postseason roster.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Roberts called Diaz’s final outing with OKC was “his best one yet.” Diaz pitched a scoreless inning, gave up a double and didn’t get a single swing-and-miss on any of 15 pitches.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said of what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Cesar Perdomo, 0-1, 3.68 ERA) at Dodgers (RHP Tyler Glasnow, 4-1, 3.50 ERA), Friday, 7:10 p.m., Apple TV, 570 AM

title: Edwin “Sugar” Díaz será activado el viernes por los Dodgers
author: Por Redacción El Nuevo Día
body:
Edwin Díaz se unirá este viernes a los Dodgers en el inicio de una serie ante los Giants de San Francisco. (Nick Wass)
Por Redacción El Nuevo Día
El relevista puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz retornará con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles cuando la novena lo active de la lista de lesionados este viernes, confirmó el dirigente Dave Roberts.
El regreso de Díaz se producirá después de completar el miércoles una entrada sin permitir carreras en su quinta aparición de rehabilitación en Triple A con la novena de Oklahoma City.
“La idea es que esté activo el viernes”, expresó Roberts este jueves, según SportsNet LA.
El naguabeño trabajó la novena entrada y necesitó 15 lanzamientos, 11 de ellos para strikes. Permitió un doble con dos outs, pero evitó que el corredor anotara para completar el episodio en blanco.
Roberts calificó la actuación como la mejor de Díaz durante su asignación de rehabilitación.
Dodgers injury updates, per manager Roberts (via @ByJackHarris):
• Edwin Diaz (neck) will be activated from IL on Friday • Andy Pages (hand) "very likely" to be activated during final homestand • Shohei Ohtani (biceps) could still return before end of regular season
La salida resultaba particularmente importante para el boricua después de su difícil presentación del domingo, cuando permitió cinco carreras limpias, concedió tres bases por bolas y apenas consiguió dos outs.
De hecho, Roberts había reconocido el lunes que Díaz necesitaba lanzar mejor y que su presencia en el roster de los Dodgers para la postemporada no estaba garantizada.
El regreso tampoco significa que Díaz retomará inmediatamente las funciones de cerrador.
Roberts había adelantado que utilizará inicialmente al derecho de 32 años en situaciones de poca presión mientras intenta recuperar la confianza del cuerpo técnico.
Los Dodgers ya aseguraron su pase a los playoffs y marchan primeros en la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. El viernes inician una serie de tres juegos ante San Francisco.
Díaz está en la lista de lesionados desde el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Es su segunda ausencia prolongada de la temporada luego de que en abril fuera sometido a una operación para remover cuerpos sueltos de su codo derecho.
Díaz tiene marca de 2-2 y efectividad de 11.85 en 16 apariciones, con 18 carreras limpias permitidas en 13.2 entradas. Además, ha desperdiciado cuatro de sus 11 oportunidades de salvamento.

“La idea es que esté activo el viernes”, expresó Roberts este jueves, según SportsNet LA.
El naguabeño trabajó la novena entrada y necesitó 15 lanzamientos, 11 de ellos para strikes. Permitió un doble con dos outs, pero evitó que el corredor anotara para completar el episodio en blanco.
Roberts calificó la actuación como la mejor de Díaz durante su asignación de rehabilitación.
Dodgers injury updates, per manager Roberts (via @ByJackHarris):
• Edwin Diaz (neck) will be activated from IL on Friday • Andy Pages (hand) "very likely" to be activated during final homestand • Shohei Ohtani (biceps) could still return before end of regular season
La salida resultaba particularmente importante para el boricua después de su difícil presentación del domingo, cuando permitió cinco carreras limpias, concedió tres bases por bolas y apenas consiguió dos outs.
De hecho, Roberts había reconocido el lunes que Díaz necesitaba lanzar mejor y que su presencia en el roster de los Dodgers para la postemporada no estaba garantizada.
El regreso tampoco significa que Díaz retomará inmediatamente las funciones de cerrador.
Roberts había adelantado que utilizará inicialmente al derecho de 32 años en situaciones de poca presión mientras intenta recuperar la confianza del cuerpo técnico.
Los Dodgers ya aseguraron su pase a los playoffs y marchan primeros en la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. El viernes inician una serie de tres juegos ante San Francisco.
Díaz está en la lista de lesionados desde el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Es su segunda ausencia prolongada de la temporada luego de que en abril fuera sometido a una operación para remover cuerpos sueltos de su codo derecho.
Díaz tiene marca de 2-2 y efectividad de 11.85 en 16 apariciones, con 18 carreras limpias permitidas en 13.2 entradas. Además, ha desperdiciado cuatro de sus 11 oportunidades de salvamento.

title: Dodgers 2026 injured list tracker

body:

Basically any time a player misses time that requires a roster move, we’ll note it here.
During the 2025 season, 28 different Dodgers players spent time on the injured list, some of them for multiple stints. That matched the team total from 2024, while in 2023 the Dodgers saw 34 players miss time on the IL.

title: Dodgers' Edwin Diaz to return for series opener against Giants
author: Sportsnet Staff
body:
The closer will be active for Game 1 of the Dodgers' series against the San Francisco Giants, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday.
Roberts added that Diaz will pitch in low-leverage situations.
The 32-year-old right-hander signed a three-year, $60-million contract in the off-season to become the Dodgers' closer, but has struggled with injuries and underperformance.
Diaz underwent an arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right eblow in April and most recently missed time due to neck inflammation. He has an 11.85 ERA with 19 strikeouts and 10 walks over 13.2 innings.
Roberts also said that the Dodgers plan to activate outfielder Andy Pages on their upcoming homestand, and that Shohei Ohtani could still return this season.
The two-time reigning National League MVP tried to return from a nagging bicep injury on Sept. 7 but was placed on the 15-day injured list afterward. He will not pitch again this season.

title: Shohei Ohtani’s feeling ‘normal…ish’ as Dodgers sort out health issues before playoffs
author: Fabian Ardaya
body:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers have kept open the possibility that Shohei Ohtani will return before the end of the regular season, though they are up against a running clock.
Any progress is good progress for the Dodgers’ most important piece, so it was a good thing when Ohtani started up activity Tuesday and Thursday and didn’t report any discomfort in his bothersome biceps, balky left knee and tight neck.
“Feels normal…ish,” manager Dave Roberts said Thursday morning.
Advertisement
Ohtani went on the injured list late last week, ending a months-long injury saga and giving him a maximum of five additional regular season games to play in before another the playoffs. He is eligible to return as soon as Sept. 23, though Roberts did not commit to that timeline.
There are still steps for Ohtani to take. He swung off a tee on Tuesday, had Wednesday off from baseball activity and could hit off a coach’s pitching by the end of the week. He will need to face some sort of live pitching before he appears in a game and even then, the maximum of five games does not feel like a lot for him to get his timing right.
Especially since, given how the Dodgers tried kicking the can on shelving Ohtani, he will return after having taken just four plate appearances since Sept. 2. Ohtani, clearly compromised by his nagging injuries, had just six hits over his final 49 at-bats before hitting the IL.
They still need Ohtani, even if he is not 100 percent. The oldest lineup in baseball has shown its age. Even if Ohtani’s role on the postseason roster is simply to provide the threat of launching a ball into the seats, that is valuable in their quest for a third consecutive World Series title. The Dodgers’ first road trip without Ohtani since his arrival in 2024 has been noticeably different.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yoshinobu Yamamoto joked through interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. Yamamoto has instead had to rely on Roki Sasaki, “but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Díaz’ place in the bullpen
Edwin Díaz will return to the Dodgers on Friday, but not as the club’s closer. Nothing is guaranteed for the guy the Dodgers gave $69 million to solve their ninth-inning problem and who now could be on the bubble for the postseason roster thanks to his 11.85 ERA.
Díaz, who has made only 16 major-league appearances thanks to arthroscopic elbow surgery and a later neck issue, has also pitched poorly in rehab. A five-run blowup on Sunday with Triple-A Oklahoma City caused the Dodgers to delay Díaz’s return. But a scoreless inning on Wednesday — albeit one in which Díaz gave up a 104 mph double and did not induce a single swing-and-miss — was enough for the Dodgers to bring him back to the big leagues.
“It was his best one yet,” Roberts said of Díaz, whose has a low bar to clear.
Advertisement
Díaz will return in lower-leverage situations and have to show prove over the final week of the regular season he deserves a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen, even if their list of right-handed relief options is thinning.
“I think like anything it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities but then you also got to perform, right?”
Edgardo Henriquez was the club’s most trusted reliever before he went on the injured list on Monday. Subsequent imaging showed what Roberts dubbed a “low-grade” back strain, and the manager said he was “hopeful” that Henriquez could still be a postseason option.
Another potential solution, Sasaki, is now needed in the rotation after Blake Snell exited Wednesday’s start with left groin tightness. The Dodgers will know more about Snell’s fate once they return to Los Angeles and potentially get imaging done, but Sasaki is currently slated to pitch at some point next week against the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers have also been cagey about Tyler Glasnow’s status. Roberts was vague after Glasnow’s last start, but said the right-hander “didn’t feel great” going into it. The Dodgers sent Glasnow directly to Los Angeles afterwards rather than have him travel with the club to Cincinnati, and Roberts said Glasnow’s preparation for Friday’s start has otherwise been normal.
Pages’ return imminent
Andy Pages will “very likely” return to the Dodgers’ lineup without playing in rehab games at some point during the six-game home stand that opens Friday. Pages has progressed quickly from left hand fracture and the Dodgers are banking on the All-Star’s defensive value in center field despite the chances he’ll struggle on offensive.
Pages moved from hitting softer baseballs to hitting normal ones this week and will hit off the Trajekt Arc machine to simulate live at-bats. There aren’t a lot of games to go around on a rehab assignment, anyway, though Oklahoma City did clinch a postseason berth on Wednesday (those games start next week).

rss_title: Shohei Ohtani’s feeling ‘normal…ish’ as Dodgers sort out health issues before playoffs
rss_body:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers have kept open the possibility that Shohei Ohtani will return before the end of the regular season, though they are up against a running clock.
Any progress is good progress for the Dodgers’ most important piece, so it was a good thing when Ohtani started up activity Tuesday and Thursday and didn’t report any discomfort in his bothersome biceps, balky left knee and tight neck.
“Feels normal…ish,” manager Dave Roberts said Thursday morning.
Advertisement
Ohtani went on the injured list late last week, ending a months-long injury saga and giving him a maximum of five additional regular season games to play in before another the playoffs. He is eligible to return as soon as Sept. 23, though Roberts did not commit to that timeline.
There are still steps for Ohtani to take. He swung off a tee on Tuesday, had Wednesday off from baseball activity and could hit off a coach’s pitching by the end of the week. He will need to face some sort of live pitching before he appears in a game and even then, the maximum of five games does not feel like a lot for him to get his timing right.
Especially since, given how the Dodgers tried kicking the can on shelving Ohtani, he will return after having taken just four plate appearances since Sept. 2. Ohtani, clearly compromised by his nagging injuries, had just six hits over his final 49 at-bats before hitting the IL.
They still need Ohtani, even if he is not 100 percent. The oldest lineup in baseball has shown its age. Even if Ohtani’s role on the postseason roster is simply to provide the threat of launching a ball into the seats, that is valuable in their quest for a third consecutive World Series title. The Dodgers’ first road trip without Ohtani since his arrival in 2024 has been noticeably different.

title: Dodgers latest injury crisis throws Roki Sasaki usage plan in flux
author: Jack Harris
body:
CINCINNATI –– Even after watching Roki Sasaki complete the final checkmark in his recovery from a blister on Wednesday afternoon, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts couldn’t say for sure how the team would use the 24-year-old phenom pitcher.
All year, it seemed clear that Sasaki was destined to wind up back in the Dodgers bullpen, reprising the late-inning leverage role he unexpectedly ascended to as a rookie last October.
Though he had turned a corner as a starter during the second half of this campaign, posting a 2.31 ERA in his first six outings after the All-Star break, he had still long looked like a superfluous piece of the Dodgers’ rotation, an excess arm stuck behind the four veteran superstars the club had penciled in to lead this fall’s World Series push.
However, Roberts remained non-committal about Sasaki’s plan on Wednesday, after the right-hander completed a four-inning, 48-pitch session of live batting practice in Cincinnati, in what was hoped to be his final step before returning from the injured list.
On the one hand, the skipper noted, the Dodgers could shift Sasaki to the bullpen now, give him time to re-acclimate to relief duties, and let him focus on just short-burst stints.
But on the other, “one can argue it’s best to [let him] take down a couple starts and keep him built up,” Roberts countered. “Because if something does happen, then he is built up.”
Hours later, the something Roberts was worried about might have suddenly happened –– with Blake Snell’s groin injury having direct repercussions on Sasaki’s potential task.
In Wednesday night’s game, Snell left his start after just one inning because of left groin tightness. While he’s hopeful he avoided any serious injury, he has had bouts of groin issues in the past that have sidelined him for up to a month at a time.
If that were to be the case again now, Sasaki would be first in line to replace Snell in the Dodgers’ postseason rotation.
Mix in the uncertainty surrounding fellow starter Tyler Glasnow faced following his four-inning outing last weekend in Miami –– after which he conspicuously returned immediately to Los Angeles to limit extra travel on the rest of this road trip –– and Sasaki now seems like a valuable starting-pitching insurance policy the Dodgers might still need to utilize in the playoffs.
That’s why, by the end of Wednesday’s game, Roberts was able to at least be definitive about the team’s plan for Sasaki when he comes off the injured list, confirming he is likely to make a start sometime next week, perhaps during a visit from the San Diego Padres.
In a best-case scenario, that will be Sasaki’s last time starting a game this year, with an otherwise healthy rotation allowing the Dodgers to shift him to an equally banged-up bullpen.
But for now, the team can’t be certain of anything.
Which means, when it comes to Sasaki, all options remain on the table.

title: This day in Dodgers history: Hideo Nomo, Sandy Koufax and more
author: Blake Williams
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have a long line of notable pitchers and on this day in franchise history, those stars shined a little brighter throughout the years.
On Sept. 17, 1963, Sandy Koufax pitched a shutout against the St. Louis Cardinals at Sportsman’s Park while giving up just four hits.
The shutout was his 11th of the season, which set a new National League record for the most in one year by a left-hander in MLB history. Grover Cleveland Alexander held the Major League Record with 16 shutouts during the 1916 season for the Philadelphia Phillies.
Also on this day in Dodgers history but during the 1981 season, Fernando Valenzuela threw his eighth shutout of the year with a three-hitter against the Atlanta Braves.
With eight shutouts, Valenzuela tied the rookie record that was set by Chicago White Sox pitcher Ewell Russell in 1913. In addition, Valenzuela broke the previous NL mark shared by Irving Young (Boston Beaneaters, 1905), Grover Cleveland Alexander (Phillies, 1911), and Jerry Koosman (New York Mets, 1968).
Dodgers history: Sept. 17
Nomo no-hitter
In 1996, 15 years after Valenzuela and 33 years after Koufax set their shutout records, Hideo Nomo threw the only no-hitter in history at Coors Field. It was one of two Nomo tossed during his 12-year career.
Nomo’s historic game came with the club locked in a pennant race and it was the 20th no-hitter in franchise history.
Joe Torre retires
Also on this day in Dodgers history, manager Joe Torre announced he will retire following the end of the 2010 season. He finished his career with a record of 2326-1997 (.538) during his 30 seasons as a skipper with Mets, Braves, Cardinals, New York Yankees, and the Dodgers.
The Dodgers then announced the team’s hitting coach Don Mattingly was hired to replace Torre, who accepted a position to assist Major League Baseball Commissioner Bud Selig as the new Executive Vice President for Baseball Operations.

title: Dodgers To Make Edwin Diaz Earn High Leverage Appearances Again
author: Aaliyan Mohammed
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are expected to activate Edwin Díaz from the injured list on Friday, but he will not slot back into closing games right away.
According to the Orange County Register's Bill Plunkett, Dave Roberts said the plan is to activate Díaz for the San Francisco Giants series, but to have him pitch in "low leverage" situations for the time being. Roberts also called the bullpen a "meritocracy" and said that Díaz needs to prove himself.
Díaz was the National League Reliever of the Year last year and has won three career Reliever of the Year Awards. The Dodgers gave him a three-year, $69 million deal in the offseason, but he has had a terrible season.
Through his first six games, he had a 10.50 ERA and blew a save. He then underwent a procedure to remove loose bodies from his elbow. After returning, he posted a 12.91 ERA in nine games, blowing three saves. The Dodgers placed him on the injured list with neck inflammation on Aug. 18 and are hoping for the best version of him this time.
Díaz has noted that he thinks fixing his arm angle will help him, but it's a results-based business. He will have to prove he can pitch like the Dodgers expected him to be, and the Dodgers need him more now than ever.
Since the All-Star Break, the Dodgers bullpen has a 4.34 ERA, ranked 20th in baseball. The bullpen also has a 10.4% walk rate, the seventh-worst in baseball. Dodgers relievers have also given up 24 home runs in the second half. If Díaz can come back and pitch like an All-Star, it will go a long way in fixing the bullpen woes. The team is currently without Edgardo Henriquez, so they need a reliable right-hander in the bullpen.
Roberts also confirmed that outfielder Andy Pages (hand) is expected to rejoin LA during upcoming homestand without requiring a minor-league rehab assignment.
More MLB: Los Angeles Dodgers Reveal When Andy Pages Will Make Return

Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said it's "very likely" that outfielder Andy Pages (hand) will be activated during the team's upcoming homestand, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Los Angeles begins a six-game homestand on Friday. Pages has been sidelined since August 21 by a fractured left hand, but it appears he is now on the doorstep of a return to the big leagues. Across 550 plate appearances before the injury, the 25-year-old hit .272/.338/.458 with 21 home runs, 80 RBI, 72 runs scored, and 12 stolen bases. Pages was the Dodgers' everyday center fielder before getting hurt and should resume that role upon his return. Once activated, Pages profiles as a must-start outfielder for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris

rss_title: Andy Pages "Very Likely" to Be Activated During Upcoming Dodgers Homestand - MLB News | Fantasy Baseball
rss_body:
Sep 17, 2026, 11:27 AM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said it's "very likely" that outfielder Andy Pages (hand) will be activated during the team's upcoming homestand, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Los Angeles begins a six-game homestand on Friday. Pages has been sidelined since August 21 by a fractured left hand, but it appears he is now on the doorstep of a return to the big leagues. Across 550 plate appearances before the injury, the 25-year-old hit .272/.338/.458 with 21 home runs, 80 RBI, 72 runs scored, and 12 stolen bases. Pages was the Dodgers' everyday center fielder before getting hurt and should resume that role upon his return. Once activated, Pages profiles as a must-start outfielder for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris
More Recent News
Sep 17, 2026, 11:34 AM ET
Across 470 plate appearances in 2026, Chicago White Sox outfielder Tristan Peters is hitting .273/.343/.452 with 12 home runs, 54 RBI, 61 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. The lefty-swinger is hitting .192 across just 63 plate appearances against left-handed pitching, so his big-side platoon role limits his fantasy value to some degree. However, Peters owns an .824 OPS against right-handers and brings a balanced profile at the plate that allows him to provide modest production across all five fantasy categories. After hitting six home runs across 87 plate appearances in August, the 26-year-old has gone without a homer in his first 56 trips to the plate in September. Still, Peters hits for average and should continue to provide steady run production in stretches where the White Sox face a string of right-handed starting pitchers. Heading into the final week-plus of the regular season, Peters could be worth targeting as an outfield streamer off the waiver wire.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller

                                Will Brady
                                                            
                            
                        
                    
                    Sep 17, 2026, 11:19 AM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said that right-hander Edwin Diaz (neck) will be activated from the 15-day injured list on Friday, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Diaz has struggled on his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he's made five appearances. However, the 32-year-old pitched a scoreless inning on Wednesday and is now on his way back to the big leagues. It's been a lost season for Diaz, who has missed extensive time due to elbow and neck issues. He's also been awful when healthy, pitching to an 11.85 ERA with a 2.56 WHIP across 13 2/3 innings in his first season with the Dodgers. It's unclear whether he'll assume the Dodgers' closer role immediately upon his return, or if he will need to prove that he's regained his form first. Dodgers left-hander Tanner Scott has largely been effective in Diaz's absence, logging a 2.87 ERA and 22 saves across 59 2/3 innings.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris
Sep 17, 2026, 11:12 AM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter/starting pitcher Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) is making progress and has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, per Jack Harris of the California Post. Ohtani is currently on the 15-day injured list as he battles lingering knee and biceps issues. The Dodgers have already announced that Ohtani will not pitch again this season, but the 32-year-old is expected to resume his role as the team's everyday designated hitter. Across 596 plate appearances in 2026, Ohtani is hitting .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 89 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases. His production had begun to trail off before he was placed on the IL, with just one hit in 14 plate appearances in September. Still, Ohtani has the potential to swing fantasy leagues if he can return for the final weekend of the regular season.--Will Brady
Source: California Post - Jack Harris

Gore was given a no-decision at Globe Life Field, allowing three earned runs on two hits (one homer) while walking three and striking out none in four innings of work. The 27-year-old southpaw is now up in the air for his next scheduled start, which is tentatively for next Tuesday against the New York Mets. Gore has been up and down in 2026 in his first year with the Rangers, going into Wednesday's start with an 8-11 record, career-high 4.62 ERA (3.77 FIP), and 1.35 WHIP with 172 strikeouts and 66 walks in 161 2/3 innings across his 31 starts. He has not pitched into the sixth inning since his first start of the month on Sept. 1, and he has allowed at least three earned runs in each of his last three starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Dallas Morning News - Shawn McFarland
Sep 16, 2026, 11:10 PM ET
Updating a previous report, Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell (groin) said he felt his left groin "grab" during his pre-game bullpen, and he decided not to push it after the first inning on Wednesday in the 6-2 loss to the hosting Cincinnati Reds, according to Jack Harris of The California Post. Snell added that he will take things day to day, but he feels like he "should be good" to make another start before the end of the regular season. The Dodgers pulled the veteran southpaw after he threw a scoreless first inning with one hit allowed and a strikeout, but it sounds like he avoided a serious injury. The 33-year-old has a history of groin trouble, so although he might not think it is serious, the Dodgers could decide to play it safe and hold him out until the postseason in October. The 33-year-old two-time Cy Young winner has not been a picture of health in recent years and has only made 19 starts in the regular season for the Blue since joining them before the start of the 2025 season. Snell entered Wednesday's start with a nice 1.91 ERA, though, and he has also posted a 1.09 WHIP with 51 strikeouts and 16 walks in 37 2/3 innings across seven starts.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The California Post - Jack Harris

Still, Gallegos reports that A's manager Mark Kotsay said the team is hoping Kurtz can progress to taking batting practice at some point in the next couple of weeks. Across 434 plate appearances before suffering the injury, the 23-year-old hit .256/.396/.483 with 21 home runs, 69 RBI, 62 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. Kurtz's batting average upside is limited by his elevated 32.5% strikeout rate, but he remains an OBP asset with his elite 18.2% walk rate. The lefty slugger also profiles as one of the best power hitters in baseball when healthy, posting an 18% barrel rate and a 57.3% hard-hit rate in 2026. Assuming Kurtz makes a full recovery over the offseason, he should come off the board in the first few rounds of fantasy drafts heading into 2027.--Will Brady
Source: MLB.com - Martín Gallegos
Sep 16, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Atlanta Braves starting pitcher Chris Sale's next scheduled start is being pushed back, per Jesus Cano of The Athletic. Cano reports that the veteran left-hander is "not dealing with anything" and that there is "no need to panic." Still, it appears that Sale's next scheduled start will now be next Wednesday against the Cincinnati Reds instead of this upcoming weekend against the Houston Astros. Sale has been one of the best pitchers in baseball in 2026, recording a 14-9 record with a 2.18 ERA, 0.99 WHIP, and 190 strikeouts across 157 innings (26 starts). He was effective in his most recent outing on September 11, allowing three earned runs while recording six strikeouts across seven innings pitched against the Philadelphia Phillies. Still, with the Braves locked into a playoff berth, it looks like the team is prioritizing having Sale as fresh as possible in October.--Will Brady
Source: The Athletic - Jesus Cano
Sep 16, 2026, 10:36 PM ET
St. Louis Cardinals outfielder Joshua Baez (side) is considered day-to-day after exiting early from his team's loss to the San Francisco Giants on Wednesday with side tightness, per Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. Baez was hitless in four at-bats before leaving the game. Across 108 plate appearances since making his MLB debut in mid-August, the 23-year-old is hitting .230/.278/.510 with seven home runs, 18 RBI, 18 runs scored, and two stolen bases. Baez hit 34 home runs across 410 plate appearances at Triple-A this season and has posted impressive barrel (12.5%) and hard-hit (48.4%) rates in the big leagues. However, he's also struck out in 30.6% of his plate appearances while logging just a 3.7% walk rate. If Baez ends up missing time, Cardinals outfielder Bryan Torres could be in line for an increase in at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Derrick Goold
Sep 16, 2026, 10:28 PM ET
Baltimore Orioles infielder Jackson Holliday (wrist) has been placed on the 10-day injured list due to left wrist inflammation. Infielder Jose Barrero was recalled from Triple-A Norfolk to take Holliday's place on the team's active roster. While Holliday could technically return to the Orioles before the end of the regular season, his 2026 campaign may be over. Across 354 plate appearances this year, the 22-year-old hit .229/.300/.340 with seven home runs, 30 RBI, 45 runs scored, and eight stolen bases. Holliday's season got off to a rough start, as he suffered a broken hamate bone in Spring Training that delayed his 2026 debut until mid-May. The young infielder has struck out in 23.7% of his plate appearances while also posting the worst hard-hit rate of his career (33.1%). With Holliday sidelined, Orioles infielder/outfielder Jeremiah Jackson will likely see an increase in playing time at second base.--Will Brady
Source: Baltimore Orioles
Sep 16, 2026, 10:17 PM ET

The 30-year-old's production faded in the second half, as he posted a 16.7% strikeout rate and a 5.29 ERA across 47 2/3 innings after the All-Star break. If Bradish has been pitching through discomfort over the last few months, it could explain the downturn in his numbers. Assuming he's ready to go for the start of the 2027 season, Bradish could be an under-the-radar bounce-back candidate for fantasy managers.--Will Brady

title: Who Will Be the Dodgers Game 1 Starter in the Playoffs? | Just Baseball
author: Cade Lalim
body:
Earlier this week after Monday’s 4-1 road victory against the Cincinnati Reds, the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched a playoff berth for the fourteenth consecutive season, an all-time record that ties them with the Atlanta Braves who accomplished it from 1991 to 2005.
A large part of the Dodgers’s success this season has been how good their starting rotation has been. The team has an enormous amount of pitching depth which means they are constantly sending elite starting pitchers to the bump day-in-and-out.
| ERA | WHIP | BB/9 | K/9 | 
| 3.45 (2nd) | 1.09 (2nd) | 2.57 (3rd) | 9.19 (4th) | 
When I said that the Dodgers have an enormous amount of starting pitching depth, I really did mean a ton of depth.
Their active starting rotation currently consists of Tyler Glasnow, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but they also have Justin Wrobleski down in the bullpen who put up an excellent first-half in the starting rotation.
You’d think that’s a pretty good rotation by itself and it certainly is, but they have plenty more quality arms remain either in the minors or on the injured list. These names include: Kris Bubic, Landon Knack, Eric Lauer, Roki Sasaki, Emmet Shehaan, Gavin Stone and of course, Shohei Ohtani.
That right there is enough talent to construct two top-10 starting rotations in the majors, which is incredible. The Dodgers’ plethora of depth is great, but it brings us to an interesting discussion.
The Dodgers coaching staff will have a large selection of elite arms to choose from to open up Postseason action, but who is the most logical and realistic starting pitcher for Game 1?
All stats updated prior to games on Thursday, September 17
Blake Snell, LHP
Snell has pitched really well since returning to the starting rotation in early August. Injuries have kept him out most of the season, as his last start prior to his activation in August came back on May 9 — his season was delayed due to left shoulder fatigue. He left his start on Wednesday after just 19 pitches thanks to a groin injury, so his status is currently up in the air.
Snell has made eight total starts this season, six of those coming after he got activated off the injured list again in August. His injuries don’t seem to be lingering as he’s proven to still be one of the best pitchers in the majors.
Across 38.2 innings pitched, Snell owns a 1.86 ERA and 1.09 WHIP while his underlying metrics prove that he’s still the elite pitcher we’ve been used to. His expected numbers look great, supported by an excellent 2.16 xERA and 2.94 xFIP proving that he is more than ready for playoff action.
Snell, a veteran of 11 seasons, has plenty of postseason innings under his belt and has proved at times to be really good when it matters the most.
When I say at times, it is because last season across 13 postseason innings, he struggled with a 6.92 ERA and 1.77 WHIP. On the other hand, he’s accumulated 82.2 total playoff innings in his career, pitching to a respectable 3.27 ERA and 1.15 WHIP between the three teams he’s suited up for.
Keep in mind that Dave Roberts elected to start Snell in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card last year against the Cincinnati Reds, tossing seven quality innings allowing just two runs while striking out seven. Maybe they will go the same direction this year.
Tarik Skubal, LHP
This year’s mid-summer trade deadline was headlined by the fact that Detroit Tigers sensation Tarik Skubal would probably be on the move when it was all said and done. Well, it happened and Skubal found himself as the blockbuster of the deadline, being traded to the Dodgers.
Being named the American League Cy Young in back-to-back seasons with the Tigers in both 2024 and 2025, the Dodgers got one of the best starting pitchers in the majors.
The Dodgers likely would’ve been completely fine without him, but when a team has trade assets like the Dodgers do, it was a no-brainer for them to get a deal done.
Skubal was a solid pitcher from 2020 to 2023, but the last three seasons for him, including this year, have been absolutely phenomenal. Presently in 2026, splitting time between the Tigers and Dodgers, Skubal has logged 146.2 innings spanning 24 starts, while pitching to a 2.70 ERA and 0.95 WHIP.
If the Dodgers decide they want their ace to start Game 1, it’s going to be Skubal. He’s proved way more than he needs to show that he can be a reliable option in the Postseason. On top of his regular season success, Skubal has looked almost better in October.
He totaled 39.2 innings between the 2024 and 2025 postseasons with the Tigers and looked utterly dominant, hence his 2.04 ERA and 0.73 WHIP. Skubal’s 2025 epic performance alone is incredible.
Last year in his American League Wild Card start against the Cleveland Guardians, Skubal tossed 7.2 innings, only allowing one earned run off of three hits, along with a whopping 14 strikeouts.
Subsequently in the Tigers American League Divisional Series against the Seattle Mariners, he made two starts, totaling 13 innings where he allowed only three earned runs, seven total hits, while striking out 22 and issuing just one walk — ace quality numbers for sure.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, RHP
Finally, we have Yamamoto, who might not be getting enough praise that he deserves. He’s in the middle of his third season with the Dodgers and has quietly asserted himself as one of the better starting pitchers in baseball.
The now two-time All-Star finished third in National League Cy Young voting in 2025, and has been incredible thus far in his young career. He’s posted a career ERA of 2.60 so far to go along with a 0.87 WHIP.
This year has been Yamamoto’s best season, and he’s been building off of his 2025 success. Over 27 starts totalling a season-high 179 innings pitched, he’s posted a 2.51 ERA and career-best 0.87 WHIP.
Yamamoto is no stranger to pitching when the lights are the brightest, as he played a massive role contributing to the Dodgers’ World Series title in 2025 against the Toronto Blue Jays. He logged 56 innings of postseason work between 2024 and 2025, resulting in a 2.25 ERA and 0.84 WHIP.
His World Series performance last year was one to remember, tossing 17.2 innings between two starts and a relief appearance with a 1.02 ERA and 0.68 WHIP. In Game 7, he pitched out of relief and closed out the game and series when he got Alejandro Kirk to ground into a double-play.
He’s been an absolute work-horse and should play a huge role this year for the Dodgers in the Postseason, no-matter what role he is given.
The Verdict…
Now onto the final verdict in pinning one of the arms mentioned above to start Game 1 in the playoffs for the Dodgers — a decision that Dave Roberts and his coaching staff won’t take lightly.
The best way to build the Dodgers starting rotation is to alter the handedness each game, so that it’s tougher on whoever their opponent may be. That means with Snell and Skubal both being left-handers and Yamamoto being a right-hander, Yamamoto is best suited to lineup as the Game 2 starter.
As I mentioned previously, the Dodgers did elect to start Snell in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series last year, but I do think there will be a change of guard this year.
The Dodgers didn’t go and acquire Skubal to be their Game 3 starter; they acquired him to be their bonafide ace and lead them to another World Series title. It only fits best that he takes the ball for Game 1, meaning Snell would line up best for Game 3.
Skubal, being a two-time Cy Young award winner, two-time All-Star, Triple Crown winner and two-time ERA title winner, indicates that he is more than ready and able to be the Dodgers rotation anchor and leader when October baseball rolls around in a few weeks.

title: Treinen Says Dodgers Ignore Magic Number With Division Title in Reach
author: Eduardo Solano
body:
As a missed clinching opportunity keeps the National League West race alive, veteran reliever Blake Treinen reveals why the Los Angeles Dodgers prioritize internal refinement over tracking daily postseason math.
The Los Angeles Dodgers entered Wednesday night’s game against the Cincinnati Reds with a magic number of one. A victory or a San Diego Padres loss would have secured another National League West title.
Neither result occurred. Blake Snell lasted only one inning before leaving his start because of left groin tightness, and the Dodgers suffered a 6-2 loss. The Padres also defeated the Colorado Rockies 9-3, preventing Los Angeles from clinching the division.
Blake Treinen replaced Snell in the second inning and delivered a scoreless appearance. He surrendered two hits with a strikeout in one inning.
Treinen is 4-1 with a 3.33 ERA and 1.37 WHIP in 27 innings over 33 appearances this season. He has also recorded one save and six holds.
The magic number doesn’t matter
After the loss, Treinen provided some perspective on how closely Dodgers players follow magic numbers and the different milestones associated with winning a division title.
The veteran reliever told SportsNet LA that he had no idea what the Dodgers’ magic number was until a reporter mentioned it. He explained that the team is concentrating on becoming the best possible version of itself rather than following the changing number.
Treinen also dismissed the possibility that the situation was creating additional pressure or contributing to any inconsistency. He said the magic number had not occupied his thoughts and that he had not noticed it affecting his teammates.
The right-hander compared the current situation with previous seasons when the division remained undecided until late in the schedule. He specifically recalled the 2024 race against the Padres, when the Dodgers had reason to wonder whether everything would come together in time for them to win the division.
Treinen believes this season feels different because Los Angeles has worked hard to establish a strong position. He expects the division championship to arrive when it arrives. In the meantime, the Dodgers are attempting to refine every aspect of their game, including his own performance.
“I honestly have zero idea where our magic number is until you said that," Treinen said. "I haven’t had a chance to follow it. I know we’re really focused on getting the best version of ourselves right now. So, to highlight your assumption of whether we’re struggling with back and forth or is it on our minds, I don’t think it’s on our minds. I haven’t seen it.
“There’s been years in the past where it’s come down to the wire, I think, in ‘24 against the Padres, you start wondering, is this going to click, and we’re going to have an opportunity to win a division?" Treinen continued.
"Right now, I think we’re just focused on being the best version of ourselves," he said. "We’ve worked really hard to be in a good position to win the division. That’ll come when it comes, and I think we’re just doing our best to fine-tune as much as we can, myself included.”
Treinen could be minimizing the significance of the race because he is a clubhouse veteran who wants to establish the proper example for younger teammates. The Dodgers could also be avoiding looking ahead because they have a morning game Thursday to complete the Cincinnati series.
Either way, Los Angeles will receive another opportunity to clinch the National League West on Thursday. Afterward, its attention can shift toward the next magic number, which is seven. That represents the number of victories needed to secure a bye through the Wild Card round.
Treinen’s value
Treinen’s perspective reflects the composure expected from an experienced reliever. Bullpen pitchers must move beyond disappointing results quickly because another demanding situation can arrive the following day.
His willingness to focus on execution instead of external milestones can help stabilize the clubhouse. Treinen understands that clinching celebrations follow consistent preparation, not scoreboard watching.
He also accepts personal responsibility by including himself among those who must continue improving. That accountability, calmness and postseason experience make his voice valuable as the Dodgers prepare for October.

Treinen’s perspective reflects the composure expected from an experienced reliever. Bullpen pitchers must move beyond disappointing results quickly because another demanding situation can arrive the following day.
His willingness to focus on execution instead of external milestones can help stabilize the clubhouse. Treinen understands that clinching celebrations follow consistent preparation, not scoreboard watching.
He also accepts personal responsibility by including himself among those who must continue improving. That accountability, calmness and postseason experience make his voice valuable as the Dodgers prepare for October.

title: Dodgers' Dalton Rushing: Advancing through hitting progression
author: RotoWire Staff
body:
The Dodgers announced Wednesday that Rushing (elbow) is continuing to work his way through a hitting progression with the hope of returning from the 10-day injured list before the end of the season, MLB.com reports.
If Rushing ends up returning, he would be limited to serving as a designated hitter or pinch hitter off the bench since his injured right elbow hasn't been responding well to throwing. The 25-year-old has made tremendous strides as a hitter during his second big-league season, slashing .249/.332/.466 with 12 home runs in 250 plate appearances before landing on the shelf Sept. 6.

title: Shohei Ohtani Gold Logoman game-worn jersey from 2025 Tokyo Series could set record
author: SCD Staff
body:
Auctions
Shohei Ohtani Gold Logoman game-worn jersey from 2025 Tokyo Series could set record
Shohei Ohtani’s game-used shoes from the 2025 MLB Tokyo Series have already sold for a $440,055, a record for baseball footwear.
Now his game-worn jersey from the historic game, his first MLB game in Japan, is coming to auction.
Ohtani’s game-worn Los Angeles Dodgers jersey is up for bid at TheRealest.com through Oct. 17. The auction house calls the jersey one of “the most significant Ohtani memorabilia pieces in existence” and projects it to become the most valuable modern-era game-worn baseball jersey ever sold.
Related Content:
Adding to its significance and value, the jersey carries the first Gold MLB Logoman ever worn in an official MLB game. First introduced by MLB in 2025, the Gold MLB Logoman Patch is worn by the previous season's MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year award winners. Ohtani was part of the first class of MLB players to ever wear the patch following his 2024 NL MVP.
“This is one of those rare pieces where the history, provenance and market all come together,” said Scott Keeney (aka DJ Skee), founder and CEO of The Realest. “This is the jersey from Shohei Ohtani's first Major League Baseball game ever played in Japan, and it carries the first Gold MLB Logoman ever worn in an official Major League Baseball game—a grail feature that has helped reset the market for Ohtani memorabilia on multiple occasions.”
The jersey also features Ohtani’s rare Kanji signature (大谷翔平) and personal inscriptions marking “Opening Day Tokyo Series,” “GU 3-18-25” and “NL MVP.”
Items containing Ohtani's game-worn MLB Gold Logoman patches have sold for millions, with a 1/1 Ohtani Gold Logoman Auto card selling for $3 million and a Dual Gold Logoman Auto carrying two game-worn patches and signatures in both English and kanji selling for a record $11 million in July 2026.
In his historic homecoming to Japan, Ohtani went 2-for-5 with two runs scored in the Dodgers’ 4-1 victory over the Chicago Cubs. Ohtani would go on to win his fourth MLB MVP in 2025 as the Dodgers won their second straight World Series.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Quickly Make Josue De Paula Change
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Thursday afternoon, the Los Angeles Dodgers will finish their series with the Cincinnati Reds in Ohio.
They have won two out of the first three games, so they will look to take the series.
Most recently, the Dodgers lost by a score of 6-2 on Wednesday night.
Josue De Paula was not in the lineup.
That said, he had one walk off the bench.
Los Angeles Dodgers Make De Paula Change
For Thursday’s game, the Dodgers have announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Dodgers 9/17 T. Edman CF F. Freeman 1B K. Tucker RF T. Hernández LF M. Muncy 3B J. De Paula DH H. Feduccia C A. Freeland 2B M. Rojas SS J. Wrobleski SP”
De Paula is back in the lineup (and hitting 6th) on Thursday.
The 21-year-old rookie is batting .143 with two hits, one home run, three RBIs, two runs and one stolen base in his first six games at the MLB level.
He made his debut earlier this month.
The Dodgers wrote (via X) on September 11: “The Dodgers have selected the contract of OF Josue De Paula and placed designated hitter/pitcher Shohei Ohtani on the injured list with right biceps inflammation, backdated to 9/8. In order to make room on the 40-man roster, the Dodgers moved LHP Eric Lauer to the 60-day injured list.”
Looking At The Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers come into the day as the top team in the National League West with a 92-60 record in 152 games.
They have won seven out of their last ten games (and are 45-32 in 77 games on the road).
Following the Reds, the Dodgers will return home to host the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Looking At The Reds Right Now
The Reds have had a tough 2026 season.
They are at the bottom of the National League Central with a 71-81 record in 152 games.
At home, the Reds have gone 37-40 in 77 games.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Make Sudden Mookie Betts Decision During Reds Series
author: Cole Sullivan
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are set to wrap up a four-game series on Thursday afternoon with the Cincinnati Reds after dropping Wednesday night’s game 6-2.
Ahead of the finale, however, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts decided to make some sudden changes to his starting lineup, one of which includes veteran star Mookie Betts, who is coming off a three-hit performance.
Dodgers Make Sudden Betts Decision
After hitting in the two-hole on Wednesday and drawing the start at shortstop, Betts is nowhere to be found in Thursday’s starting lineup as Roberts is seemingly giving the veteran the day off.
With that decision, as they gear up to face right-handed pitcher Brady Singer of the Reds, slugger Freddie Freeman will move into the two-hole behind leadoff hitter Tommy Edman, while Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernandez will bat in the three and four spots.
Here’s the full Dodgers lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Dodgers 9/17 T. Edman CF F. Freeman 1B K. Tucker RF T. Hernández LF M. Muncy 3B J. De Paula DH H. Feduccia C A. Freeland 2B M. Rojas SS J. Wrobleski SP.”
Dodgers 9/17
T. Edman CF
F. Freeman 1B
K. Tucker RF
T. Hernández LF
M. Muncy 3B
J. De Paula DH
H. Feduccia C
A. Freeland 2B
M. Rojas SS
J. Wrobleski SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 17, 2026
Looking at Betts’ 2026 Season
In his 13th MLB season and seventh as a member of the Dodgers, Betts has appeared in 114 games and is hitting .250 across 444 at-bats, with 64 runs, 111 hits, 20 home runs, and 62 RBIs while slugging .430 with a .746 OPS.
Dodgers Right Now
Los Angeles is dealing with a few concerning injuries at the moment. Most notably to Shohei Ohtani, but they still enter Thursday having clinched the NL West with a 92-60 overall record.
They’re still looking to secure a top-two seed, which would get them a first-round bye. After wrapping up their series with the Reds, they’ll finish the regular season with series against the San Francisco Giants, San Diego Padres, and then the Giants again.

title: Dodgers Stars Return to Lineup Looking for Series Win vs. Reds
author: Aaron Coloma
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers brought third baseman Max Muncy and outfielder Josue De Paula back into the lineup for Thursday’s series finale against the Cincinnati Reds.
The Dodgers lost Wednesday’s game after Cy Young winner Blake Snell went down with a groin injury after pitching just one inning. Luckily, Snell believes he can still make a start before the end of the regular season, which ends in less than two weeks.
LA won the first two games of the series, shutting down a powerful Reds lineup, and will look to do the same to win the series Wednesday.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
Justin Wrobleski will start for the Dodgers on Wednesday, making his 25th appearance of the regular season. Two of his last three appearances have come out of the bullpen, and none of them have lasted more than three innings since his return from the injured list with a forearm problem.
He has a 3.78 ERA on the year, striking out 111 batters over the course of 133.1 innings—his heaviest workload in an MLB season so far.
How deep into the game he goes depends on him, but the Dodgers will have backup in the form of Landon Knack whenever Wrobleski is ready to come out.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
The Dodgers still don’t have Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but Tommy Edman has replaced him well and will play center field on Thursday. Freddie Freeman moves up a couple of spots into the No. 2 hole, followed by right fielder Kyle Tucker, who will bat third.
Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez takes over the cleanup spot, followed by Muncy, who slides back into third base and bats fifth. De Paula serves as the designated hitter and will bat sixth, with catcher Hunter Feduccia giving Will Smith an off day in the No. 7 spot.
Second baseman Alex Freeland will bat eight for the Dodgers, with Miguel Rojas rounding out the lineup and playing shortstop—giving Mookie Betts a well-deserved rest day.
Dodgers Lineup vs. Reds
1. Tommy Edman, CF
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Kyle Tucker, RF
4. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
5. Max Muncy, 3B
6. Josue De Paula, DH
7. Hunter Feduccia, C
8. Alex Freeland, 2B
9. Miguel Rojas, SS
P. Justin Wrobleski, LHP
Who is Starting for the Reds?
Veteran right-hander Brady Singer is starting for the Reds, making his 30th appearance of the season. He has reached that mark in each of the last three seasons, and has 25 or more appearances in all seven of his MLB campaigns bar 2020.
He isn’t having the best year despite his regular consistency, though, as he has a 5.38 ERA through 150.2 innings with only 125 strikeouts on the season.
Singer didn’t face the Dodgers in last week’s series in Los Angeles, but he has a pretty good track record against the team. In three appearances against LA, all of which came during his time with Kansas City, he has a 1.89 ERA through 19 innings with 15 strikeouts.
The Dodgers will hope to break that trend on Thursday as they look to bring themselves even closer to a first-round postseason bye. The first pitch of Thursday’s game comes at 9:40 p.m. PT.

rss_title: Dodgers Stars Return to Lineup Looking for Series Win vs. Reds
rss_body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers brought third baseman Max Muncy and outfielder Josue De Paula back into the lineup for Thursday’s series finale against the Cincinnati Reds.
The Dodgers lost Wednesday’s game after Cy Young winner Blake Snell went down with a groin injury after pitching just one inning. Luckily, Snell believes he can still make a start before the end of the regular season, which ends in less than two weeks.
LA won the first two games of the series, shutting down a powerful Reds lineup, and will look to do the same to win the series Wednesday.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
Justin Wrobleski will start for the Dodgers on Wednesday, making his 25th appearance of the regular season. Two of his last three appearances have come out of the bullpen, and none of them have lasted more than three innings since his return from the injured list with a forearm problem.
He has a 3.78 ERA on the year, striking out 111 batters over the course of 133.1 innings—his heaviest workload in an MLB season so far.
How deep into the game he goes depends on him, but the Dodgers will have backup in the form of Landon Knack whenever Wrobleski is ready to come out.

The Dodgers still don’t have Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but Tommy Edman has replaced him well and will play center field on Thursday. Freddie Freeman moves up a couple of spots into the No. 2 hole, followed by right fielder Kyle Tucker, who will bat third.

title: Dodgers find silver lining with Edgardo Henriquez's injury after MRI
author: Matthew Moreno
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are on the verge of clinching the National League West for a 13th time in the past 14 seasons, but it’s coming with notable questions, if not concern, regarding health heading into October.
Shohei Ohtani, Dalton Rushing, Andy Pages and Edgardo Henriquez are among the team’s key contributors who currently are on the injured list. Blake Snell could find himself there after leaving his start on Wednesday due to left groin tightness.
Henriquez was the most recent addition to the IL, due to an official diagnosis of low back discomfort. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts suggested there was the potential for an oblique issue as well.
Edgardo Henriquez MRI results
Henriquez returned to Los Angeles before the end of the road trip in order to meet with doctors and undergo testing. According to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic, an MRI revealed Henriquez suffered a back strain.
Edgardo Henriquez has a “low-grade” back strain, Dave Roberts said. Dodgers are “hopeful” to have him back for the postseason.
— Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) September 16, 2026
Prior to having the MRI results, Roberts had previously expressed a hope Henriquez would return in time for the postseason. That possibility will hinge on his recovery process.
What is already guaranteed is the hard-throwing righty won’t pitch again during the 2026 regular season because of being ineligible to get activated within the remaining timeframe. Henriquez’s status is further reason for the Dodgers to secure one of the top two seeds in the NL and thus a first-round bye in the postseason.
Doing so would push the Dodgers’ first playoff game to Oct. 3 with the start of the NL Division Series.
Henriquez allowed two runs last Sunday against the Miami Marlins in what was his final appearance before going on the IL. He retired just two batters after entering in the eighth inning, trying to protect a 3-0 lead.
Henriquez gave up two singles and a walk, which loaded the bases. Then another base hit drove in two runs, prompting Dodgers manager Dave Roberts to turn to Tanner Scott.
The 24-year-old finishes his 2026 season with 61 appearances in what became a true breakout year. Henriquez went 4-1 with a 2.85 ERA and also set a Dodgers record for the fastest pitch thrown on a strikeout earlier this year.
Henriquez was an option to receive more save opportunities moving forward as he continued to impress in high-leverage situations while others in the bullpen struggled. That could still hold true, but now health becomes paramount.

title: Dodgers Announce Starting Pitcher, Roster Move for Thursday's Game vs Reds
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to win their series against the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday and clinch the National League West division for the 13th time in the last 14 years.
The Dodgers had the opportunity to clinch the NL West on Wednesday, but fell to the Reds, 6-2, while the San Diego Padres beat the Colorado Rockies.
On Thursday, a Dodgers win or Padres loss will make it official, as LA's magic number remains just one.
Dodgers Calling Up Landon Knack, Optioning Bobby Miller
The Dodgers are shuffling the bullpen ahead of Thursday's game, with right-handed pitcher Landon Knack returning to the active roster and right-hander Bobby Miller heading back to Triple-A.
Miller pitched during Wednesday night's impromptu bullpen game after Blake Snell exited with an injury, allowing two runs on three hits with one strikeout over 2.1 innings.
It was his second appearance at the big league level this season after spending most of the year on the injured list.
As for Knack, he last pitched in MLB on Aug. 12, when he threw 2.2 scoreless innings against the Kansas City Royals. In his two prior appearances for the Dodgers this season, he allowed five runs over five innings of work.
Knack is expected to factor into the team's pitching plans on Thursday, likely taking down multiple innings. He won't be the starting pitcher, though, which has finally been announced.
Dodgers vs Reds Pitching Matchup on Thursday
The Dodgers announced that left-handed pitcher Justin Wrobleski is getting the spot start on Thursday.
The 2026 All-Star has struggled mightily in the second half of the season, sporting a 7.09 ERA over 33 innings while allowing 13 home runs.
Wrobleski went on the injured list last month with a forearm injury and returned in a bullpen role. However, amid the injuries to a handful of the team's starters, Wrobleski is set to make his second start in the last two weeks.
He and Knack will likely combine to take down a majority of the innings on Thursday.
Opposite Wrobleski will be veteran right-hander Brady Singer, who's 6-14 with a 5.38 ERA across 29 starts and 150.2 innings this season.
He's also struggled in the season's second half, owning a 6.34 ERA over 11 starts and 61 innings since the break.
How to Watch Dodgers vs Reds on Thursday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Cincinnati Reds on Thursday, Sept. 16 is 9:40 a.m. PT/12:40 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.

title: 【MLB】「彼は重要な存在」佐々木朗希、リリーフ濃厚から先発で復帰戦 スネル緊急降板で風向き一変 患部の〝接着剤〟は公式戦で使用可
author: 横山尚杜
body:
【シンシナティ（米オハイオ州）16日（日本時間17日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの佐々木朗希投手（24）がレッズ戦の試合前にライブBP（実戦形式の打撃練習）に登板。「右手中指のまめ」で負傷者リスト（IL）入り後、2度目で4回50球を消化した。レッズ戦に先発したスネルが「左股関節の張り」を訴え、1回19球で緊急降板。ポストシーズンの先発に暗雲が立ち込め、佐々木は復帰戦で先発する見込みとなった。
地区優勝が手に届く直前で、アクシデント続きだ。ドジャースは先発したスネルが1回19球で緊急降板。既往歴4度の「左股関節の張り」を訴え、次回登板が白紙。ポストシーズン（PS）に黄色信号が灯った。一方、「右手中指のまめ」から復帰目前の佐々木は、試合前のライブBPで4回50球を消化。救援転向が濃厚な状況から一気に風向きが変わった。
「ロウキは今週末のジャイアンツ戦では先発しないと思う。ただ、彼の次の登板は先発になると思う」
試合後のロバーツ監督は佐々木の復帰戦が先発になる見込みだと明言。当初は山本由伸、スクバル、スネル、グラスノーでPS先発枠は満席だったが、空席が出る可能性が浮上。この日の佐々木は患部に公式戦でも使用可能なダーマボンド（皮膚接着剤）を患部に施し、球威抜群の速球を投げ込んだ。
ドジャースはスネル緊急降板で、救援陣をつぎ込むも敗戦。地区優勝マジック「1」で迎えたが、自力で決められず2位パドレスも勝利したため、敵地に用意されたシャンパンの封は閉ざされたままとなった。17日（同18日）レッズ戦で勝利するか、パドレスがロッキーズに敗れた時点で5年連続の地区優勝が決定する。
「彼は重要な存在になる」。ロバーツ監督は佐々木をポストシーズンのキーマンに挙げた。後半戦は内容のある投球を見せていた矢先のアクシデントだった。シーズン最終週で、2年連続のPSに弾みをつける。

地区優勝が手に届く直前で、アクシデント続きだ。ドジャースは先発したスネルが1回19球で緊急降板。既往歴4度の「左股関節の張り」を訴え、次回登板が白紙。ポストシーズン（PS）に黄色信号が灯った。一方、「右手中指のまめ」から復帰目前の佐々木は、試合前のライブBPで4回50球を消化。救援転向が濃厚な状況から一気に風向きが変わった。
「ロウキは今週末のジャイアンツ戦では先発しないと思う。ただ、彼の次の登板は先発になると思う」
試合後のロバーツ監督は佐々木の復帰戦が先発になる見込みだと明言。当初は山本由伸、スクバル、スネル、グラスノーでPS先発枠は満席だったが、空席が出る可能性が浮上。この日の佐々木は患部に公式戦でも使用可能なダーマボンド（皮膚接着剤）を患部に施し、球威抜群の速球を投げ込んだ。
ドジャースはスネル緊急降板で、救援陣をつぎ込むも敗戦。地区優勝マジック「1」で迎えたが、自力で決められず2位パドレスも勝利したため、敵地に用意されたシャンパンの封は閉ざされたままとなった。17日（同18日）レッズ戦で勝利するか、パドレスがロッキーズに敗れた時点で5年連続の地区優勝が決定する。
「彼は重要な存在になる」。ロバーツ監督は佐々木をポストシーズンのキーマンに挙げた。後半戦は内容のある投球を見せていた矢先のアクシデントだった。シーズン最終週で、2年連続のPSに弾みをつける。

title: Blake Snell Provides Injury Update As Concern Grows
author: Aaliyan Mohammed
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers pulled Blake Snell from Wednesday's start after just one inning with left groin tightness.
Snell threw just 19 pitches, and the timing of the injury is a major concern. The regular season is coming to an end, and the Dodgers are about to start playing postseason baseball. Snell was expected to be in the postseason rotation, so an injury has the potential to throw off the Dodgers' plans.
The extent of Snell's injury is unknown, but he does not think it is anything too serious.
"I think it was more of a scare," Snell told The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
"I'll see where I'm at, day to day," Snell said, "but I should be good."
Snell said he first felt the issue in the bullpen on a slider, and then was trying to avoid using his lower half on the mound. His velocity was down a tick, and at this point in the year, it's better to be safe than sorry. The game turned into a bullpen day for the Dodgers, and they ultimately lost to the Cincinnati Reds.
"I wasn't trying to use my lower half. It was only a couple pitches where I got into my legs and threw the ball hard," Snell said. "Outside of that, I was kind of guiding it in there."
Snell has missed most of the season with injuries. It started with shoulder fatigue and then a procedure to remove loose bodies from his elbow. However, when he has been on the mound, he looks like the Cy Young Award winner he is.
The Dodgers will reportedly wait to see how he feels on Thursday before sending him for imaging. If he goes to the injured list, the Dodgers may have no choice but to return Roki Sasaki as a starter off the injured list. There was discussion about sending him to the bullpen now since that will likely be his role in October, but plans may change.

title: Tarik Skubal could still find his way to Braves despite trade failure
author: Nick Halden
body:
One of the biggest pieces of trade deadline news for the Atlanta Braves is the fact that the franchise made a strong push to add current Los Angeles Dodger Tarik Skubal. It seems that the Detroit Tigers had fallen in love with a certain Dodger prospect, leaving Atlanta little chance of completing a deal that would've cemented the Braves alongside the two-time defending champs as clear World Series favorites. With this in mind, it is fair to have a level of frustration around the failed deal, while realizing the road to adding Skubal might not be gone just yet.
The left-hander is getting ready to hit free agency and unquestionably will be at the top of any wishlist for a fanbase looking for starting pitching. Skubal is an unquestioned ace who could step in and take pressure off an aging Chris Sale and allow the Braves to get the absolute best out of their current options.
Signing Skubal is going to be undeniably expensive, but the Braves could look to make salary room by parting ways with a combination of Sean Murphy, Jurickson Profar, Mike Yastrzemski, and Reynaldo Lopez, all of whom are on high-paying deals and could easily have the page turned to create the needed space to sign a player like Skubal.
Already, you know the Braves have a level of interest in the pitcher based on the trade deadline pursuit. Waiting until the offseason and only needing to give up salary to add the pitcher, and doing so on a long-term deal, is arguably the better decision if the Dodgers aren't able to beat the Braves to the punch and offer an unrealistic deal.
Braves Fans Shouldn't Give up on Dreams of Adding Tarik Skubal to Atlanta's Rotation Just Yet
Skubal has been solid with the Dodgers, offering 50.0 innings and a 2.52 ERA, producing the level of production you expect from a top-of-the-rotation option. Everything about Skubal's past three seasons suggests that this level of production can be maintained, and the Braves would be adding a defining presence in the rotation for years to come.
Injuries to Spencer Strider and the team's young options have left no question that you can never have too much pitching. Both Martin Perez and Tyler Mahle are set to hit free agency as well, making it all the more urgent that you find a way to add to the current rotation.
Signing Skubal is going to be difficult, but very plausible for an Atlanta team with a core capable of World Series contention and the ability to open up salary space. No question, it is a fit to keep a close eye on over the early weeks of the offseason.

title: Shohei Ohtani Could Make Dodgers Return Directly in Postseason
author: Nelson Espinal
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani may not even need to return in the regular season to play in the postseason.
Japanese reporter Masaya Kotani asked general manager Brandon Gomes whether Ohtani could return in the postseason after missing the rest of the regular season.
“Yeah, I think that’s a possibility,” Gomes said, according to the translation of Kotani’s tweet. “The most important thing is that he’s healthy and in good shape. Whether it’s during the regular season or after that, as long as he’s fully prepared and ready to go, we’re fine with it.”
Ohtani is currently sitting out with a bicep injury from pitching, which has landed him on the injured list, and is also dealing with left soreness, according to manager Dave Roberts.
What is the next step for Shohei Ohtani?
Ohtani spent some time hitting off a tee on Tuesday at Dodger Stadium, his first taste of baseball action since landing on the injured list.
The Japanese star “felt good” after the session, per the Dodgers skipper.
The Dodgers will likely have him continue swinging the bat gradually, and they will monitor him every step of the way to see whether a regular-season activation is possible.
According to Roberts, Ohtani spent Wednesday resting back in Los Angeles, not engaging in baseball activities.
The Dodgers have one more game in Cincinnati left for Thursday, Sept. 17th, before they travel to Los Angeles for two home stands against the Giants and Padres.
During their time in LA, with the coaching staff available to evaluate Ohtani, they’ll have a clearer picture of his outlook before the season ends.
Compared to what was previously assumed, Ohtani’s regular-season participation matters much less if he plays in the postseason no matter what.

title: Dodgers Notes: LA Cuts Ties With Outfielder, Blake Snell Injury Update, Edwin Diaz Disappointment
author: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers lost to the Cincinnati Reds, 6-2, on Wednesday and fell to 92-60 on the year.
Blake Snell pitched just one inning before he was removed from his start due to groin tightness. After Blake Treinen pitched a clean second inning, the Reds took advantage of the impromptu bullpen game and halted any potential NL West-clinching celebrations.
Offensively, Mookie Betts still shined with a three-hit outing and Will Smith also enjoyed a multi-hit night. The backstop appears to be gaining his footing once again, hitting .273 with three RBIs in his last seven games.
Ahead of the eventual defeat, the Dodgers surprisingly designated an outfielder for assignment hitting .218 in his first 20 MLB games in order to make room on the roster to activate All-Star right-hander Kris Bubic. Though it wasn't the most ideal situation to be making his debut with the two-time defending champions, Bubic struck out two in a scoreless eighth inning.
After the game, both Snell and manager Dave Roberts provided an update on the left-hander's injury. Snell revealed that he felt his groin "grab" during a pregame bullpen and knew then he shouldn't go beyond the first inning. Regardless, he said he "should be good" to make another start before the postseason.
Roberts, however, wasn't as sure.
“It’s a possibility,” Roberts said. “I like where his head is at, but he just can’t afford any more setbacks. So, whether it’s his next start or being pushed back or whatever it is, we’ve got to make sure that he comes out ready to go in the postseason.”
Finally, right-hander and presumed closer Edwin Díaz doesn't appear to be making much progress amid his return from another injured list stint. Manager Dave Roberts, among others, was not happy with the results of his rehab outing over the weekend, and knows that at this moment, Díaz is not someone a World Series favorite wants in their bullpen this postseason.
Díaz had a slightly better outing Wednesday (one scoreless inning) after his disastrous Sunday performance of five earned runs in 0.2 innings.

After the game, both Snell and manager Dave Roberts provided an update on the left-hander's injury. Snell revealed that he felt his groin "grab" during a pregame bullpen and knew then he shouldn't go beyond the first inning. Regardless, he said he "should be good" to make another start before the postseason.
Roberts, however, wasn't as sure.
“It’s a possibility,” Roberts said. “I like where his head is at, but he just can’t afford any more setbacks. So, whether it’s his next start or being pushed back or whatever it is, we’ve got to make sure that he comes out ready to go in the postseason.”
Finally, right-hander and presumed closer Edwin Díaz doesn't appear to be making much progress amid his return from another injured list stint. Manager Dave Roberts, among others, was not happy with the results of his rehab outing over the weekend, and knows that at this moment, Díaz is not someone a World Series favorite wants in their bullpen this postseason.
Díaz had a slightly better outing Wednesday (one scoreless inning) after his disastrous Sunday performance of five earned runs in 0.2 innings.
