title: Ranking the most important Dodgers who could come back for the MLB Playoffs
author: Christopher Kline
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are on track to win the NL West and probably earn a first-round bye in the postseason. That comes despite a recent onslaught of injuries. Los Angeles is not unaccustomed to a stacked injury list, but the Dodgers' elite depth — aided by a top-ranked farm system and unrivalred spending power — makes them uniquely resilient.
What has helped L.A. win back-to-back World Series titles, however, is their knack for getting healthy at the right time and charging into October at full strength. The Dodgers are hoping to do just that, again. Let's rank six potential returners who could make an outsized impact.
6. RHP Edwin Díaz
Should Edwin Díaz actually come back for the playoffs? He got rocked in his recent Triple-A rehab appearance. The Dodgers' prized $69 million investment has only pitched 13.2 innings in the majors this season, with a disastrous 11.85 ERA (not a typo). Díaz has not looked right at any point.
While the Dodgers presumably want such an expensive and accomplished reliever on the postseason roster, it may be smarter to punt on this season entirely. Díaz is more than capable of rebuilding confidence and getting healthy in the offseason, but it's unclear if L.A. can rely on him in even the lowest-leverage spots currently. Rather than playing with fire, so to speak, the Dodgers should probably lean on their spectacular bullpen depth and keep Díaz on the sidelines. The risk far outweighs the potential reward of rushing him back.
That said, when healthy, Díaz has a long track record as one of MLB's best closers. We know he can electify in the late innings. If the Dodgers are confident for reasons we on the outside aren't privy too, never say never on a triumphant turnaround.
5. RHP Roki Sasaki
Through two seasons, the Rōki Sasaki experience has not quite lived up to expectations for Dodgers fans. Hailed as the best Japanese pitching prospect in a generation, the 24-year-old looks an awful lot like... a prospect. A work in progress. Los Angeles expected immediate results. Now, the Dodgers are hoping Sasaki can iron out command issues against MLB competition. He appeared briefly in the minors this season, but the Dodgers are effectively all-in on Sasaki as a major league pitcher.
Sasaki is expected to recover from a blister before the playoffs, although the Dodgers are uncertain about his exact role. The rotation is much too deep for Sasaki to start in a must-win environment. He was effectively L.A.'s closer last October — a role in which he thrived — but a healthy Tanner Scott removes Sasaki from consideration for that role. Expect him in the bullpen, probably handling bulk work if one of L.A.'s starters is forced out early.
4. C Dalton Rushing
Dalton Rushing was recently returned to the IL after suffering a setback in his recovery from UCL surgery. He's done catching for the season, but L.A. still hopes the 25-year-old can return as a hitter. Of course, if Rushing is effectively relegated to DH, it will be hard to get him in the lineup with Shohei Ohtani also on the roster. Rushing could end up as a situational, pinch-hitter type in October, if he's even on the roster.
It's a credit to how deep the Dodgers are that Rushing being "situational," rather than essential, is even in the cards. The rookie backstop cooled off after the All-Star break, but he's still phenomenally talented. He has a .798 OPS and 120 wRC+ as a rookie, with 12 home runs in only 250 at-bats.
Rushing is stuck behind Will Smith on the org chart, which complicates his future somewhat, but the Dodgers will find ways to use him if he's available.
3. RHP Edgardo Henriquez
The Dodgers hope Edgardo Henriquez can return from a low-grade back strain come the playoffs. The 24-year-old fireballer has quickly established himself as one of baseball's most dominant relievers. He has a 2.85 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with 71 strikeouts in 60.0 innings pitched this season; he ranks in MLB's 99th percentile for both hard-hit rate (27.1 percent) and average fastball velo (100.8 mph).
Henriquez is more than a hard-thrower. He misses barrels and limits explosive hits, able to force groundballs or lifeless bloopers just as often as he forces swing-and-miss. He leans heavily on his four-seam and sinker combo, with a sweeping slider that leaves opposing hitters gasping for air (.191 xwOBA). Should Henriquez return in time, the Dodgers can plug him right into high-leverage spots and expect results. He's the real deal, folks.
2. OF Andy Pages
Andy Pages is back in the batting cage after breaking his hand in mid-August. The Dodgers' centerfielder has enjoyed a proper breakout campaign, posting a .797 OPS and 119 wRC+ with elite defensive metrics and 12 stolen bases. In terms of fWAR, or wins above replacement, Pages ranks third among L.A. positional players (3.9), behind only Shohei Ohtani (6.8) and Max Muncy (4.0).
The Dodgers really need Pages on cleanup duty in centerfield. He covers so much ground and features a killer arm, which wipes runs off the board. Pages' bat cooled down before the injury, but he's still far more dangerous than L.A.'s alternatives — although the recent promotion of top prospect Josue De Paula does create a difficult decision for manager Dave Roberts, assuming the DH spot reverts back to Ohtani.
Speaking of which...
1. DH Shohei Ohtani
This was obvious, yeah? Shohei Ohtani is currently on ice as he attempts to shed bicep and knee problems. That said, the Dodgers plan to get him back before the regular season ends — and it would be absolutely shocking if Ohtani weren't leading off in Game 1 of the Dodgers' first postseason series.
The nagging nature of Ohtani's injuries mean he won't take the mound again in 2026, but he's still the most valuable hitter in the majors, on balance. Yes, Yordan Álvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong are enjoying better seasons, but Ohtani is the man you want at the plate in a big spot. Drafting a fantasy team, he's your No. 1 pick. So on and so forth.
After spending the early portion of his MLB career on an unserious Angels team, Ohtani is two-for-two in the World Series since joining the Dodgers. He has consistently come up large in the playoffs. Assuming Ohtani is anywhere close to 100 percent, the Dodgers are once again (easy) favorites to win it all.

title: Dodgers Make Kyle Tucker Playoff Roster Decision After $240 Million Disappointment
author: Peter Chawaga; Contributor
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have a difficult decision ahead as they prepare for the postseason, and it could mean a harsh end for a star offseason acquisition.
With All-Star reliever Edwin Diaz struggling to earn his way back into the bullpen following an injury, the team has indicated that he won't be guaranteed a spot on the playoff roster.
"All-Star closer Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, as Tanner Scott did a year ago, and his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City has gone poorly enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Monday the club could leave the three-time All-Star closer off the postseason roster," Fabian Ardaya wrote for The Athletic.
That uncertainty creates an obvious question about another high-profile Dodgers addition who has struggled throughout his first season in Los Angeles: Kyle Tucker.
The four-time All-Star signed a four-year, $240 million contract with the Dodgers during the offseason, but his production has fallen well short of what the team presumably expected when it made that investment.
Los Angeles Dodgers Send Definitive Kyle Tucker Message With Playoffs Looming
Though the Dodgers' willingness to leave Diaz off of the postseason roster suggests the team is evaluating performance alone, Roberts sent a clear message about any upcoming roster decisions involving Tucker.
"I told him, I'm gonna ride or die with him," Roberts said, according to the New York Post's Jack Harris.
That commitment comes despite a season in which Tucker has produced a .226/.327/.374 slash line with 15 home runs and 66 RBI through 143 games, soliciting calls that he be benched or platooned, if not removed from the upcoming playoff roster altogether. His performance has also been dramatically different at home than it has been on the road. Tucker has hit .187 with a .572 OPS at Dodger Stadium, compared with a .266 average and .826 OPS away from home.
That split adds another layer to the pressure surrounding Tucker as the Dodgers move toward the postseason.
$240 Million Los Angeles Dodgers Disappointment Brings Kyle Tucker Playoff Question Into Focus
Roberts' definitive commitment is particularly notable given how disappointing his first season has been relative to his contract.
"At this point, it is all adding up to a lost season for the 29-year-old, who is threatening to become one of the biggest free-agent flops in at least the sport's recent high-priced history," Harris added. "And yet, the Dodgers aren't wavering from their commitment to keep playing the four-time All-Star, rolling the dice 'talent level' and 'proven track record,' as Roberts cited, by keeping him in the lineup for the long haul."
That gives Tucker a clear path to remain part of the Dodgers' postseason plans, even as the club evaluates other difficult roster decisions.
This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Possible Blake Snell timeline after injury would ruin Dodgers' master plan
author: Matthew Swigonski
body:
Just when you thought that everything was starting to snap back into place, the Los Angeles Dodgers could be dealing with yet another possible injury. After throwing just one inning against the Cincinnati Reds, Blake Snell was forced to exit the game with left groin tightness. While it is still way too early to hit the nuclear panic button, another Snell injury would pretty much spoil the team's postseason plans.
When it was announced that Shohei Ohtani would no longer pitch for the remainder of the season, the Dodgers were certainly disappointed. But with several strong pitchers already on the road back from injury, they knew that they had options. But with Snell unable to throw more than 19 pitches against the Reds, he may no longer be one of those starting options in the playoffs. That could put the Dodgers in a box that they don’t want to be in.
Could Snell’s early exit have been completely precautionary? Certainly. But it’s still not a good look for a pitcher who has yet to even throw 40 innings in 2026. It’s an especially bad look for the same pitcher who has already been placed on the IL twice this season.
As noted by Dodgers reporter Blake Harris, it’s an even worse look for that very pitcher who suffered a left groin strain just two seasons ago. While pitching for the San Francisco Giants in 2024, Snell was shelved for five weeks for a strain to the same side of the groin he just aggravated in the game against the Reds.
A Blake Snell injury could limit the Dodgers’ World Series run
Again, it’s too early to tell for certain. We might not know the extent of Snell's potential injury for a day or two. However, the most optimistic of recovery timelines would still diminish any chance that Snell has at starting any of the games in the Dodgers’ first postseason series, especially if Snell is dealing with a similar injury to his strained groin.
At 92-59, the Dodgers are in a good position to finish the regular season as one of the top two teams in the National League. That would mean that their first postseason game wouldn’t be until October 3. That would give Snell just two weeks to rest up and treat a potential injury. If he’s looking at anything more than just an acute case of tightness, Snell may even be unavailable for the entire postseason.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow, the Dodgers will have a formidable top three to lead the way. That may be enough to get them through a five-game series in fairly good shape. But if they advance to the NL Championship Series, they will need a fourth starting pitcher.
So what options do the Dodgers have if they need to replace Snell? Emmet Sheehan has looked like an entirely different pitcher over his last two starts. After striking out 10 hitters in 5.2 innings against the Reds on September 7, he backed it up with six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins in his most recent start. But even with renewed faith in Sheehan, would the Dodgers be comfortable giving him the ball in such a high-stakes series?
Justin Wrobleski has been wildly inconsistent in the second half of the season. With 20 earned runs allowed over his last 20.2 innings pitched, he would likely not be an option for Dodgers manager Dave Roberts. In a perfect world, Kris Bubic would have been the next man up in the rotation, but he will be limited to the bullpen following his own return from the IL.
If the Dodgers are looking at even a modest injury for Snell, their postseason rotation could be their most serious question mark heading into October. They could have enough firepower to cover their weak spot, but it may ultimately be their undoing.

title: Will Smith is Dodgers nominee for Roberto Clemente Award
author: Eric Stephen
body:
Dodgers catcher Will Smith was the team's nominee for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award, the annual honor that recognizes players for their contributions both on and off the field, named for the legendary Hall of Fame former Pittsburgh Pirates outfielder.
Smith and his wife Cara founded Catching Hope, "a nonprofit organization working to help underprivileged children with critical skills needed for leadership, self-advocacy, and self-sufficiency." Among the projects by the organization this year include an art installation at Marquez Elementary School in Los Angeles in April, a comedy night in Beverly Hills in May as part of the Netflix is a Joke Fest, a community clinic for an elementary school at Dodger Stadium in May, and a visit to UCLA hospital in August.
Will Smith stopped by the @UCLAHealth Santa Monica Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Clinic to surprise some special Dodger fans. 🥹 pic.twitter.com/3FpwRKY7Y0
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) August 17, 2026
Fans can vote on the Clemente Award through September 27, the final day of the regular season. The fan vote will count as one vote in a panel that also includes members of the MLB commissioner's office, MLB.com writers, MLB television media partners, and members of Roberto Clemente's family.
The winner will be announced during the World Series. Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts won the award last year.
Old friend Justin Turner, who won the Clemente Award in 2022 and was also the Dodgers nominee for the honor in 2017, 2018, 2020, and 2021 as well, won another title on Tuesday night. His Tijuana Toros beat the Tabasco Olmecas four games to two to win the best-of-7 Serie del Rey to win the Mexican League championship.
Turner hit .295/.395/.469 with 21 doubles and six home runs in 65 games in his age-41 season for Tijuana, which was managed by former Dodgers outfielder Roberto Kelly. The World Baseball Softball Confederation has more on Tijuana's Tuesday triumph.

title: 더 리얼리스트, 오타니 쇼헤이의 역사적인 2025 MLB 도쿄 시리즈 실착 저지 경매
author: Joyce Li
body:
The Realest가 Shohei Ohtani가 2025 MLB Tokyo Series 개막전에서 실제 착용한 Los Angeles Dodgers 저지에 대한 일반 입찰을 개시하였다.
이 컬렉터블에는 공식 경기에서 착용된 것 중 최초의 Gold MLB Logoman 패치와 함께, 희소성이 높은 한자 사인과 친필 문구가 더해져 있다.
해당 아이템에 대한 입찰은 현재 TheRealest.com에서 진행 중이며, 2026년 10월 17일 공식 종료될 예정이다.
더 리얼리스트가 오타니 쇼헤이의 2025 MLB 도쿄 시리즈 다저스 실착 저지 경매를 공식 시작했다. 이 저지는 2025년 3월 18일 도쿄돔에서 열린 시즌 개막전에 착용한 것으로, 오타니가 일본에서 처음 출전한 메이저리그 공식 경기의 유니폼이다.
이 저지는 역사적 이정표가 된 유물로, 공식 경기에서 처음으로 착용된 골드 MLB 로고맨 패치를 달았다. 이 표식은 2025년부터 디펜딩 MVP, 사이영상, 신인왕 수상자에게 적용됐다. 유니폼에는 첫 골드 패치와 함께 공식 2025 도쿄 시리즈 엠블럼, 다저스의 페르난도 발렌수엘라 등번호 34 추모 패치가 그대로 부착돼 있다.
개별 소장 이력 또한 특별하다. 오타니는 저지에 한자로 ‘大谷翔平’이라고 직접 사인하고, ‘Opening Day Tokyo Series’, ‘GU 3-18-25’, ‘NL MVP’라는 친필 문구를 남겼다. 이 피스는 MLB 경기장 현장 인증 프로그램을 통해 검증됐으며, SIA 포토매칭의 사진 대조와 더 리얼리스트의 인증 평가 프로그램 일환으로 진행된 파나틱스 어센틱의 기록 절차도 거쳤다.
오타니 쇼헤이의 2025 MLB 도쿄 시리즈 실착 저지 경매는 현재 더 리얼리스트에서 진행 중이며, 2026년 10월 17일 토요일에 마감된다.

title: The Shoulders on Which Titles Are Built: Tarik Skubal Is Calibrated for October
author: Tom Verducci
body:
In the last moment before fury overtakes calm, Tarik Skubal stands on the plateau of a 10-inch-tall pedestal of dirt and clay as an imposing and finely calibrated 240 pounds of human pitching machinery. Nothing superfluous. Nothing without purpose. Brutally efficient.
The calibrations that lead him to the mound for a playoff game are no different than for a midseason start. The pulses of electromagnetic waves over his body, the four shots of espresso, the hot tub, the peanut butter and jelly sandwich, the dynamic warmup, the 17 to 22 pitches in the bullpen ... all of it as detailed, immutable and unassailable as Newton’s second law of motion. Skubal is so detail-obsessed that he tracks the speed of the bar when he lifts weights.
“I’m always monitoring everything,” he says. “I’m making sure that I’m doing the right things to where my body is ready to go and my nervous system is ready to go out there and pitch. It’s very complex, but it’s also simple. Everything that I do has a plan. There is always a reason for everything. I don’t do anything just mindlessly.”
All of it is done so that when it comes time for the catcher to transmit the audio signal for one of Skubal’s five pitches, Skubal is good with whatever is the choice.
The planning, scheming and studying are over. It is time to accelerate particles with ferocious force. Skubal is the only pitcher on the planet who can throw 100 mph and get hitters to miss his changeup almost half the time, the highest whiff rate on the pitch among such flamethrowers who have thrown it at least 300 times. He owns both ends of the speed spectrum.
“I’m just going to go out there and compete and try to execute pitches, so I let the catchers call what they see,” he says. “There’s a lot more stuff going on cerebrally with catchers than with me when I’m on the mound. When I’m on the mound, it’s just, get the pitch. Whatever it is, execute the pitch. I don’t really want to be thinking about too much.
“The time in between starts? I’m thinking about stuff. The time in between innings? I’m thinking about stuff. But when I’m out there, I want my process to be pretty simple.”
“If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.”
The quote is attributable to Isaac Newton in 1675, though it might be appropriated these days by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman. Skubal rocketed to an elite pitching level in 2023 with the help of a 3-D printer. Tigers pitching coaches Chris Fetter and Robin Lund introduced him to the concept of seam-shifted wake, the uneven airflow the raised seams create over a baseball. A pitcher without natural pronation can still deaden the baseball and create movement by harnessing these aerodynamics.
Lund, a former associate professor of kinesiology with a PhD in exercise science, had been hired that season from the University of Iowa. He had the Tigers use a 3-D printer to create a plastic mold that cradles half a baseball. The mold had a circular opening that let Lund draw a black dot with a Sharpie inside the horseshoe of the seams. “Keep the dot on top of the baseball,” he told Skubal, “and think about cutting across the face of the ball.”

• T-minus 120 minutes: Four shots of espresso. “That way,” he says, “I’m heavily caffeinated and ready to go.”

The glove points toward the upper deck, flashed to the hitter like a magician’s diversion. His shoulders are severely slanted, as if throwing a javelin.

He also is the only writer to be a game analyst for World Series telecasts. He lives in New Jersey with his wife, with whom he has two children.

rss_title: The Shoulders on Which Titles Are Built: Tarik Skubal Is Calibrated for October
rss_body:
In the last moment before fury overtakes calm, Tarik Skubal stands on the plateau of a 10-inch-tall pedestal of dirt and clay as an imposing and finely calibrated 240 pounds of human pitching machinery. Nothing superfluous. Nothing without purpose. Brutally efficient.
The calibrations that lead him to the mound for a playoff game are no different than for a midseason start. The pulses of electromagnetic waves over his body, the four shots of espresso, the hot tub, the peanut butter and jelly sandwich, the dynamic warmup, the 17 to 22 pitches in the bullpen ... all of it as detailed, immutable and unassailable as Newton’s second law of motion. Skubal is so detail-obsessed that he tracks the speed of the bar when he lifts weights.
“I’m always monitoring everything,” he says. “I’m making sure that I’m doing the right things to where my body is ready to go and my nervous system is ready to go out there and pitch. It’s very complex, but it’s also simple. Everything that I do has a plan. There is always a reason for everything. I don’t do anything just mindlessly.”
All of it is done so that when it comes time for the catcher to transmit the audio signal for one of Skubal’s five pitches, Skubal is good with whatever is the choice.
The planning, scheming and studying are over. It is time to accelerate particles with ferocious force. Skubal is the only pitcher on the planet who can throw 100 mph and get hitters to miss his changeup almost half the time, the highest whiff rate on the pitch among such flamethrowers who have thrown it at least 300 times. He owns both ends of the speed spectrum.
“I’m just going to go out there and compete and try to execute pitches, so I let the catchers call what they see,” he says. “There’s a lot more stuff going on cerebrally with catchers than with me when I’m on the mound. When I’m on the mound, it’s just, get the pitch. Whatever it is, execute the pitch. I don’t really want to be thinking about too much.
“The time in between starts? I’m thinking about stuff. The time in between innings? I’m thinking about stuff. But when I’m out there, I want my process to be pretty simple.”
“If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.”
The quote is attributable to Isaac Newton in 1675, though it might be appropriated these days by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman. While the state of starting pitching declines—starters last postseason threw fewer innings than relievers and this regular season just 57% of innings—Friedman has assembled the most expensive rotation in postseason history, if not the most decorated. He did so by seizing from other teams six elite arms whose fastballs average between 95 and 98 mph.
Dodger Stadium, ever resplendent in its timeless mid-century vibe, is home to a style of pitching that also is a throwback. Los Angeles won the World Series last year by pulling from the catalog of Koufax and Drysdale. Dodgers starters threw 10 quality starts in the 2025 postseason, the most by a world champion since the 2010 Giants. Contrary to the prevailing bullpen-heavy approach, the Los Angeles starters won postseason games, not just managed them. They were 9–4 with a 2.68 ERA. Only the 1998 Yankees and 2007 Red Sox rotations won more games in this era of expanded postseasons. The rest of MLB postseason starters last year were 13–25.
The Los Angeles aces are back, and then some. To his Ocean’s Eleven of rotations—marquee-worthy names everywhere—Friedman on Aug. 1 added Skubal, the two-time defending American League Cy Young Award winner, in a heist of a trade with the Tigers. In a span of 32 months, through free agency and trades, Friedman acquired Shohei Ohtani, Tyler Glasnow, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Roki Sasaki and Skubal. They represent six regular-season and postseason MVP awards, four Cy Young Awards and $1.38 billion in salaries, or about what it cost to pay half the players in the majors in 2011.
In the Big Four of Skubal, Yamamoto, Snell and Ohtani, the Dodgers have acquired four of the five pitchers with the lowest ERA in baseball over the past four years (minimum 50 starts), with only the Pirates’ Paul Skenes having evaded their clutches. In their combined postseason careers, the Big Four are 18–8 with a 2.85 ERA.
As L.A. attempts to become the first team in National League history to win three straight World Series, the prevailing question of this postseason is not just, Can anybody beat the Dodgers? It is, Can anybody beat the Dodgers’ starters?
“For us it’s always been ideal to go into any October with the best starting pitching you can,” Friedman says. “If there are 150-plus starting pitchers with injuries, there are certainly not 30 number ones and an abundance of ones and twos. So, there’s scarcity there. This has been a perfect storm for us being able to access so many top-end talented arms in one moment in time.”
The Dodgers’ plan this postseason is a lather-rinse-repeat exercise of last October. They conserve innings from their starters in the regular season so they can turn them loose in the highest stakes games. When L.A. faced elimination in the World Series last year, for instance, down three games to two on the road to Toronto, manager Dave Roberts used seven pitchers over the final two games, all of whom started multiple times during the regular season. Game 7 was an embarrassment of riches. Roberts used six pitchers, including Ohtani, Glasnow, Snell and Yamamoto—$1.34 billion worth of pitchers in one game, with future Hall of Famer Clayton Kershaw warming in the bullpen. Yamamoto and Snell each threw more than 525 pitches in the postseason, the first pair of World Series–winning teammates to carry such a load since Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling for the 2001 Diamondbacks.
“The thought for me has never wavered,” Friedman says of building championship teams around starting pitching. “There is more appreciation for that now because there aren’t enough of those starters—the ones you can give the ball to and feel confident they will give you six or seven innings. It’s just important to be realistic with your personnel. In ’24, with the injuries to our starting pitching, our relievers were really good. The group was deep, and we leaned on our bullpen more. In ’25, our relievers were kind of going through it a little bit and our starters were rolling. And we leaned on that. I think it’s having an appreciation for what your strengths are going into October and doing the best you can to leverage it.”
The Dodgers are a modern dynasty. They are headed to a 13th straight full season with more than 90 wins. Twelve division titles in the past 13 years. Five of the past nine NL pennants. Three of the past six World Series titles. And yet before this season began Friedman, who took over as president of baseball ops in October 2014, called this the most talented team of them all. Privately, he yearned for one more player.
“We looked to do everything we could over the offseason to avoid being a buyer in July, short of a real impact-type talent,” he says. “And so, from our standpoint, our buy side list was Tarik Skubal. End of list.”
Detroit unwittingly cooperated. The Tigers went 6–22 in May, the second-worst May in franchise history. They played themselves into shopping Skubal, a free agent after the season, before the Aug. 3 deadline. President of baseball operations Scott Harris began exploratory talks with teams about Skubal in the week before the deadline. On July 31, Friedman says, “I went to sleep and I would have thought there was no chance that the deal would wrap the next day.”
The next morning, Harris and Friedman spoke again. Later in the afternoon, everything suddenly changed. Harris wanted final offers. He would present them to the Tigers’ ownership, and they would pick the winning bid within hours. According to one executive, the Dodgers sent signals they were in parallel discussions with the Mariners for pitcher George Kirby, a word on the street seen as a gambit to raise the pressure on Detroit. Friedman, however, denies that scenario. Skubal, he reiterates, was the only name on his shopping list. “If we were fortunate enough to wind up with him, great,” Friedman says. “If not, we weren’t out in the market looking for pitching.”
Friedman put three players in the package for Skubal, none of whom would hurt the Dodgers’ current and near-term plans: River Ryan, a soon-to-turn 28-year-old pitcher coming off Tommy John surgery; Double A outfielder Zyhir Hope, 21; and Class A pitcher Brady Smith, also 21. Harris accepted.
The package was a testament to the Dodgers’ treasure-hunting expertise, the secret sauce underneath their vast spending power. Ryan, a former 11th-round pick, was plucked from the Padres for Matt Beaty, a utility player and former 12th-round pick. Hope was another former 11th-round pick swiped from the Cubs when the Dodgers needed to move first baseman Michael Busch. Smith was the 95th player picked in the 2023 draft. The Dodgers turned straw into gold. And Skubal says he immediately felt comfortable changing teams for the first time, in this case to a franchise known for its abundant resources, including two team planes, one for players only.
“I mean, all the amenities are first class, you know?” he says. “All the recovery modalities, all the spaces they have, the way they treat the families, the family room ... I mean, they’re unreal.
“It’s awesome to be a part of something where the standard is winning a World Series. That’s the way everybody goes about their business, from ownership to president to GM to manager to players, and then you talk about support staff and the chefs in the kitchen, the flight attendants ... They all go out of their way to make sure you have everything you need to go out there and perform. I feel like everyone in this organization is rowing in the same direction and everybody wants a World Series just as bad as the players do.”
Says Friedman, “He has been awesome. He has seamlessly fit into the group. He has gone out of his way to try to forge relationships with teammates and staff. He is very convicted in his prep work, but also really curious.”
Skubal rocketed to an elite pitching level in 2023 with the help of a 3-D printer. The lefthander always had trouble mastering a changeup because his hand more easily supinates than pronates, meaning he lacked the natural forearm and wrist action that creates sink and fade by letting the baseball slip from his ring and pinkie fingers as the thumb turns down. Tigers pitching coaches Chris Fetter and Robin Lund introduced him to the concept of seam-shifted wake, the uneven airflow the raised seams create over a baseball. A pitcher without natural pronation can still deaden the baseball and create movement by harnessing these aerodynamics.
Lund, a former associate professor of kinesiology with a PhD in exercise science, had been hired that season from the University of Iowa. He had the Tigers use a 3-D printer to create a plastic mold that cradles half a baseball. The mold had a circular opening that let Lund draw a black dot with a Sharpie inside the horseshoe of the seams. “Keep the dot on top of the baseball,” he told Skubal, “and think about cutting across the face of the ball.”
When Skubal throws a baseball in that manner, the air catches the seams in a way that sinks and fades his changeup like a traditional changeup but without the pronation. Over the past four seasons, Skubal’s seam-shifted pitch ranks as the best changeup in baseball, according to Run Value among pitchers with at least 1,000 changeups. (Snell’s changeup is ranked No. 2.)
“Every once in a while, when I feel a little off, I’ll get it marked up and go right back to it,” Skubal says of the dotted training baseball. “But I haven’t done that in a while. It’s more just been about pitch execution, not pitch shape right now.”
The wonder of Skubal is that the game’s best changeup pitcher over those same four years also has the No. 3-ranked four-seam fastball among starting pitchers who have thrown at least 1,500 of that pitch. (Ohtani and Yamamoto rank Nos. 1 and 2.) With his natural supination, Skubal throws his fastball with a spin axis equivalent to the hour hand of a clock pointing to 11:15. “I throw a heater that’s not 100% efficient,” he says. “When it is 100% efficient, it’s actually a worse pitch. I need to cut it a little bit. I need to get like 94%, 92% efficiency because then I get more ride and a little bit more cut.”
Changeups and four-seamers account for 61% of his pitches. Sinkers, sliders and curveballs complete his arsenal, unless you include the adrenalin that makes him one of the most ferociously aggressive pitchers. Skubal has ranked first or second in first-pitch strike percentage two years running.
“The game is as analytic as ever,” he says. “You do want to get scouting reports and all that stuff. You can get as deep as you want, but for me it’s really about first-pitch strikes. It’s winning your 1–1 counts. It’s getting to two-strike counts as fast as possible because when you’re in those moments, you have the most leverage ever.
“When you get into two-strike counts, you should have all the confidence in the world. You’ve worked your ass off to get to this count. Now I’ve given myself room to get out of the zone a little bit. And sometimes I challenge guys in the zone, too, because when you get into count leverage, you have everything. Just execute a pitch, and the guy’s out.”
Skubal’s adrenalin-laced, pedal-to-the-floor style of pitching is well-suited for the postseason, in which he has made six career starts, all on the road and all with only two or three runs of support. Among the 219 pitchers who have made at least six starts in postseason history, Skubal ranks first in strikeouts per nine innings (12.7), second in WHIP (0.731) and third in hits per nine innings (5.2) and strikeouts per walk (9.33). His 2.04 postseason ERA is the lowest ever by a pitcher never to reach the World Series (minimum 35 innings).
“I love it,” he says of the postseason. “I feed off environments and energy and stadiums all in a positive way. The average velocity on the heater goes up. All the shapes kind of go up. The execution gets a little bit better, too.”
Come October, the calibrations that prepare him for the mound will not change. Skubal will stick to his mission-control like pre-launch routine:
• T-minus 150 minutes: Training room treatment with pulsed electromagnetic field therapy to relieve any soreness and stimulate blood flow.
• T-minus 120 minutes: Four shots of espresso. “That way,” he says, “I’m heavily caffeinated and ready to go.”
• T-minus 115 minutes: Hot tub followed by stretching and general body warmup.
• T-minus 60 minutes: Peanut butter and jelly sandwich. “Always Uncrustables,” he says. “[An] Uncrustable right to a toaster is the best thing in the world. They’re so convenient and they have them everywhere. And I know my stomach handles them well, so that’s why I eat them.”
• T-minus 40 minutes: Dynamic warmup to raise heart rate and body temperature.
• T-minus 30 minutes: Play catch.
• T-minus 20 minutes: Warm up on bullpen mound. “It always ends up being 17 to 22 pitches,” he says. “Seventeen to 22 throws is all it really takes for me.”
• T-minus eight minutes: Last bullpen pitch. Walk to dugout.
• T-minus one minute: A last reminder.
“The main thing that I remind myself in bigger moments is the game still stays the game,” he says. “The bigger the moment, the simpler the process needs to be. Just go do the things that make you great ... the first-pitch strikes, getting ahead, throwing strikes, getting into leverage, and getting these guys out early and often and putting them on their toes as much as you can. So, the bigger the game, the simpler my game gets on the mound.”
Skubal will stand on that plateau with his hands in front of his chest. The catcher will give him the radio-transmitted signal for the pitch. Skubal, who wears only the receiving device, not a transmitter, inevitably will agree. There is little mystery what is coming. Skubal threw a fastball on the first pitch of 153 of his 159 career starts through mid-August, postseason included.
With the ball in his glove, he will raise his hands in front of his face, peering over his mitt like a marksman through a sight. With a sidestep of his right leg, Skubal rocks his hands down to his belt. title: Shohei Ohtani’s Dodgers Jersey From His First MLB Game in Japan Is up for Auction
author: Rachel Cormack
body:
Shohei Ohtani is arguably the best baseball player of his generation, with the rare ability to pull double duty as a power hitter and an elite pitcher. In his seminal first year with the Los Angeles Dodgers, he became the first player in major league history to hit 50 home runs and steal 50 bases in a season. The Dodgers went on to win the 2024 World Series, with Shotime receiving his very first championship ring. At the beginning of 2025, he reached another milestone, playing his first official MLB game in his home country of Japan. The jersey he wore that day can now be yours.
The Realest is auctioning off Ohtani’s game-worn Dodgers jersey from the MLB Tokyo Series opener played at the Tokyo Dome on March 18, 2025. During the match, Ohtani scored two runs, leading the Dodgers to a 4-1 victory over the Chicago Cubs. It was a cracking start to a season in which he would win his fourth career MVP Award and the Dodgers would capture a second consecutive World Series championship.
“Ohtani’s career is already filled with milestones, and there are going to be many more, but he only gets one homecoming as a Major League Baseball player, and it landed in the prime of his career,” Scott Keeney, a.k.a. DJ Skee, founder and CEO of The Realest, told Robb Report. “It happened at the Tokyo Dome, in front of the country he represents, in what became the most-watched game in Japan, drawing a larger audience than any World Series game.”
Adding to the prestige is the fact that the jersey features the first Gold MLB Logoman patch ever worn in an official MLB game. It is also emblazoned with Ohtani’s signature—in kanji rather than English—along with his personal inscriptions “Opening Day Tokyo Series,” “GU 3-18-25,” and “NL MVP,” documenting the game, date, and game-used status.
“When you combine the significance of that homecoming with the first Gold Logoman he ever wore, the Tokyo Series patch, and his rare kanji signature, you have something that simply cannot be recreated,” adds Keeney. “From my perspective, this is the most important game-worn Ohtani jersey we’ve ever seen.”
The jersey is, of course, expected to fetch a pretty penny. Collectors have already shown they are willing to shell out for Ohtani memorabilia, with his shoes from this exact game and another jersey from the Tokyo Dome previously selling for $440,055 and $1.5 million, respectively. His 50-50 ball also sold for a record $4.39 million. The Realest didn’t give an exact estimate for the lot, but Keeney is expecting “a multimillion-dollar result that resets the modern-era record for a baseball jersey.”
The online auction has just kicked off, with bidding at a modest $15 at the time of writing. The sale will close on Saturday, October 17.

title: Exclusive | Inside Pawn Shop, the star-studded LA sports bar backed by Mark Cuban and Andrew Friedman
author: Michael Duarte
body:
Apparently, Mark Cuban and Andrew Friedman weren’t content conquering professional sports.
Now they’re coming for your neighborhood sports bar.
Tucked inside a sprawling 8,500-square-foot former pawn shop that dates back to the 1930s, L.A.’s newest reinvention on sports, luxury, and fine dining is born. Located on the corner of Melrose and Cahuenga sits Pawn Shop, a new restaurant and sports bar that features more than 60 televisions, two enormous media walls, private suites, and high-end cocktails galore.
Sign up for the California Morning Report newsletter
The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.
Thanks for signing up!
It’s led by founder and CEO Diego Torres-Palma and James Beard Award-winning chef Tony Messina. Together they’ve made the standard sports bar menu of chicken wings, nachos and mozzarella sticks look insulting by comparison.
A housemade wagyu hot dog, beef tallow fries, chicken liver mousse, caviar and charbroiled Maine oysters are just some of the menu’s highlights.
But the most interesting thing about Pawn Shop isn’t what’s on the walls or plates.
It’s who is behind it.
Billionaire entrepreneur and former Dallas Mavericks owner Mark Cuban is an investor. So is Dodgers’ president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman.
The list of names interested in either investing or being a part of the business is longer than a CVS receipt.
“We literally traded emails when Aaron announced he was coming back,” Torres-Palma said.
Donald isn’t the only Dodgers-or-Rams-adjacent star circling the new sports bar. Dodgers’ shortstop Mookie Betts met with the company and will now feature his Tequila Providencia behind the bar. Torres-Palma said Providencia’s CEO Rodd Rafieha’s tequila impressed his beverage team enough to earn a place in the well.
Kendall Jenner’s 818 Tequila also wanted in on the fun.
“We’re excited to have 818 Tequila featured at Pawn Shop LA,” said Lanay Jacobs, President of 818 Tequila. “It’s a lively destination that brings together sports, cocktails, and community in a way our audience will love.”
Torres-Palma has other meetings set up with L.A. superstar athletes as well.
That collection of names helps explain why Pawn Shop has quickly become less a sports bar and more a hangout spot for athletes and celebrities alike.
Former NBA player Chandler Parsons, now the co-host of the online show “Run It Back,” makes a point to stop by at least once a week.
“Pawn Shop is exactly what LA needed,” he said. “Great food, great energy, amazing people, and a genuine love for sports that you can feel when you walk in.”
Sportscaster and radio host Rich Eisen recently held his fantasy football draft there. The entire LAFC team did the same. Actor Anthony Ramos has stopped by several times. Several entertainment executives have used the space, while nearby Paramount staffers have turned its private upstairs suites into off-site work rooms.
Cuban recently visited with his son and was in awe.
“Of all the investors, Mark is probably the one that I communicate with the most,” Torres-Palma said. “He’s so pumped. Honestly, he’s probably been our top supporter.”
The timing of Pawn Shop’s opening could hardly have been better.
It arrived during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, instantly giving an unknown sports bar the kind of crowds and atmosphere most restaurants spend years trying to manufacture.
Torres-Palma compares those first weeks to hosting a wedding every few days: hundreds of customers arriving together, watching the same event and wanting food and drinks at virtually the same moment.

title: Hit de Mookie resuelve a favor de los Dodgers el juego y la serie en San Diego - AGP Noticias
author: AGP Noticias
body:
San Diego, California.- Freddie Freeman consiguió una base por bolas con las bases llenas que rompió el empate ante un Michael King repentinamente descontrolado en la quinta entrada, y Mookie Betts le siguió con un sencillo de dos carreras para los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, que vencieron a los Padres de San Diego 4-2 el domingo para ganar dos de tres partidos.
Los Dodgers, bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial y con el mejor récord del béisbol (54-30), extendieron su ventaja a 10 juegos sobre los Padres en la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Los equipos volverán a enfrentarse de jueves a domingo en el Dodger Stadium.
Manny Machado conectó un jonrón ante Emmet Sheehan con un out en la cuarta entrada para empatar el partido a 1. Fue el 15º jonrón de la temporada para Machado.
King, quien permitió el sencillo productor de Shohei Ohtani al jardín izquierdo con un out en la tercera entrada, se metió en problemas inmediatamente en la quinta cuando otorgó una base por bolas al primer bateador, Alex Freeland. Logró que Chuckie Robinson bateara un elevado, pero permitió que los siguientes cuatro bateadores llegaran a base.
Ohtani recibió base por bolas y Andy Pages fue golpeado por un lanzamiento, llenando las bases. Freeman bateó tres fouls seguidos antes de recibir base por bolas en el noveno lanzamiento, impulsando a Freeland. Betts conectó un sencillo al jardín central, trayendo a Ohtani y Pages al plato para poner el marcador 4-1 y sacar a King del juego.
Betts conectó un jonrón de tres carreras en la sexta entrada, en la que anotaron nueve carreras, en la victoria del sábado por la noche por 15-3.
King (5-7) venía de una victoria por 1-0 contra Atlanta el lunes por la noche. Antes de eso, no había ganado desde que derrotó a los Dodgers por 1-0 en casa el 18 de mayo. Los Dodgers, tras una derrota en el primer partido de la serie, consiguieron dos victorias en cada una de sus dos series en San Diego esta temporada.
Sheehan (4-5) se recuperó tras perder sus últimas cuatro aperturas. Limitó a los Padres a una carrera y dos hits en cinco entradas, ponchó a cinco y otorgó dos bases por bolas.
Edgardo Henríquez lanzó la novena entrada para conseguir su primer salvamento.
A continuación
El lanzador zurdo de los Dodgers, Eric Lauer (3-5, 4.87 ERA), se enfrentará al lanzador zurdo de los Athletics, Gage Jump (3-1, 2.04), en Sacramento el lunes por la noche.
Los Padres no han anunciado al lanzador abridor para el partido del lunes por la noche contra los Cachorros de Chicago.
Información: AP.

El lanzador zurdo de los Dodgers, Eric Lauer (3-5, 4.87 ERA), se enfrentará al lanzador zurdo de los Athletics, Gage Jump (3-1, 2.04), en Sacramento el lunes por la noche.

title: Mookie Betts, inactivo por lesión - AGP Noticias
author: AGP Noticias
body:
Washington, D.C.- Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles colocaron al campocorto Mookie Betts en la lista de lesionados el domingo debido a una distensión en el oblicuo derecho y llamaron a Hyeseong Kim de la filial Triple-A de Oklahoma City.
Betts abandonó el partido del sábado, en el que los Dodgers ganaron 10-5 a los Nacionales de Washington, tras recibir una base por bolas y anotar una carrera en la primera entrada. El mánager Dave Roberts declaró que los Dodgers creen que Betts se lesionó inicialmente al intentar un swing incompleto durante su turno al bate.
Aunque Roberts dijo que dudaba en fijar un plazo para el regreso de Betts, espera que sea más rápido que una ausencia de 4 a 6 semanas.
“En realidad está de mejor humor”, dijo Roberts. “Obviamente está decepcionado, pero por cómo se siente hoy, creo que ya ha pasado por algo similar antes y dice que es mejor de lo que recuerda de experiencias pasadas, así que eso es alentador”.
Betts tiene un promedio de bateo de .179 en los primeros ocho partidos de Los Ángeles. El jugador de 33 años bateó .258 con 20 jonrones y 82 carreras impulsadas en 150 partidos la temporada pasada.
Kim bateó .280 con tres jonrones y 17 carreras impulsadas en 71 juegos como novato la temporada pasada.
Roberts indicó que Kim y Miguel Rojas probablemente se repartirán el tiempo en el campocorto mientras Betts esté ausente. Rojas reemplazó a Betts en el partido del sábado y bateará de segundo el domingo contra los Nacionales. Roberts añadió que es probable que Kim sea titular en dos de los tres partidos de la serie de los Dodgers en Toronto, que comienza el lunes.
La alineación de los Dodgers también presentará cambios. Betts bateó en el tercer puesto en todos los partidos de esta temporada, después de haber bateado segundo durante gran parte del año pasado.
“Es Mookie Betts, así que sin duda cambia las cosas”, dijo Roberts. “Pero esa es la gran ventaja de tener profundidad en el equipo, algo que muchos equipos no tienen. Un sistema de rotación en el campocorto, donde sientes que tienes buenos emparejamientos, no es del todo malo y les da oportunidades a otros jugadores. Pero es un golpe, sin duda”.
Información: AP.

title: Dodgers news: Blake Treinen dismisses 'magic number' talk after loss to Reds
author: Matty Breisch; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Blake Treinen dismisses 'magic number' talk after loss to Reds appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Heading into Wednesday night's game against the Cincinnati Reds, the "magic number" for the Los Angeles Dodgers was one, with either their own win or a San Diego Padres loss punching their ticket to another NL West pennant.
Unfortunately, that didn't happen, as after Blake Snell's start was limited to one inning, the Dodgers lost 6-2, and the Padres put a whopping on the Colorado Rockies, 9-3. But how much do the players actually care about "magic numbers" and when pennant milestones are reached? Well, according to reliever Blake Treinen, they don't at all, as he told reporters after the loss.
"I honestly have zero idea where our magic number is until you said that. I haven't had a chance to follow it. I know we're really focused on getting the best version of ourselves right now. So, to highlight your assumption of whether we're struggling with back and forth or is it on our minds, I don't think it's on our minds. I haven't seen it," Treinen revealed.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"There's been years in the past where it's come down to the wire, I think, in '24 against the Padres, you start wondering, is this going to click, and we're going to have an opportunity to win a division? Right now, I think we're just focused on being the best version of ourselves. We've worked really hard to be in a good position to win the division. That'll come when it comes, and I think we're just doing our best to fine-tune as much as we can, myself included."
Now granted, maybe Treinen is just downplaying things because he's the veteran in the clubhouse, and wants to set a good example for his younger teammates. Or maybe the Dodgers simply know they have a morning game to close out their Reds series and don't want to get too ahead of themselves down the stretch? Either way, the Dodgers have a chance to do it again on Thursday and turn their attention to the next "magic number," seven, which is how many wins they need to clinch a Wild Card round bye.
Related: Dodgers' nightmare seeding, matchup scenarios for 2026 MLB Playoffs

title: Dodgers news: Dave Roberts' plan for bullpen game vs. Reds after Blake Snell injury
author: Josh Davis; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Dave Roberts' plan for bullpen game vs. Reds after Blake Snell injury appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers will turn to Justin Wrobleski and Landon Knack for the bulk of Thursday's series finale vs. the Cincinnati Reds after Blake Snell's early exit Wednesday night.
Wrobleski will start at Great American Ball Park, while Knack will return to the active roster and follow him as Los Angeles navigates its pitching depth. The Dodgers will option Bobby Miller to Triple-A Oklahoma City in the corresponding move after he worked 2 1/3 innings Wednesday.
The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya took to X, formerly Twitter, relaying manager Dave Roberts' pitching plan as the Dodgers adjust following Snell's unexpected departure with left groin tightness.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Justin Wrobleski will start and he and Landon Knack will take the bulk of the game tomorrow. Bobby Miller is being optioned for Knack, Dave Roberts said."
Snell felt his groin "grab" during his pregame bullpen Wednesday but still made his scheduled start. The two-time Cy Young winner threw one scoreless inning on 19 pitches before the Dodgers removed him as a precaution.
His departure forced the Dodgers to use six relievers over the final seven innings in their 6-2 loss. Miller accounted for 2 1/3 of those frames after the club recalled him Monday when Edgardo Henriquez went on the injured list.
Wrobleski, meanwhile, has pitched out of the bullpen since returning from a left forearm injury on September 1. The 2026 MLB All-Star was already on the active roster, while Knack was with the Reds as organizational pitching depth ahead of his recall.
Los Angeles is 92-60 after Wednesday's loss. The San Diego Padres' 9-3 win over the Colorado Rockies kept the Dodgers from clinching the NL West that night and left the magic number at one. A victory Thursday against the Reds, or a Padres loss, would give the Dodgers their fifth consecutive division crown.

title: Blake Snell sale tras la primera entrada en juego de Dodgers ante Rojos por rigidez en la ingle
author: Associated Press Spanish
body:
CINCINNATI (AP) — El zurdo de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Blake Snell, abandonó su apertura la noche del miércoles contra los Rojos de Cincinnati después de una entrada debido a rigidez en la ingle izquierda.
“Me sentí bien todo el día (y luego) en el penúltimo lanzamiento del bullpen, (sentí) un tirón”, dijo Snell. “Hice un lanzamiento más, luego corrí hacia el dugout. Estuve como hablándome a mí mismo durante toda esa primera entrada. Iba a intentar llegar a cinco, pero realmente no tenía muchas posibilidades de hacerlo”.
Snell permitió un sencillo a Sal Stewart y ponchó a un bateador en la primera entrada. Stewart fue sorprendido fuera de base para terminar la entrada. Snell realizó 19 lanzamientos, 10 en zona de strike antes de abandonar el juego.
Snell (4-1, 1.86 de efectividad) comenzó la temporada en la lista de lesionados por una inflamación en el hombro izquierdo. Se sometió a una cirugía en mayo para retirar cuerpos sueltos y espolones óseos del codo izquierdo.
Ha tenido problemas en la ingle en el pasado. En 2021, pasó tiempo en la lista de lesionados por una distensión del aductor izquierdo, se perdió casi un mes en 2022 y tuvo una estadía en la lista de lesionados en 2024 debido a distensiones en la ingle .
“No se siente tan grave como las veces que hemos lidiado con esto en el pasado”, dijo Snell. “Seguí lanzando en dos de ellas y me distendí ambas. Así que para mí parar, eso es una primera vez” .
Snell dijo que le gustaría tener una apertura más en la temporada regular.
“Obviamente, contento de que nos lo avisara temprano para sacarlo del juego, no empeorarlo”, dijo el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts. “Creo que lo primero es que veremos cómo amanece mañana, cómo se siente, darle más tratamiento. Cuando regresemos a LA entonces podemos tomar esa decisión”.
Los Dodgers utilizaron seis relevistas después de que Snell salió en la derrota 6-2 ante los Rojos que les impidió asegurar el título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. Ya aseguraron su 14ta clasificación consecutiva a la postemporada.
___

title: Kyle Tucker, Dodgers eager to add to Marlins' misery
body:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Kyle Tucker may be getting hot just in time for the playoffs.
The National League West-leading Dodgers (90-57) will look to extend their winning streak to nine games when they visit the Miami Marlins (72-76) on Saturday. The Marlins, in turn, have lost seven of their past eight games.
Tucker went 3-for-3 with a season-high five RBIs in Los Angeles’ 6-2 victory over Miami on Friday. He fell a double short of the cycle.
Entering Friday, Tucker was on pace for his fourth straight month with an OPS at or below .700, and that’s not what the Dodgers thought they were getting when they signed him to a four-year, $240 million contract in January.
Tucker, who has posted OPS numbers of .993 and .841 over the past two years, impressed Marlins manager Clayton McCullough with his performance on Friday.
“Independent of how this season has gone, (Tucker) is still a terrific hitter,” McCullough said. “He handles lefties well. He got a hanging breaking ball and turned the game for them.”
Tucker produced five straight seasons with more than 20 homers before mustering just 14 in 2026. But if he can finish strong, that will help a Dodgers squad that is missing injured sluggers Shohei Ohtani (right biceps inflammation), Freddie Freeman (right knee) and Andy Pages (left hand). Those three players have hit a combined 67 homers this season.
Los Angeles also saw Josue De Paula make his MLB debut on Friday. De Paula went 0-for-3 with a walk after tearing up Double-A pitching.
“We want to get him some major-league at-bats to see what it looks like,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
The Dodgers will turn to right-hander Tyler Glasnow (4-0, 3.12 ERA) to make the start on Saturday.
His per-nine-innings averages are outstanding in terms of hits allowed (5.3), walks (2.7) and strikeouts (10.9). The Dodgers are 8-2 when he starts, and this will be his fourth start since coming back from a near-three-month injury absence.
Glasnow is 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA in five career starts versus the Marlins.
Miami will counter with right-hander Tyler Phillips (5-6, 3.51), who is 1-0 with a 6.94 ERA in six career appearances (one start) against the Dodgers.
For his career overall, Phillips has a sterling 2.49 ERA in 71 relief appearances, but a 5.13 ERA in 25 career starts.
As for Miami’s offense, the Marlins are hoping that shortstop Otto Lopez is back on track after a 4-for-5 performance on Friday.
This year, Lopez hit .322 in March/April; .339 in May; and .340 in June. That hot start made him a first-time All-Star. However, he batted .284 in July and just .236 in August.
Thanks to Friday’s big game, he is now hitting .342 in September.
“After the phenomenal first half, he struggled for a bit,” McCullough said. “He looks to be back in a good spot, hitting the ball to all fields. It’s something we have grown accustomed to, and it bodes well for us to have him get hits in bunches.”
–Field Level Media

title: Blake Snell exits Dodgers' loss early because of injury
author: Maddie Lee
body:
Blake Snell exits Dodgers’ loss early because of injury
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
CINCINNATI — The trouble started as Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell threw in the Great American Ball Park bullpen before the game.
“I felt good all day, and then the second-to-last pitch of the bullpen, I threw a slider and then I felt it grab,” Snell said of the groin tightness that ended up taking him out of the Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Reds early. “So I was like, ‘Alright, let’s see what we can do.’”
With Snell guiding the ball without driving hard off his back leg, his velocity was down a tick or two through a 19-pitch first inning. He gave up one hit, a single to Sal Stewart, which he quickly erased with a successful pick-off that caught Stewart in an inning-ending run-down.
“I was going to try to get through five [innings],” he said, “but I just knew I didn’t really have a good shot at doing that and remaining healthy.”
In a conversation with manager Dave Roberts, pitching coach Mark Prior and head athletic trainer Thomas Albert, they all agreed the best course of action would be to pull Snell from the game. Right-handed reliever Blake Treinen replaced him in the second inning.
With only 10 games left in the season, it’s unclear when Snell will be ready to pitch again.
“The next couple days are really going to decide,” Snell said. “But I’d love to throw on my next [scheduled start day]. Either there or a couple days after. But definitely, I want to try to get one more in the regular season.”
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
The Dodgers’ loss marked Snell’s eighth start of the season. His 2026 debut was delayed by shoulder fatigue. And then after one start, he landed back on the injured list to undergo arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow.
Since returning, he hasn’t given up more than one run in a start. Through Wednesday, Snell has a 1.86 ERA. And he’s a key member of the Dodgers’ projected postseason rotation.
“I don’t think anyone can sit here right now and say what’s going to happen in the next week to 10 days,” Roberts said, noting that the team would decide whether to send him to get imaging after they returned to Los Angeles. “It’s under the, ‘I’m glad it’s not worse and we caught it early’ [category].”
Snell has a history of left groin and adductor strains. He spent time on the IL in 2021, 2022 and 2024 for such injuries. He said this injury didn’t feel nearly as severe as any of those.
“[In the past] I felt like that and then I kept pitching on two of them and strained both of them,” he said. “One was a grade one, one was a grade two. So I’m definitely happy I stopped. … I’m aware if I kept pitching, I definitely would’ve strained it. So for me to stop, that’s a first. Maybe I’m growing up. I don’t know. But that was definitely the right move. And next couple days, we’ll see where we’re at and go from there. But I think I’ll be good to go.”
The last couple years, in an effort to avoid another groin strain, Snell has incorporated Copenhagen planks into his routine, strengthening the area.
“I thought I had this thing figured out,” Snell said. “Well, technically, I still do. I didn’t strain it, so that was a good thing. … I haven’t felt it at all until that pitch in the bullpen, and I was just kind of thrown off by it. So I’ve done what I’ve needed to do to be strong and healthy. Definitely a shock to me.”
After Snell left the game, the Dodgers used six relievers to get through seven innings. They combined to give up six runs and 12 hits, including a pair of home runs.
Left-hander Kris Bubic, acquired at the trade deadline while on the IL (flexor strain, shoulder impingement), made his Dodgers debut in the eighth inning. In his first major-league appearance since mid-May, he allowed an infield single and recorded two strikeouts in a scoreless inning.
The Dodgers missed a chance to clinch the division with a win. And the Padres beat the Rockies on Wednesday to keep the division race mathematically alive.
So, the Dodgers will get another shot at champagne showers in Cincinnati Wednesday when left-hander Justin Wrobleski takes the mound. The Dodgers optioned right-hander Bobby Miller after his 2 ⅓ innings Wednesday and plan to recall righty Landon Knack, Roberts said.
The Dodgers’ pitching plans for the next couple weeks are in flux.
Though right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and left-hander Tarik Skubal have been rounding into the best versions of themselves down the stretch, Snell’s injury is the latest to deplete the ranks.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) has been on the IL for almost three weeks. He threw a four-inning, 48-pitch live batting practice session Wednesday, with Dermabond covering the sensitive area on his finger.
The Dodgers had planned to discuss how to deploy him when he returns from the IL, but after the game, Roberts said to “make sure guys have ample rest,” his next outing will be a start.
Sasaki would be lined up to pitch against the Padres next week.
“It’s playable,” manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s blister. “And given the Dermabond, the time that he’ll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it’s dang near close to being healed.”
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow hit a rough patch in his last two starts but said his back, which sidelined him for three and a half months, “feels good.” The Dodgers sent him back to Los Angeles after the series in Miami to cut down on the number of flights he’d have to sit on before his scheduled start Friday.
“Get him home, get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time, not have to do two legs,” Roberts said. “So Tyler feels great. He’ll be ready to go on Friday.”
Roberts reiterated after the game that he’s “not concerned with Tyler,” who came out of a bullpen session Wednesday feeling “normal.”
If the Dodgers need another spot start in the next week and a half, they have right-hander Emmet Sheehan waiting in the wings. They optioned him to triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday, in favor of an extra reliever. But over his last two major-league starts, he’s limited opponents to one run and five hits in 11 ⅔ innings.

After Snell left the game, the Dodgers used six relievers to get through seven innings. They combined to give up six runs and 12 hits, including a pair of home runs.
Left-hander Kris Bubic, acquired at the trade deadline while on the IL (flexor strain, shoulder impingement), made his Dodgers debut in the eighth inning. In his first major-league appearance since mid-May, he allowed an infield single and recorded two strikeouts in a scoreless inning.
The Dodgers missed a chance to clinch the division with a win. And the Padres beat the Rockies on Wednesday to keep the division race mathematically alive.
So, the Dodgers will get another shot at champagne showers in Cincinnati Wednesday when left-hander Justin Wrobleski takes the mound. The Dodgers optioned right-hander Bobby Miller after his 2 ⅓ innings Wednesday and plan to recall righty Landon Knack, Roberts said.
The Dodgers’ pitching plans for the next couple weeks are in flux.
Though right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and left-hander Tarik Skubal have been rounding into the best versions of themselves down the stretch, Snell’s injury is the latest to deplete the ranks.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) has been on the IL for almost three weeks. He threw a four-inning, 48-pitch live batting practice session Wednesday, with Dermabond covering the sensitive area on his finger.
The Dodgers had planned to discuss how to deploy him when he returns from the IL, but after the game, Roberts said to “make sure guys have ample rest,” his next outing will be a start.
Sasaki would be lined up to pitch against the Padres next week.
“It’s playable,” manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s blister. “And given the Dermabond, the time that he’ll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it’s dang near close to being healed.”
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow hit a rough patch in his last two starts but said his back, which sidelined him for three and a half months, “feels good.” The Dodgers sent him back to Los Angeles after the series in Miami to cut down on the number of flights he’d have to sit on before his scheduled start Friday.
“Get him home, get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time, not have to do two legs,” Roberts said. “So Tyler feels great. He’ll be ready to go on Friday.”
Roberts reiterated after the game that he’s “not concerned with Tyler,” who came out of a bullpen session Wednesday feeling “normal.”
If the Dodgers need another spot start in the next week and a half, they have right-hander Emmet Sheehan waiting in the wings. They optioned him to triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday, in favor of an extra reliever. But over his last two major-league starts, he’s limited opponents to one run and five hits in 11 ⅔ innings.

title: Dodgers Quietly Announce Huge Dalton Rushing News
author: Simeon Kotto
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers spent Wednesday in Cincinnati wrapping up the middle of a three-game set with the Reds after taking the first two contests, including a 4-0 win on Tuesday.
While the club kept winning on the field, the bigger news coming out of the series was an update on catcher Dalton Rushing, who has been sidelined since September 5.
According to an MLB.com report on Wednesday, Rushing is working through a hitting progression.
He will not catch again this season, but he could still return as a designated hitter or other non-catching role before the regular season ends.
That possibility leaves the door open for a late-September appearance, though the Dodgers have not put a firm date on his activation.
Before the injury, Rushing had given Los Angeles a productive stretch in his second major-league season. In 78 games he hit .249 with 55 hits, 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and 37 runs scored.
Selected by the Dodgers in the second round of the 2022 draft, he is still only 25 and will turn 26 in February. Last year he also appeared in one postseason game, giving him a small but real taste of October baseball.
Rushing’s absence has been felt behind the plate, yet the Dodgers have continued to roll.
They sit first in the National League West at 92-59 through 151 games and are chasing a third straight World Series title after winning the last two.
The roster depth that has defined the franchise in recent years has allowed them to absorb the loss of a young catcher without falling out of first place.
Thursday afternoon brings the series finale against Cincinnati before the Dodgers fly home to open a weekend series with the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Whether Rushing can contribute as a bat-only option in those final weeks remains an open question, but the latest update at least confirms he is progressing at the plate and has not been ruled out for the remainder of the regular season.
For a club built to win now and later, even a limited return from a 25-year-old who already has 12 homers this year would be a welcome addition as the calendar turns toward October.
The Dodgers have shown they can win without him. Getting him back in some capacity would only add another layer to a lineup that has already carried them to the top of the division.

title: Tarik Skubal and the 2026 Mariners would have been wasted on each other
author: Paul Taylor
body:
So there you have it, it's official -- the Mariners have secured their first losing season since 2020, albeit that was a shortened COVID-impacted campaign of just 60 games. Irrespective, the 82 losses are their most since 2019 and based on current projections, they could finish with their second-most losses since 2013. With that wonderful benefit of hindsight, it now seems safe to proclaim they did the right thing in not pursuing Tarik Skubal ahead of the trade deadline.
To be clear, we total understand why there were suggestions from the likes of ESPN's Jeff Passan, that the Mariners should make a play for Skubal prior to the Aug. 3 deadline. He was perceived by many as the type of generational talent who could lift a rotation and by extension an entire team, even if he was going to effectively just be a two-month (or hopefully three) rental. And when the Dodgers acquired him, their return package for the Tigers had critics believing the M's missed the boat.
However, as asinine as it might initially seem to say this, we don't believe Skubal would have saved the Mariners' bacon this season. Sure they could have used the 2.52 ERA and 1.040 WHIP he's produced over eight starts for the Dodgers, but it still likely wouldn't have been enough for an M's team which has been in freefall since the last time they had a winning record. At that time in late-July they were 51-50 following a series-opening win versus the Reds, but have since gone a disappointing 19-32.
Tarik Skubal just wouldn't have been able to do enough to save the Mariners from themselves
Even if you transfer the three wins Skubal has recorded with the Dodgers over to Seattle, the Mariners would still be just 73-79 and sitting four losses back of the Astros in the division as well as the final AL wild card spot, with just 10 games remaining. Some may want to contend you could also add the three games the Dodgers won even when he wasn't tagged with the W, but they were all tense one-run games. Do you really believe an M's bullpen which ranks dead last in team ERA since the beginning of August, would have come through for the team?
In that respect, the rotation hasn't been much better, ranking 24th in team ERA over the same time period. Throw in an offense which is third-worst in runs scored per game and last in Fielding Run Value, and it all would have just been too much for Skubal to overcome, regardless of being the two-time reigning AL Cy Young winner. Despite being capable of a galvanzing impact similar to Josh Naylor last season, even this alone would have been compromised to an extent by only pitching once every five days.
The other reason trading for Skubal would have been a pure waste is the acquisition cost. As much as people believe the Dodgers got a favorable deal with the Tigers to get the southpaw, they still had to give up two top-100 prospects. Clearly the M's could have blown the Dodgers out of the water with a superior return package, but you would probably be looking at the likes of Lazaro Montes and Felnin Celesten, which even at the time would have felt like a gut punch of sorts, never mind now.
Even for Skubal himself, a trade to Seattle would have been a waste, if for no other reason than he wouldn't have gotten a chance to pad his free agent value in the playoffs. Look, we get it that plenty of Mariners fans wish the front office would be more adventurous and take risks like other teams such as the Dodgers, and Yankees. However, as bad as this season has been -- and it has been truly awful -- it would have been worse with such a big swing and miss.

author: Jgiesler
body:
By Field Level Media Sep 17 (Field Level Media) – Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell was removed from Wednesday’s game in Cincinnati after one inning and replaced with reliever Blake Treinen. The Dodgers announced that Snell left the game due to left groin tightness. Snell struck out Dane Myers to open the bottom […]
Sports
Dodgers LHP Blake Snell (groin) removed from start after 1st inning
By Field Level Media
Sep 17 (Field Level Media) – Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell was removed from Wednesday’s game in Cincinnati after one inning and replaced with reliever Blake Treinen.
The Dodgers announced that Snell left the game due to left groin tightness.
Snell struck out Dane Myers to open the bottom of the first and Elly De La Cruz lined out to center before Sal Stewart singled to left. It was the first hit Snell had allowed at Great American Ball Park since he threw a no-hitter there on Aug. 2, 2024, in a 3-0 win for the San Francisco Giants.
The left-hander then caught Stewart leaning from first base and the Reds’ runner was caught stealing to end the first inning. Treinen came on to replace Snell to start the second.
Snell had arthroscopic surgery in May to remove loose bodies in his left elbow and returned in August. He has been one of the hottest pitchers in baseball since, going 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA with 46 strikeouts in his last six starts entering Wednesday.
(–Field Level Media)

title: Dodgers’ Roki Sasaki throws simulated game – but what role awaits him?
author: Bill Plunkett
body:
CINCINNATI — Now what?
Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in four simulated innings to Dodgers hitters on Wednesday afternoon, testing the blister on his right hand that landed him on the injured list. He gave up a home run to Eliezer Alfonzo but otherwise “was good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Sasaki threw with Dermabond on his injured finger. A surgical adhesive used to close cuts and incisions, pitchers are allowed to use it in games if their team gets permission from MLB in advance.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. What does it look like as we sit here on the 17th or 18th of September, whatever? So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
Sasaki seemed destined for a bullpen role again this postseason, a role he assumed successfully last year. But the Dodgers have reason to hesitate on turning Sasaki into a reliever with Blake Snell leaving his start after just one inning on Wednesday night and Tyler Glasnow’s status.
Glasnow flew back to Los Angeles after his start in Miami. It was the second consecutive start in which Glasnow was not sharp and this time he could be seen in the dugout stretching out his back. But after the game, he said his back felt fine and Roberts said Glasnow threw a “normal” bullpen session in L.A. on Wednesday and is scheduled to make his next start on Friday night.
Sasaki is penciled in now to start during the series against the San Diego Padres in Los Angeles next week and remain a starter at least for now.
“One can argue it’s best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up, because if something does happen, he’s built up,” Roberts said. “The other side is you can assimilate him into the ’pen and get comfortable in that role – if that is the role.
“But again, I don’t want to speak out of turn and say that’s done, because it’s not.”
NO SHO
The Dodgers are about to complete their first road trip in three seasons without Shohei Ohtani. Yoshinobu Yamamoto might have missed Ohtani more than any other of his teammates.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yamamoto joked through his interpreter when asked about Ohtani’s absence. “All I have is Roki, but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Back in Los Angeles, Ohtani has been receiving treatment for his knee and bicep injuries. According to Roberts, Ohtani began swinging a bat, hitting off a tee this week.
“There’s going to be a consistent build-up,” Roberts said. “Don’t know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive, and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”
Ohtani will be eligible to be activated from the IL next Wednesday. Whether he is ready to play that day or shortly after, Roberts said the expectation is that Ohtani will return in time to play before the regular season ends on Sept. 27.
“I do,” Roberts said. “Whether it happens or not is to be determined. But I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games. Don’t know how many of them.”
COMING/GOING
Right-hander Edwin Diaz made his fifth rehab appearance with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless inning to close out the Comets’ playoff berth-clinching victory. Diaz did allow a double to a fellow big-leaguer on rehab, Miguel Andujar.
Meanwhile, Edgardo Henriquez returned to Los Angeles and underwent an MRI, which confirmed the diagnosis of a “low-grade back strain,” Roberts said. He won’t be eligible to pitch again in the regular season but Roberts said the Dodgers are “hopeful” he could come back for the postseason.
Left-hander Kris Bubic was activated from the 60-day IL before Wednesday’s game and right-hander Paul Gervase was returned to OKC. In order to clear a spot on the 40-man roster for Bubic, Triple-A outfielder Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Right-hander Landon Knack will be added to the active roster before Thursday’s game and Bobby Miller will be returned to OKC.
ALSO
Outfield prospect Charles Davalan (the 41st pick in last year’s draft) was named MVP of the Class-A Midwest League and Great Lakes manager Jair Fernandez was named the league’s Manager of the Year. Davalan hit .292 with 24 home runs and a .937 OPS. He is scheduled to play in the Arizona Fall League, where he is expected to start testing out a possible conversion to second base.
UP NEXT
Dodgers (LHP Justin Wrobleski, 11-5, 3.78 ERA) at Reds (RHP Brady Singer, 6-14, 5.38 ERA), Thursday, 9:40 a.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

Outfield prospect Charles Davalan (the 41st pick in last year’s draft) was named MVP of the Class-A Midwest League and Great Lakes manager Jair Fernandez was named the league’s Manager of the Year.
