title: Dodgers’ Mookie Betts Announces Personal News After Securing Post-Season Berth
author: Dibyendu Mondal
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts is producing a new movie. On Monday, he announced the project away from the field. He's producing a movie titled "Cannon Street All-Stars."
Los Angeles clinched a playoff berth the same day, beating the Cincinnati Reds 4-1. The win pushed them to 91-59 with 12 games left. It marks the Dodgers' 14th straight postseason appearance.
However, Betts did little to contribute to that win. He went 0-for-4. No hits, home runs or RBIs.
He is having a down year by his standards.
Betts is batting .248 with 20 home runs, 62 RBIs and 108 hits this season. His career average sits at .288. Betts won AL MVP in 2018 and has made eight All-Star teams.
Off the diamond, however, he is excelling in his projects.
More on Mookie Betts' Latest Project
Betts is producing the film alongside Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry, Deadline reported in an exclusive Monday.
Director Reggie Rock Bythewood and his wife, Gina Prince-Bythewood, are developing the project through their company, Undisputed Cinema. Bythewood will write and direct.
The film tells the true story of the Cannon Street YMCA All-Stars. The all-Black Little League team from Charleston, South Carolina, tried to enter the 1955 state tournament.
Little League baseball in the South remained segregated at the time, eight years after Jackie Robinson broke MLB's color line. The team's push sparked forfeits and national attention. The Jackie Robinson Foundation backs the project.
Bythewood called the film overdue recognition. Surviving players were honored at last year's Little League World Series. "Now it is time to honor them on film," Bythewood said.

Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman Latest Updates
Despite clinching the postseason, few key pieces remain uncertain.
Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day injured list with left knee and right biceps issues. He landed there Sept. 11.
Manager Dave Roberts said Monday that Ohtani could begin swinging off a tee as early as this week. The Dodgers expect Ohtani back as a hitter in late September. He won't pitch again this season. Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs this year.
Freddie Freeman sat out Monday's game to rest a sore right knee, described as patellar tendinitis. The team does not plan to place him on the injured list. Freeman is expected back in the lineup Tuesday.

title: Dodgers celebran 14to pase seguido a los playoffs con discreto brindis e igualan récord
author: JOE REEDY
body:
Dodgers celebran 14to pase seguido a los playoffs con discreto brindis e igualan récord
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles celebraron su 14ta clasificación consecutiva a la postemporada de las Grandes Ligas, para igualar un récord, con un brindis de champán tras la victoria del lunes por la noche por 4-1 sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati.
Las celebraciones más grandes llegarán después.
“Es difícil decir que alguna vez se sienta rutinario, pero esa es la expectativa aquí. Siempre me río cuando aseguramos un lugar en la postemporada: simplemente hacemos un brindis pequeño y agradable”, dijo el tercera base Max Muncy. “Los muchachos que no han estado aquí ven eso y esperan un poco más. Eso pasa cuando aseguras la división”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial, que se unieron a Milwaukee y Tampa Bay como equipos que ya aseguraron un lugar en los playoffs, redujeron su número mágico a tres para un quinto título consecutivo del Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en 14 temporadas.
Los Ángeles igualó la racha de postemporadas de los Bravos de Atlanta de 1991 a 2005. Los Bravos alcanzaron cinco veces a la Serie Mundial durante ese lapso, pero la única vez que se consagraron fue en 1995.
“Por suerte lo estamos haciendo un poco mejor que eso”, dijo Muncy sobre los tres títulos de los Dodgers y sus cinco participaciones en el Clásico de Otoño durante esta racha.
Tarik Skubal —quien lanzó siete entradas sin permitir carreras y concedió apenas tres hits— señaló que la manera en que los Dodgers manejaron el hecho de asegurar un lugar en la postemporada fue definitivamente distinta en comparación con las situaciones de clasificación que vivió las dos temporadas anteriores con Detroit.
“Creo que eso habla de la gente que está en este vestuario y de lo que esperan de este equipo. Eso estuvo genial. Un pequeño brindis y a seguir. Olvidar que pasó. Tenemos más por lograr esta temporada”, expresó.
Dave Roberts, quien cumple su 11ma temporada como mánager, dijo que su mensaje durante el brindis fue que los Dodgers han logrado mucho hasta este punto, pero aún no se han acercado a jugar su mejor béisbol.
“Cada año pasan muchos jugadores por aquí, y los muchachos encuentran la manera de dar un paso al frente, y eso es de lo que probablemente me siento más orgulloso: la consistencia de ganar a largo plazo. Cualquier equipo, cualquier organización puede ganar en un año determinado cuando las cosas se alinean, pero hacerlo todos los años, cuando se espera que lo hagas, dice algo sobre toda la organización”, dijo Roberts.
Los Dodgers (91-59) actualmente son el segundo sembrado en la Liga Nacional. Están dos juegos y medio por delante de Atlanta y están dos juegos detrás de Milwaukee por el primer puesto.
Un pase directo en la primera ronda es importante en cualquier momento, pero especialmente este año para los Dodgers, que no están a plena capacidad. El primera base Freddie Freeman arrastra molestias en la rodilla derecha y Shohei Ohtani, dos veces Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Nacional, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en términos de salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, dijo Roberts antes del juego del lunes.
___

title: Dodger notes: Edwin Diaz and the state of the pitching staff
author: Andy Lane Chapman
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made Edwin Diaz the highest paid closer over the offseason. Now, he might not even make the postseason roster.
Diaz had a rehab outing Sunday in which he faced eight batters, retiring only two while walking three and hitting a batter. He threw 30 pitches to get those two outs, with only 13 strikes. Manager Dave Roberts talked about his recent woes on Monday before the Dodgers game against the Cincinnati Reds.
“He needs to pitch better. It hasn’t been good,” Roberts said on Monday. “He’s going to pitch on Wednesday, and I guess we’ll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well. So for me, Wednesday, we’ll be watching closely.”
He also acknowledged that Diaz might not make the postseason roster.
“Yeah … we have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff. So my bet is that he will be (one of them). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. My bet is yes, but we still have to see something.”
Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic has more on the terrible season overall that Diaz has had as a Dodger here.
The Dodgers are already down another reliever, at least for the rest of the regular season. Edgardo Henriquez went on the IL on Monday with lower back discomfort. Bobby Miller was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. Right-hander Paul Gervase and left-hander Kris Bubic also joined the team in Cincinnati. Gervase was added to the active roster, and Bubic could be added in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki has been sidelines with a blister and is tentatively scheduled to pitch on Thursday in Cincinnati. However, the weather is supposed to be hot and humid, and the team is worried about how that will affect Sasaki’s blister.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward. And so obviously people can look at Thursday. But again, if he can’t do it without accomplishing it, finishing a start, and not regress, then it’s not worth it. So I think for us, we’re just keeping it open-ended right now.”

title: Dodgers' Tarik Skubal looks to duplicate recent outing vs. Reds
body:
The two-time reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers are closing in on the National League West title and still have their sights on the NL’s top seed.
Despite the positives, the Dodgers are limping into the opener of a three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Monday.
Los Angeles (90-59) enters play having dropped two straight against the Miami Marlins, including a 6-4 loss on Sunday that saw the club allow four runs in the ninth and a walk-off homer.
Maybe even more concerning is the injury status of manager Dave Roberts’ star players. After placing Shohei Ohtani on the injured list on Friday with knee and biceps ailments, Roberts announced plans to keep first baseman Freddie Freeman out of the lineup on Monday as he deals with right knee tendinitis.
“(Freddie) is obviously not moving as well as he’s used to,” Roberts said. “I’ll give him a chance to recover and then he’ll be back in there on Tuesday. He’s doing everything he can to prepare, but it’s been obvious the last week that he’s not himself in the box.”
Freeman, 37, sat on Wednesday and Friday before returning to the lineup and going 0-for-8 the last two games. The 10-time All-Star is batting .293 with 16 home runs and 66 RBIs this season.
Tarik Skubal (9-7, 2.84 ERA) will make his eighth start since being traded from Detroit to the Dodgers and his second against the Reds in as many appearances. The 29-year-old tossed 7 1/3 innings of two-run, four-hit ball against Cincinnati on Tuesday. The left-hander struck out five and walked two in a 3-2 win.
Skubal has a 2.93 ERA with the Dodgers and has surrendered two earned runs or fewer in four of his last five starts. Still, the two-time American League Cy Young Award winner believes he has more to give. Coming off the longest outing of his short Los Angeles career, Skubal is beginning to live up to his lofty expectations.
“I think that’s ultimately the job of a starting pitcher,” Skubal said of his longest start with the Dodgers on Tuesday. “One, to give your team a chance to win every time you’re out there, and two, to eat as many innings as you can. … I don’t think I’ve thrown the ball as well as I know I’m capable of yet.”
Skubal is 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA in two career starts against the Reds.
With only a few starts left in what’s been a lackluster year, Nick Lodolo (3-4, 5.12) is hoping to correct an inconsistent personal stretch for the Reds (70-79). The 28-year-old has battled through a pair of stints on the injured list due to a blister on his left index finger.
Since returning on Aug. 11, Lodolo has failed to complete five innings in four of six starts. The left-hander faced Skubal and the Dodgers in a losing effort on Tuesday, when he allowed three runs on five hits across 4 2/3 frames. He struck out six and walked three, extending a seven-start stretch without a win.
“I thought early, he wasn’t commanding the ball,” Reds manager Terry Francona said of Lodolo’s last start. “When he got into the third, fourth and fifth (inning), I actually thought he got better. I really wanted him to get through that fifth. I thought it would have been good for him.”
In three career starts against Los Angeles, Lodolo is 0-2 with a 5.52 ERA.
–Field Level Media

title: Los Dodgers se aseguran el pase a los playoffs y aspiran a su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva
author: AFP
body:
Los Dodgers se aseguran el pase a los playoffs y aspiran a su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva
El equipo de Los Ángeles se encuentra actualmente en posición de asegurarse uno de los dos primeros puestos de la Liga Nacional junto a los Milwaukee Brewers, que también tienen garantizada una plaza en la postemporada. En la Liga Americana, los Tampa Bay Rays ya se han clasificado.
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, que aspiran a su tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial, aseguraron el lunes su plaza en los playoffs tras imponerse por 4-1 a los Reds de Cincinnati. Con un récord de 91-59 y 12 partidos por disputar en la temporada regular, los Dodgers tienen ahora asegurada, como mínimo, una plaza en la serie de comodines.
Los Dodgers se encuentran actualmente en posición de asegurarse uno de los dos primeros puestos de la Liga Nacional —lo que les da derecho a saltarse la primera ronda y a la ventaja de jugar en casa en la serie divisional— junto con los Milwaukee Brewers, que también tienen asegurada su plaza en la postemporada. En la Liga Americana, los Tampa Bay Rays ya se han clasificado.
Los Dodgers, con su generosa inversión, vencieron a los Yankees de Nueva York en la Serie Mundial de 2024 y se impusieron a los Blue Jays de Toronto el año pasado.
Los fichajes de Skubal y Kyle Tucker convierten a los Dodgers en favoritos aún más claros
Tras incorporar al jardinero Kyle Tucker durante la temporada baja y al lanzador Tarik Skubal —ganador en dos ocasiones del Premio Cy Young— el mes pasado, los Dodgers son los favoritos para completar su triplete.
Podrían convertirse en el primer equipo de la Liga Nacional en ganar la Serie Mundial tres años seguidos y el primero desde los Yankees de 1998 a 2000. Pero llegar a los playoffs por decimocuarta temporada consecutiva no ha sido precisamente un camino de rosas.
Una temporada de altibajos
Tras llegar al parón del All-Star con una ventaja de 11,5 partidos sobre Arizona en la división Oeste de la Liga Nacional —con diferencia, el mayor margen de cualquier líder de división—, los Dodgers sufrieron un bajón de forma. La superestrella polivalente Shohei Ohtani ha estado de baja por lesiones, y no se espera que vuelva a lanzar esta temporada; su rendimiento al bate también ha bajado.
Sin embargo, una racha reciente de ocho victorias consecutivas —la mejor de la temporada— ha restablecido la considerable ventaja de los Dodgers al frente de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. Sus rivales más cercanos por uno de los dos primeros puestos son los Atlanta Braves de la División Este de la Liga Nacional.
Kyle Tucker y Teoscar Hernández conectaron sendos jonrones en la cómoda victoria de los Dodgers el lunes por la noche en Cincinnati.

title: Henriquez (back) hits IL, while Díaz's Triple-A struggles further complicate LA's bullpen woes
author: Sonja Chen
body:
CINCINNATI -- At one point this season, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts proclaimed his "trust tree" of high-leverage bullpen arms to be as large as it had been in quite some time. But in the final two weeks before the postseason, his proverbial tree has grown far more bare.
The Dodgers lost hard-throwing right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, who had emerged as one of the team's most reliable relievers, to the 15-day injured list due to lower back discomfort before Monday's postseason-clinching 4-1 win over the Reds.
Henriquez is not eligible to return during the regular season, but the Dodgers are hopeful he could return for the playoffs. The team will know more after Henriquez undergoes imaging on his back and side.
The loss of Henriquez came after Roberts acknowledged that the rehabbing Edwin Díaz could be pitching himself out of a postseason bullpen role if he does not show improvement in what could be his final rehab outing with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday.
Right-handers Paul Gervase and Bobby Miller were recalled from Triple-A to shore up the bullpen on Monday.
As the most important games of the year draw near, the Dodgers' bullpen situation is starting to feel similar to last year, when they had more questions than answers for piecing together the late innings.
Henriquez posted a 2.85 ERA through 60 innings, striking out 71 against 25 walks. He hit 103 mph or higher 17 times, more than any Major League pitcher not named Jacob Misiorowski (140 pitches) or Mason Miller (33 pitches). But Henriquez became more than just a hard thrower this year, developing the command and the confidence to be a leverage weapon for the Dodgers.
With Díaz on the IL as he deals with inflammation on the right side of his neck, the Dodgers have not had a set closer, although Tanner Scott has gotten the bulk of save situations. Henriquez established himself as not only part of the bridge to the ninth inning, but also as a legitimate option to close out games.
"He’s got just really electric stuff, and in the ninth inning that stuff plays," Roberts said earlier this month. "In all honesty, there’s four or five guys that I feel can finish a game. But yeah, Edgardo is certainly high up the rungs."
The Dodgers have not seen enough from Díaz on his rehab assignment -- which was initially expected to span just a couple of outings -- to bring him back to the bullpen, further complicating the leverage picture.
Through four outings with Oklahoma City, Díaz has allowed six earned runs in 3 1/3 innings. He has struggled mightily with his command, issuing seven walks against four strikeouts. The hope was that he could use the stint in the Minors to work on his mechanical issues, but it is unclear whether he has made much progress.
Accordingly, it's questionable whether the Dodgers can afford to carry this version of Díaz on the postseason roster.
"We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff," Roberts said. "My bet is that he will be [on the postseason roster]. But again, there's got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. So my bet is yes, but we still got to see something."
Díaz is on his second IL stint of the year after having surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April. In the first season of his three-year, $69 million contract with the Dodgers, Díaz has recorded an 11.85 ERA and blown four of his 11 save opportunities.
Roberts has already said that Díaz is set to pitch in lower leverage, rather than return to the closer role, when he's activated. If Díaz can earn back the ninth inning -- or any leverage opportunities -- it would partially solve the Dodgers' growing bullpen problem. But it comes down to whether he can perform when called on.
"He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good," Roberts said. "He's going to pitch on Wednesday, and so I guess we'll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it's like, where we're at, there's got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He wants to pitch well."

title: Teoscar Hernández apunta al tercer título consecutivo de los Dodgers - Momento Deportivo RD
author: Hector Garcia Sr
body:
Por Luis Tomás Rae
Teoscar Hernández asegura que los Dodgers de Los Ángeles no han perdido de vista el objetivo más ambicioso de la temporada: convertirse en el primer equipo en décadas en conquistar tres Series Mundiales consecutivas.
El dominicano, campeón con Los Ángeles en 2024 y 2025, atraviesa además un repunte ofensivo en el tramo final de la campaña, producto, según explicó, de un ajuste sencillo en su enfoque.
“Es tratar de buscar una forma de llegar al home plate, a tratar de sentirme cómodo, de tener más tiempo, de mirar la pelota, de calmarme un poquito más y, gracias a Dios, las cosas empezaron a salir”, dijo Hernández.
Sobre la posibilidad de alcanzar un tercer campeonato consecutivo, fue directo:
“Obviamente sí. Sí, al principio del año, los entrenamientos, esa es la meta que nos trazamos desde el día uno”. Subrayo Teoscar al ser entrevistado por Ronald Guevara para “Luis Tomás en los Deportes” del Canal 10 de Musa Visión del Telecable de Puerto Plata.
Hernández, quien también recibió un anillo por el campeonato de Houston en 2017 aunque no participó con el club durante esa postemporada, admitió que cambiaría uno de sus títulos por conquistar el Clásico Mundial de Béisbol con República Dominicana.

title: Tarik Skubal silences Reds as Dodgers clinch 14th straight playoff berth
author: Int-No Author
body:
Tarik Skubal threw seven scoreless innings and Teoscar Hernandez hit a two-run homer as the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 4-1 on Monday night to clinch a playoff spot.
Skubal (10-7) allowed three hits — all singles — while striking out nine and walking one for Los Angeles (91-59), which earned a postseason berth for the 14th straight year and pulled within two games of the Milwaukee Brewers for the National League’s best record. Skubal is 2-0 with a 1.73 ERA in his last four starts.
Nick Lodolo (3-5) threw seven innings of four-run, three-hit ball as he struck out four and walked four in his longest outing of the season. The left-hander’s personal winless stretch extended to eight starts in the loss.
Elly De La Cruz connected for his 27th homer of the year in the ninth inning for the Reds’ only run. Cincinnati (70-80) has dropped six of its last seven and its elimination number dropped to one.
Los Angeles struck first in the second inning as Kyle Tucker belted a solo homer — his 15th of the season and his third in his last five games.
Tucker worked a two-out walk in the fourth and scored on Hernandez’s two-run homer that gave the Dodgers a 3-0 edge.
The Reds threatened in the fifth. Juan Brito singled and JJ Bleday walked with one out, but Skubal struck out Ke’Bryan Hayes and Hector Rodriguez to keep Cincinnati off the board.
After Hernandez walked and stole second in the seventh, Enrique Hernandez lined an RBI single to center to make it 4-0.
Luis Mey tossed a perfect eighth in relief of Lodolo.
Alex Vesia entered for Skubal and threw a clean eighth. In the ninth, Evan Phillips struck out pinch hitter Carlos Jorge before allowing De La Cruz’s 457-foot blast to center. Phillips then retired Sal Stewart and Tyler Stephenson to end the game.

title: MLB: Con brillante salida de Tarik Skubal Dodgers de Los Ángeles clasificaron a la postemporada 2026 - Noticias Barquisimeto
author: Hender Gonzalez
body:
El zurdo se mostró imponente frente a Cincinnati, en una de sus mejores aperturas del 2026.
Una joya de pitcheo de Tarik Skubal (10-7) este lunes en el Great American Ball Park, le dio el triunfo a los Dodgers de los Ángeles 4×1 frente a los Rojos de Cincinnati. Triunfo que le permitió a la novena californiana inscribir su nombre en la postemporada 2026 del mejor béisbol del mundo.
Leer También: MLB: El Venezolano Luis Lara de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee se llevó la Jugada de la Semana
El zurdo no le concedió mayores libertades a la toletería de Cincinnati, maniatándolos por completo durante 7.0 capítulos en los que le conectaron sólo tres inatrapables, otorgó un boleto y abanicó a nueve contrarios, dejó su efectividad en 2.70 y su WHIP en 0.95.
Skubal, quien llegó a Los Ángeles desde Detroit en medio de la temporada, completó la que hasta ahora ha sido su mejor apertura desde que se sumó a los líderes del Oeste del Viejo Circuito.
Postemporada 14 al hilo
Tras la victoria frente a los Rojos, los dirigidos por Dave Roberts hicieron oficial su clasificación a la postemporada por vez número 14 de forma consecutiva. En ese lapso sólo perdieron el banderín de su División en una ocasión, fue en la temporada 2021 cuando con récord de 106-56 escoltaron a los Gigantes de San Francisco (107-55).
Ahora el objetivo principal de los Dodgers (91-59) en esta recta final de temporada regular, será arrebatarle el mejor registro de la Liga Nacional a los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, equipo que actualmente juega para 93 triunfos por 57 descalabros.
Hender «Vivo» González

title: Dodgers put Edgardo Henriquez (back) on IL
author: Thomson Reuters
body:
By Field Level Media
Sep 15 (Field Level Media) – The Los Angeles Dodgers put relief pitcher Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list due to lower back discomfort on Monday, ending the right-hander’s regular season and causing more upheaval for the team’s bullpen.
Los Angeles has also been nursing Edwin Diaz back in a slow recovery from right elbow surgery with recent Triple-A outings that have not proven successful.
In his most recent appearance for Oklahoma City, Diaz struggled through two- thirds of an inning on Sunday, allowing five runs and three walks in a performance that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts admitted wasn’t going to be enough to merit a promotion.
The Dodgers have left open the possibility for Henriquez to return in the postseason.
Henriquez, 24, has appeared in 61 games (one start) this season, posting a 2.85 ERA with 71 strikeouts against 25 walks in 60 innings.
Diaz, a three-time All-Star, has struggled this season in limited action, logging seven saves in 11 opportunities and an 11.85 ERA in 16 appearances.
Los Angeles recalled right-handed pitchers Paul Gervase and Bobby Miller from Triple-A to help shore up their shaky bullpen. Emmet Sheehan was sent to Oklahoma City after throwing six shutout innings in a start against the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
Gervase, 26, has a 2.35 ERA over four major league appearances this season. He owns a lifetime 3.38 ERA with no decisions in 10 outings, all in relief, for the Tampa Bay Rays (2025) and Los Angeles (2025-26).
Miller, 27, has made one big-league appearance in 2026, earning a win over the Washington Nationals on Sept. 6 with three innings of one-run relief. He is 14-8 with a 5.40 ERA in 38 outings (36 starts) for the Dodgers over parts of four seasons.
Sheehan, 26, is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 starts this year, 15-12 with a 4.23 ERA in 50 career appearances (45 starts), all with Los Angeles.
(–Field Level Media)

title: Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster
author: Maddie Lee
body:
Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster
-    Click here to listen to this article
-   
- Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” from the closer to put him on the playoff roster.
- The Dodgers placed reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list and recalled Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase.
CINCINNATI — Even as the Dodgers clinched a postseason berth with their 4-1 win over the Reds on Monday, bullpen uncertainty loomed.
When they get to the playoffs, who’s going to take the ball in high-leverage situations?
Their options are dwindling. Edgardo Henriquez landed on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ruling him out for the rest of the regular season. Edwin Díaz was so shaky in his rehab assignment Sunday that a spot on the postseason roster isn’t guaranteed.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” manager Dave Roberts said before the Dodgers opened a four-game series against the Reds. “So my bet is that he will be [on the roster]. But there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us to sort of bet on. And so my bet is, yes, but we’ve still got to see something.”
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
Díaz (neck) had the worst outing of his triple-A rehab assignment, surrendering five runs and issuing two walks in two-thirds of an inning. The dud put his return timeline in doubt. His next rehab appearance is scheduled for Wednesday.
“I think the world of him, the baseball card looks great,” Roberts said. “But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well. So for me, Wednesday, we’ll be watching closely.”
So, who’s still in play?
Tanner Scott remains Roberts’ go-to in save situations. And Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Jack Dreyer and Blake Treinen all have experience in late innings.
On Monday, starter Tarik Skubal gave the group a much-needed break with seven shutout innings. He limited the Reds to three hits and a walk, cruising through their lineup almost three times in 90 pitches.
The Dodgers pulled ahead by four runs, on home runs from Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández, who have both broken out of slumps, and an RBI single from Kiké Hernández.
With the game still relatively tight, Vesia entered in the bottom of the eighth to face the left-handed heavy bottom of the order. He retired the side.
Phillips and Treinen both were warming in the ninth when the Dodgers got a runner to second base with one out. When they failed to score him, Phillips jogged in to face the top of the order. He surrendered a high-flying solo homer to Elly De La Cruz on a fastball above the zone but avoided further damage.
Before the game, the Dodgers added two fresh arms to the bullpen. They recalled right-handers Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase, as they put Henriquez on the IL and optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan.
Henriquez will undergo imaging on the area, which Roberts said stretched to his side near his oblique.
“The hope is we’ll get him back in the postseason,” Roberts said.
Roberts said he didn’t know what the move meant for Sheehan, who in his past two starts limited opponents to one run and recorded 15 strikeouts in a combined 11 ⅔ innings.
“Some of it’s probably contingent on Roki [Sasaki], and we’ve got another start coming up down the road here, as far as a bullpen kind of situation,” Roberts said. “So I don’t know, but Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. The last two have been really good.”
Sasaki (right middle finger blister) could start Thursday. His bullpen session Monday marked the first time he had tested covering the sensitive area on his finger with Dermabond, Roberts said.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward,” Roberts said.
The Dodgers also have more bullpen reinforcements coming.
Another bullpen addition is left-hander Kris Bubic, who met the team in Cincinnati and is in place to make his Dodgers debut later this week. Bubic made his last rehab appearance for triple-A Oklahoma City on Sunday, so Roberts said the Dodgers likely won’t activate him off the 60-day injured list until Wednesday at the earliest.
The Dodgers acquired Bubic from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline this year. He’d been on the IL since May, first with a low-grade flexor strain in his left forearm, and then a shoulder impingement setback.
In six triple-A rehab appearances over 5⅔ innings, Bubic didn’t yield a run and he limited opponents to two hits and two walks.
Roberts was noncommittal about Bubic being a high-leverage option.
“Seems like all of our games are leverage these days,” he said.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.

Phillips and Treinen both were warming in the ninth when the Dodgers got a runner to second base with one out. When they failed to score him, Phillips jogged in to face the top of the order. He surrendered a high-flying solo homer to Elly De La Cruz on a fastball above the zone but avoided further damage.
Before the game, the Dodgers added two fresh arms to the bullpen. They recalled right-handers Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase, as they put Henriquez on the IL and optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan.
Henriquez will undergo imaging on the area, which Roberts said stretched to his side near his oblique.
“The hope is we’ll get him back in the postseason,” Roberts said.
Roberts said he didn’t know what the move meant for Sheehan, who in his past two starts limited opponents to one run and recorded 15 strikeouts in a combined 11 ⅔ innings.
“Some of it’s probably contingent on Roki [Sasaki], and we’ve got another start coming up down the road here, as far as a bullpen kind of situation,” Roberts said. “So I don’t know, but Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. The last two have been really good.”
Sasaki (right middle finger blister) could start Thursday. His bullpen session Monday marked the first time he had tested covering the sensitive area on his finger with Dermabond, Roberts said.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward,” Roberts said.
The Dodgers also have more bullpen reinforcements coming.
Another bullpen addition is left-hander Kris Bubic, who met the team in Cincinnati and is in place to make his Dodgers debut later this week. Bubic made his last rehab appearance for triple-A Oklahoma City on Sunday, so Roberts said the Dodgers likely won’t activate him off the 60-day injured list until Wednesday at the earliest.
The Dodgers acquired Bubic from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline this year. He’d been on the IL since May, first with a low-grade flexor strain in his left forearm, and then a shoulder impingement setback.
In six triple-A rehab appearances over 5⅔ innings, Bubic didn’t yield a run and he limited opponents to two hits and two walks.
Roberts was noncommittal about Bubic being a high-leverage option.
“Seems like all of our games are leverage these days,” he said.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.

title: Elly's ballpark-fleeing blast highlights otherwise tough night for Reds' bats
author: Mike Petraglia
body:
CINCINNATI – On a night when they were nearly blanked for a Major League-leading 17th time, the Reds were once again reminded of what a playoff team looks like across the field in the other dugout.
The only thing standing between the Reds and another goose egg was a monumental home run from Elly De La Cruz with one out in the ninth. The 98 mph fastball from Evan Phillips was actually above the strike zone. De La Cruz crushed it a Statcast-projected 457 feet, the third-longest home run of his career and the longest by a Red this season.
“Maybe I'll pick it up on the way home,” joked Reds manager Terry Francona. “That's pretty impressive. It’d be a lot more fun to talk about if it put us ahead … but it was still impressive.”
The homer, De La Cruz’s 27th, soared into the alley between the bleachers in right-center and the right tall stack as fans looked into the back of the stands to get a glimpse of the ball actually landing. It also extended De La Cruz’s season-long on-base streak to 21 games, the longest active streak in MLB and the second-longest of his career.
But for highlights, that was it for the Reds.
The real frustration of this season was encapsulated by starter Nick Lodolo coming out after six innings, allowing four runs on just three hits. He went over to the ball bag and slammed his right hand into it twice out of anger.
The reason?
Free passes. Lodolo walked four and struck out four while allowing four runs on just three hits in seven innings.
“I think [two of the] walks I had scored,” Lodolo said. “Obviously not every walk you have is going to score every night, but it's something that this year that has killed me. I was just frustrated with it.”
“Oh, I don't care. I don't,” Francona said of Lodolo's reaction. “I care what they do on the mound. I don't care about hitting the ball bag.
“Three hits, but you know, two of them left the ballpark, [and one] after a walk. But still ... it's a dangerous team over there. We got behind the wrong guy.”
Lodolo (3-5) made two mistakes on the night. A 1-0 fastball left up to Kyle Tucker, who crushed it down the right-field line for a 1-0 Dodgers lead in the second. His second mistake -- a first-pitch 91.6 mph fastball that Teoscar Hernández lifted just over the fence in right-center for a two-run roundtripper and a 3-0 Dodgers lead in the fourth, after a walk to Tucker.
That was more than enough for Tarik Skubal (10-7), the big addition that the Dodgers traded for at the Deadline. He blanked the Reds on three hits, striking out nine and walking one in seven innings.
“Obviously, one of the best pitchers in the league, if not the best,” Lodolo said. “So you know that going into the game. But regardless who's on the other side, I'm more worried about doing my job and letting our guys handle that. My job is to keep us in the game, give us a chance to win. ... When a guy's rolling like that, you're trying to match it.”
Before the tape-measure blast from De La Cruz in the ninth, the Reds had one threat all night. In the fifth, they had Juan Brito at third and JJ Bleday at second with two outs. But Skubal fanned Héctor Rodríguez to keep Cincinnati off the scoreboard.
Frustration has been a common theme in the past week, as the Reds have dropped six of their past seven games, including four to the Dodgers.
Ironically, the win by the Dodgers Monday night at Great American Ball Park clinched their 14th straight playoff appearance. In those 14 years, the Reds have qualified for the playoffs just three times, including last year, when the Dodgers started their run to a second straight World Series title with a two-game sweep of the Reds in the NL Wild Card round.

title: Claves: La rodilla de Freeman, el bate de Ohtani y el cálculo de octubre de Dodgers
author: JOE REEDY
body:
Claves: La rodilla de Freeman, el bate de Ohtani y el cálculo de octubre de Dodgers
CINCINNATI — Freddie Freeman no estuvo en la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para el juego del lunes por la noche contra los Rojos de Cincinnati mientras lidia con molestias en la rodilla derecha.
Aunque el primera base no ha estado en la alineación en tres de los últimos cinco juegos, el mánager Dave Roberts manifestó que poner a Freeman en la lista de lesionados de 10 días para dejarlo listo para la postemporada —algo similar a lo que hicieron con Shohei Ohtani— no es una opción en este momento.
“No creo que (el descanso) tenga que ser de 10 días, pero ¿podría ser más de uno? Esa es una pregunta válida. Tengo que hablar un poco con el cuerpo de preparadores, con Freddie, y al final tomar esa decisión. Pero no creo que la lista de lesionados tenga sentido”, comentó Roberts.
Roberts señaló que no creía que Freeman fuera a tener problemas persistentes con la rodilla durante la postemporada si se puede manejar adecuadamente. Freeman batea para .293, pero está de 3 en sus últimos 30 turnos, con nueve ponches.
Los campeones defensores de la Serie Mundial por segundo año consecutivo llegaron al lunes por la noche con un número mágico de cuatro para asegurar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años. Su mayor preocupación es asegurarse de amarrar uno de los dos primeros puestos de preclasificación y un pase directo en la primera ronda.
Los Dodgers (90-59) llegaron al lunes con una ventaja de 2 1/2 juegos sobre Atlanta por el segundo puesto. Milwaukee (93-57) tiene la mejor marca de la Liga Nacional.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en cuanto a salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, expresó Roberts.
Ohtani, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho, hará swings desde un tee en Los Ángeles el martes. Serán sus primeros swings desde que ingresó a la lista de lesionados. Roberts indicó que Ohtani ha estado levantando pesas, entrenando y recibiendo tratamiento en los últimos días.
Con Ohtani fuera del viaje de siete juegos, definitivamente ha habido un ambiente distinto en el clubhouse.
“Se siente diferente porque él tiene mucha presencia cuando está en el campo. La última serie no fue indicativa, pero creo que en general estamos jugando buen béisbol. Sabemos que somos mejores con Shohei. Probablemente los aficionados estén decepcionados, pero no creo que nosotros realmente lo hayamos sentido”, dijo Roberts.
La mayor preocupación podría estar con el relevista Edwin Díaz, quien ha permitido seis carreras limpias en 3 1/3 entradas en cuatro apariciones de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Díaz no solo está lidiando con una inflamación en el cuello, sino también con problemas de control. Díaz firmó un contrato de 59 millones de dólares por tres años durante la temporada baja y ha tenido dificultades en su primer año en Los Ángeles.
El derecho tendrá otra salida el miércoles, pero Roberts sí dejó abierta la posibilidad de que Díaz quede fuera de los rosters de postemporada.
“Necesita lanzar mejor. No ha sido bueno. La tarjeta de béisbol se ve genial. Pero, tal como estamos, tiene que haber algo a lo que podamos aferrarnos. Y él lo sabe. Quiere lanzar bien”, afirmó Roberts.
__

title: Dodgers news: Edgardo Henriquez placed on regular season-ending IL
author: Josh Davis; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Edgardo Henriquez placed on regular season-ending IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed right-hander Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ending his 2026 regular season. Los Angeles recalled Bobby Miller from Triple-A Oklahoma City as the corresponding roster move.
Henriquez had developed into a regular bullpen option during his first full major league season, making 61 appearances. MLB.com's Sonja Chen took to X, formerly Twitter, shortly after the club announced the transaction and noted the calendar implications of Henriquez's IL placement.
"Henriquez going on the 15-day IL ends his regular season."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Henriquez last pitched Sunday vs. the Miami Marlins, allowing two earned runs on three hits and one walk over two-thirds of an inning. He also recorded one strikeout and received credit for a hold in Los Angeles' 6-4 loss.
The 24-year-old right-hander finishes the regular season with a 4-1 record and 2.85 ERA across 61 games, including one start. The right-hander struck out 71 and walked 25 over 60 innings while posting a 1.03 WHIP. His 61 appearances ranked 24th in the National League.
The timing of the move prevents Henriquez from returning before the regular season concludes September 27. A 15-day placement Monday makes him eligible to return September 29, when the Wild Card Series begins. The move does not automatically rule him out for the postseason if he recovers and earns a roster spot.
The Dodgers have not announced an MRI result, structural diagnosis, or surgery related to Henriquez's back discomfort. His absence removes another pitcher from a Dodgers staff already dealing with multiple injuries, including Shohei Ohtani's right biceps inflammation.
Miller joins the active roster as Los Angeles continues its four-game road series against the Cincinnati Reds. Henriquez's regular season is over, but the Dodgers could still have the right-hander available for the postseason depending on his recovery.
Related: Dodgers tie historic streak with Reds series opener takedown
Related: Tarik Skubal helps Dodgers clinch 14th-straight playoff berth

Henriquez had developed into a regular bullpen option during his first full major league season, making 61 appearances. MLB.com's Sonja Chen took to X, formerly Twitter, shortly after the club announced the transaction and noted the calendar implications of Henriquez's IL placement.
"Henriquez going on the 15-day IL ends his regular season."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Henriquez last pitched Sunday vs. the Miami Marlins, allowing two earned runs on three hits and one walk over two-thirds of an inning. He also recorded one strikeout and received credit for a hold in Los Angeles' 6-4 loss.
The 24-year-old right-hander finishes the regular season with a 4-1 record and 2.85 ERA across 61 games, including one start. The right-hander struck out 71 and walked 25 over 60 innings while posting a 1.03 WHIP. His 61 appearances ranked 24th in the National League.
The timing of the move prevents Henriquez from returning before the regular season concludes September 27. A 15-day placement Monday makes him eligible to return September 29, when the Wild Card Series begins. The move does not automatically rule him out for the postseason if he recovers and earns a roster spot.
The Dodgers have not announced an MRI result, structural diagnosis, or surgery related to Henriquez's back discomfort. His absence removes another pitcher from a Dodgers staff already dealing with multiple injuries, including Shohei Ohtani's right biceps inflammation.
Miller joins the active roster as Los Angeles continues its four-game road series against the Cincinnati Reds. Henriquez's regular season is over, but the Dodgers could still have the right-hander available for the postseason depending on his recovery.

title: Edgardo Henriquez a la lista de lesionados
author: Luis Viscaya
body:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles colocaron este lunes en lista de incapacitados a Edgardo Henriquez, las constantes molestias que ha venido sufriendo en su espalda en días recientes el venezolano llevó a los californianos a tomar la decisión.
Esta lesión llega en medio de la mejor campaña que ha tenido el diestro desde su debut en Las Mayores en el año 2024. En la presente temporada, el sucrense ha visto acción en 61 encuentros, con marca de 4-1, efectividad de 2.85 y 71 guillotinados en 60.0 episodios de labor.
El lugar del criollo será ocupado por el también derecho, Bobby Miller, quien fue llamado del Oklahoma City Comets, sucursal AAA de los actuales campeones de la Gran Carpa.
Miller, en 2026 cuenta con récord de 2-0 y un altísimo porcentaje de carreras limpias permitidas de 6.32 en 15.2 entradas.

title: Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, could be left off Dodgers’ postseason roster
author: Fabian Ardaya
body:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers set out this winter to address the closer position for good. Instead, they’re facing the possibility that a reliever they signed as a star free agent will be excluded from their postseason plans for a second consecutive season.
Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, as Tanner Scott did a year ago, and his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City has gone poorly enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Monday the club could leave the three-time All-Star closer off the postseason roster. Against minor-leaguers Sunday, Díaz surrendered five runs, walked three, hit a batter and recorded just two outs in his worst appearance yet.
Advertisement
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said. “So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
The Dodgers gave Díaz three years and $69 million to address a bullpen that floundered in 2025. They won their second consecutive World Series despite Scott — who signed a four-year, $72 million contract — not appearing in a single playoff game.
A second plunge into the deep end of the relief market brought even worse results than the 4.74 ERA and league-worst 10 blown saves Scott had in 2025. Díaz’s famous trumpets have sounded more like a sad trombone.
Díaz’s 16 appearances with the Dodgers yielded a disastrous 11.85 ERA. He missed three months due to arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies in his right elbow. Upon his return, he struggled enough that the Dodgers almost immediately put him back on the injured list for what they called a neck issue. They believed his struggles were mechanical, citing the lowest arm angle of his career (14.9 degrees) as a reason his stuff and command were nowhere near where they needed to be.
Attempts to correct the issue have not worked. What was supposed to be a pair of rehab outings has been extended. The organization thought Sunday’s outing could be the final step before activation, with Díaz joining the team in Cincinnati this week to try to re-earn his closer’s job.
But Díaz has allowed six runs and walked seven of the 21 batters he’s faced since starting his rehab. Even more concerning is how Díaz’s delivery seems even more out of whack than before. His fastball still lacks the north-south movement that it needs to succeed. On that pitch this season, he’s averaged 11.8 inches of induced vertical break, which measures how much “hop” or “ride” the pitch generates. The 15 fastballs he threw Sunday generated just 9.7 inches of IVB.
There’s plenty for Díaz to fix, and not a lot of time.
Advertisement
“He needs to pitch better,” Roberts said. “I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it’s like, where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well.”
So the Dodgers summoned rehabbing reliever Kris Bubic to join the big club Monday instead. Bubic is expected to pitch as soon as Wednesday, Roberts said. Bubic, a former All-Star starting pitcher with the Kansas City Royals, was acquired at the trade deadline and has thrown 5 2/3 scoreless innings with nine strikeouts on his rehab assignment since the trade.
Díaz will stick with Oklahoma City for at least one more outing on Wednesday, and the organization will evaluate from there, Roberts said.
The Dodgers will spend the coming days trying to sort out how they will attack the ninth inning. One option went on the IL on Monday, when the Dodgers placed hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the shelf with a lower back issue; Henriquez has been the Dodgers’ most effective reliever recently, with a 1.69 ERA since Aug. 5. Now, his regular season is over.
Scott, who has bounced back this year with a 2.91 ERA, will be part of fixing the ninth-inning problem they thought they’d avoid entirely when they signed Díaz.

title: Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki gets encouraging injury recovery from Dave Roberts
author: Josh Davis; ClutchPoints
body:
Dodgers news: Roki Sasaki gets encouraging injury recovery from Dave Roberts appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki took an encouraging step Monday in his recovery from a right middle-finger blister, throwing a bullpen session ahead of the club's four-game road series against the Cincinnati Reds beginning Monday. The development keeps the 24-year-old in consideration for a return Thursday vs. the Reds, though the Dodgers have not committed to activating him. The Los Angeles Times' Maddie Lee took to X, formerly Twitter, on Monday afternoon with manager Dave Roberts' latest update.
"Roki Sasaki threw a bullpen today and tested out covering the blister wirh dermabond, Dave Roberts said. He's a possibility for Thursday, but 'we just can't put him in a position to go backwards,' so still TBD."
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since August 27 after the blister opened during his start against the Atlanta Braves one day earlier. He lasted 3 1/3 innings and threw 66 pitches before leaving the game.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Monday's bullpen allowed Sasaki to test Dermabond over the healing blister while throwing. The Dodgers remain cautious because another setback could further delay his return as the regular season enters its final weeks.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA and 117 strikeouts across 119 1/3 innings and 23 starts this season. His results had improved before the injury, as he posted a 3.05 ERA over 38 1/3 innings in seven starts following the All-Star break.
Thursday remains a possible return date rather than a confirmed activation. The Dodgers have an open rotation spot for the series finale against Cincinnati, but Sasaki's availability will depend on how his finger responds following Monday's bullpen session.
The Dogers head into Monday at 90-59 and atop the NL West as it prepares for the postseason. Getting Sasaki healthy would provide another rotation option, but Roberts' update makes clear that the club will not risk reversing his progress simply to fill Thursday's opening.
Related: Dodgers tie historic streak with Reds series opener takedown
Related: Tarik Skubal helps Dodgers clinch 14th-straight playoff berth

title: Freeman (knee soreness) out of lineup again, though likely to avoid IL
author: Sonja Chen
body:
CINCINNATI -- Freddie Freeman was out of the Dodgers' starting lineup for Monday night's series opener against the Reds at Great American Ball Park as the star first baseman continues to manage soreness in his right knee, which he has described as patellar tendinitis.
It marked the third time in the Dodgers' past five games that Freeman was not in the starting nine. Manager Dave Roberts reaffirmed that he does not believe Freeman will go on the injured list, and he's expected to return to the lineup on Tuesday.
"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of -- I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Freeman is essentially day to day moving forward. Roberts believes that Freeman's knee has impacted his offensive performance lately, as the 37-year-old is hitting 3-for-30 (.100) with just one extra-base hit in September.
There is some evidence that the knee has been hindering Freeman for longer, as his power numbers have dropped off over the past couple months. He only has one home run in his past 55 games, and he's slugging .350 in that span.
For most of his power drought, Freeman was still hitting for average and consistently getting on base. But when his overall performance took a dip earlier this month, the Dodgers opted to rest him, knowing how important he will be to their offense in the postseason. Freeman is hitting .293 with an .818 OPS in 142 games this season.
Roberts is hopeful that giving Freeman time off now will make it less likely that he'll have to manage his knee throughout the postseason.
"I think that if we can kind of manage it … depending on how the season goes, as far as the recovery," Roberts said. "And then also in the postseason, there’s more off-days. So I think that just trying to get ahold of it, I think that’s the main thing."
The Dodgers' lineup is far from full strength in mid-September, with a dozen regular-season games remaining. Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day IL due to lingering right biceps and left knee issues and won't be eligible to be activated until Sept. 23. Andy Pages is working his way back from a fracture in his left hand and is also unlikely to return until the final week.
Freeman isn't the only active Dodger who is banged up. Miguel Rojas, who exited early on Sunday after aggravating his right shoulder, was back in the starting lineup on Monday. Rojas is sore but playable, so he'll start against the Reds' left-handed starters this week in Cincinnati.
It's commonly said that every player is dealing with some kind of physical issue, big or small, at this point in the season. Not only have the injuries piled up for the Dodgers of late, but they have affected some of their most important hitters.
But for the Dodgers, who entered Monday a win away from clinching their 14th consecutive postseason berth, the rest of the regular season is less consequential than the games that come after. They will use these final two weeks -- and if they finish with a top-two record in the NL, the bye week -- to get their injured players right in time for the postseason.
"Honestly, I think right now it's front of mind, it's not great," Roberts said. "But I will say this: Once you get to October, athletes have a magical way of feeling better. It happens every single year, where there's that extra adrenaline that athletes get when you get to the postseason.”

"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of -- I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Freeman is essentially day to day moving forward. Roberts believes that Freeman's knee has impacted his offensive performance lately, as the 37-year-old is hitting 3-for-30 (.100) with just one extra-base hit in September.
There is some evidence that the knee has been hindering Freeman for longer, as his power numbers have dropped off over the past couple months. He only has one home run in his past 55 games, and he's slugging .350 in that span.
For most of his power drought, Freeman was still hitting for average and consistently getting on base. But when his overall performance took a dip earlier this month, the Dodgers opted to rest him, knowing how important he will be to their offense in the postseason. Freeman is hitting .293 with an .818 OPS in 142 games this season.
Roberts is hopeful that giving Freeman time off now will make it less likely that he'll have to manage his knee throughout the postseason.
"I think that if we can kind of manage it … depending on how the season goes, as far as the recovery," Roberts said. "And then also in the postseason, there’s more off-days. So I think that just trying to get ahold of it, I think that’s the main thing."
The Dodgers' lineup is far from full strength in mid-September, with a dozen regular-season games remaining. Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day IL due to lingering right biceps and left knee issues and won't be eligible to be activated until Sept. 23. Andy Pages is working his way back from a fracture in his left hand and is also unlikely to return until the final week.
Freeman isn't the only active Dodger who is banged up. Miguel Rojas, who exited early on Sunday after aggravating his right shoulder, was back in the starting lineup on Monday. Rojas is sore but playable, so he'll start against the Reds' left-handed starters this week in Cincinnati.
It's commonly said that every player is dealing with some kind of physical issue, big or small, at this point in the season. Not only have the injuries piled up for the Dodgers of late, but they have affected some of their most important hitters.
But for the Dodgers, who entered Monday a win away from clinching their 14th consecutive postseason berth, the rest of the regular season is less consequential than the games that come after. They will use these final two weeks -- and if they finish with a top-two record in the NL, the bye week -- to get their injured players right in time for the postseason.
"Honestly, I think right now it's front of mind, it's not great," Roberts said. "But I will say this: Once you get to October, athletes have a magical way of feeling better. It happens every single year, where there's that extra adrenaline that athletes get when you get to the postseason.”

title: ¿Cuáles son las lesiones de Shohei Ohtani?
author: Rodrigo Serrano
body:
Shohei Ohtani se ha perdido seis de los últimos siete partidos de Los Angeles Dodgers debido a las lesiones que ha venido arrastrando esta temporada. La primera fue en la rodilla, una molestia que lo alejó del montículo desde principios de julio y que, con poco tiempo para recuperarse antes de los playoffs, hace casi un hecho que no vuelva a lanzar en 2026. Una baja sensible para los Dodgers en el tramo más importante de la campaña, en el que buscan conquistar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.
Shohei Ohtani to be placed on the injured list (left knee, right biceps), Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announces. pic.twitter.com/AG3VlX3TVe
— MLB (@MLB) September 10, 2026
La segunda lesión que sufrió esta temporada fue en el bíceps, una molestia que ha ido empeorando con el paso de las semanas. Ohtani comenzó a sufrir molestias en el cuello como consecuencia de este problema, lo que obligó a los Dodgers a colocarlo en la lista de lesionados y provocó que se perdiera los últimos encuentros. La buena noticia es que el japonés ha estado trabajando para regresar en este cierre de temporada regular y volver a ocupar su puesto como bateador designado de cara a los playoffs de la MLB.
Ohtani será fundamental en las aspiraciones de los Dodgers
Previo al inicio de la serie ante los Reds en Cincinnati, el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, confirmó que Ohtani tiene programado realizar swings desde un tee antes del partido del martes. La actividad representa un paso adelante en su recuperación y mantiene abierta la posibilidad de que pueda regresar a tiempo para ayudar a Los Angeles en los playoffs.
"I think it's important that he does pitch because he has the ability to do it. He's elite."@spillygoat19 shares his thoughts on whether or not he would discourage Shohei Ohtani from pitching in the future.
MLB Network + @NewBalance pic.twitter.com/KqBg6i0pMd
Por fortuna, los Dodgers se prepararon durante la temporada ante una eventual ausencia prolongada de su superestrella. Por esa razón, adquirieron al pitcher Tarik Skubal antes de la fecha límite de intercambios para fortalecer una rotación de lanzadores que buscará llegar en las mejores condiciones a la postemporada.
Shohei Ohtani could resume swinging Monday or Tuesday as he continues recovering from lingering right biceps and left knee issues.
Ohtani is eligible to return from the IL on September 23, giving him a short window to prepare for the postseason.#Dodgers #BlueDynasty pic.twitter.com/l2vdNja7kE
Además, los Dodgers llamó a uno de los mejores prospectos de las Grandes Ligas, Josue De Paula, para aportar a la ofensiva mientras Ohtani se recupera. El pelotero impresionó en sus primeros partidos ante los Marlins, una actuación que le permite a los Dodgers darle mayor tiempo de recuperación a Ohtani con la esperanza de que esté listo para disputar el Clásico de Otoño.

title: Edgardo Henríquez on injured list with back discomfort
author: Eric Stephen
body:
One day after allowing his first runs in four weeks, Dodgers reliever Edgardo Henríquez was placed on the 15-day injured list with lower back discomfort. His regular season is over.
Henríquez has been one of the best relievers on the team this season, with a 2.85 ERA and 2.47 xERA in 61 games, with 71 strikeouts and 25 walks in 60 innings, with a 29.3-percent strikeout rate and only one home run allowed. The 24-year-old leads the Dodgers bullpen in innings and xERA, and is second only to Tanner Scott in strikeouts.
Sunday was a rare rough outing for Henríquez, who allowed three hits, a walk, and two runs in the eighth inning, recording only two outs. Those were the first runs allowed by Henríquez since August 16, snapping a string of 11 consecutive scoreless appearances.
“It’s the confidence he has in his fastball. Everybody knows it’s not easy to hit 103, 104 coming at you with confidence,” outfielder Teoscar Hernández said last week on the Dodgers’ homestand. “That’s been the difference between the Edgardo we saw at the beginning of the year, and the Edgardo we’re seeing right now.”
Whether Henriquez will be ready and available once the postseason starts remains to be seen.
With Henríquez sidelined, Bobby Miller was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. Miller was just optioned last Monday, but he’s able to return before his 15 days are up because he’s replacing an injured player.
Miller pitched once for Oklahoma City after getting optioned, and it was a rough outing, with five runs allowed in 1 2/3 innings on Friday against Sugar Land, with all five runs scored on two home runs by the same player.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Sudden Kyle Tucker News Before Reds Series
author: Michael DeRosa
body:
On Monday, the Los Angeles Dodgers begin their series against the Cincinnati Reds.
The Dodgers will be aiming to get things back on track during this series, as they lost each of their last two games against the Miami Marlins.
Now, as the Dodgers prepare for their series opener against the Reds, they have announced some news regarding Kyle Tucker.
Kyle Tucker Moving Up to Fourth in Dodgers' Batting Order
After batting fifth for Los Angeles in their most recent game against the Marlins, Tucker will now be batting fourth against the Reds.
Tucker moving up in Los Angeles' batting order comes after he went 0-for-4 in each of his last two games. With this, it is a little surprising to see him move up the lineup. Yet, he will now be looking to bounce back against Cincinnati.
Here is the Dodgers' full batting order for their game against the Reds, per Underdog MLB:
T. Edman CF M. Betts SS W. Smith C K. Tucker RF T. Hernández LF M. Rojas 2B M. Muncy 3B E. Hernández 1B J. De Paula DH
Looking at Tucker
Tucker's first season with the Dodgers has been rough. In 141 games this campaign with Los Angeles, he has posted 14 home runs, 65 RBI, and a low .226 batting average. This is after he posted 22 home runs, 73 RBI, and a .266 batting average in 136 games last season the Chicago Cubs.
Yet, Tucker still has time to end the season on a high note. Let's see if he can have a big game against the Reds from here.

title: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Major Max Muncy Change Before Reds Series
author: Michael DeRosa
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up to face the Cincinnati Reds for the first game of their four-game series on Monday.
The Dodgers are entering this game cold, as they lost each of their last two games. Yet, they will now be looking to get things back on track against Cincinnati from here.
As Los Angeles prepares for their series against the Reds, they have announced a significant lineup change regarding Max Muncy.
Los Angeles Dodgers Dropping Max Muncy to Seventh in Batting Order
Muncy is being dropped to seventh in the Dodgers’ batting order for Monday’s game against the Reds. This is after he batted third against the Marlins in their Sunday matchup.
Muncy will also be switching to third base after being Los Angeles’ DH in their last game.
The Dodgers’ batting order for their game against the Marlins is as follows:
T. Edman CF
M. Betts SS
W. Smith C
K. Tucker RF
T. Hernández LF
M. Rojas 2B
M. Muncy 3B
E. Hernández 1B
J. De Paula DH
Looking at Muncy
Muncy dropping to seventh in Los Angeles’ batting order comes after he went 0-for-4 against the Marlins on Sunday, with two strikeouts.
While Muncy struggled last game, he certainly could bounce back against the Reds. Before his hitless performance against the Marlins, he had hits in each of his previous six games. With that, don’t be surprised if he has a strong bounce-back game for Los Angeles on Monday.
Muncy has 28 home runs, 71 RBI, and a .254 batting average in 137 games this season with the Dodgers. He has been a big part of the Dodgers’ offense this season, just like he has been for years now.

T. Edman CF
M. Betts SS
W. Smith C
K. Tucker RF
T. Hernández LF
M. Rojas 2B

J. De Paula DH

Muncy dropping to seventh in Los Angeles’ batting order comes after he went 0-for-4 against the Marlins on Sunday, with two strikeouts.

title: Shohei Ohtani injury; Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has an update before Reds matchup
author: Miracle Dimwesh
body:
Shohei Ohtani will not be in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ lineup again as the team takes a cautious approach with its two-way superstar.
Ohtani has been dealing with soreness in his left knee, right biceps and neck. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts provided an update before Monday’s matchup with the Cincinnati Reds.
Roberts described the decision to rest Ohtani as “proactive.” He also indicated that Ohtani would likely play if the Dodgers were preparing for a postseason game instead.
That distinction explains the Dodgers’ approach. Los Angeles has a comfortable position in the NL West, giving the team more freedom to protect its biggest star.
Ohtani’s season has still been impressive despite the physical issues. He is hitting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs and a .902 OPS in 130 games.
His pitching season is already over, though. Ohtani went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA and 144 strikeouts over 85.2 innings in 14 starts before the Dodgers shut him down on the mound.
Now, Los Angeles must manage his workload on offense as well. Ohtani returned to the lineup earlier this month but struggled during his final stretch before landing on the injured list.
The timing makes the decision easier for the Dodgers. Los Angeles entered Monday with a 90-59 record and a strong lead in the NL West.
The Dodgers are also competing with the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the National League. That makes every game important, but keeping Ohtani healthy for October carries even greater value.
The Reds entered the matchup at 70-79 and are no longer in the NL Central race. They can still create problems for a Dodgers lineup missing its biggest offensive threat.
For now, Roberts appears more concerned with the bigger picture. Ohtani does not need to push through September discomfort if the Dodgers can give him time to recover.
That could mean more rest days in the coming weeks. The Dodgers would rather have a healthy Ohtani in October than risk making his current issues worse in September.
If this were a postseason game, Roberts suggested the decision might be different. For now, the Dodgers are choosing to protect their biggest weapon.

title: Dodgers option Emmet Sheehan, recall Paul Gervase
author: Eric Stephen
body:
The fresh arm express continues to run in September, with Emmet Sheehan optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City ahead of Monday night's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park, one day after he pitched six scoreless innings on Sunday in Miami.
Paul Gervase was called up from Triple-A to give the Dodgers an extra arm in the bullpen, after the Dodgers used four relievers Friday, three on Saturday, and four more on Sunday against the Marlins. Monday is the fourth day of a stretch of 10 game days in a row for the Dodgers, their final extended stretch of games this season.
This had nothing to do with Sheehan's performance, as he allowed only one run in 11 2/3 innings last week after getting called back up from Oklahoma City himself, with 15 strikeouts. But Sheehan is on the outside looking in when it comes to the Dodgers' postseason rotation, and the team might also get Roki Sasaki at some point this week from a blister on his right middle finger.
Gervase last pitched on Friday for Oklahoma City, striking out four in a four-out save in a scoreless outing to close out a win over Sugar Land. On the season, the 6'10 right-hander had a 4.56 ERA and five saves in 38 games in Triple-A, with 66 strikeouts and 35 walks in 47 1/3 innings.
This is the fifth stint in the majors this season for Gervase, who has a 2.35 ERA in four appearances for the Dodgers, with eight strikeouts and five walks in 7 2/3 innings.

title: Dodgers Demote Red-Hot Starting Pitcher in Surprise Move
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan to Triple-A in a surprise move ahead of Monday's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds.
Sheehan has been dominant over his last two starts since returning to the MLB level, allowing a combined one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
However, the Dodgers wanted to bring up a fresh bullpen arm for the beginning of their four-game series in Cincinnati. Thus, Sheehan was the odd man out, with right-handed pitcher Paul Gervase being called up.
Dodgers Option Emmet Sheehan
Sheehan has had a rollercoaster 2026 season that began with much promise. However, the right-hander struggled across his first 20 starts, and was optioned to Triple-A on Aug. 3 after allowing five runs on six hits over 2.2 innings against the Boston Red Sox.
At the time of the demotion, Sheehan's ERA was 5.29. However, he played well across four Triple-A outings and earned another opportunity at the MLB level on Sept. 7 against the Reds.
Sheehan allowed one run over 5.2 innings with a tied-for-career-high 10 strikeouts against Cincinnati. That led to him staying in the rotation for another turn, where he dominated the Marlins on Sunday.
Sheehan is now ineligible to return to the Dodgers before the end of the regular season barring an injury to someone else that would allow him to be called back up.
He'll look to continue to keep his game strong ahead of the postseason, where he could still factor into the team's plans.
“There was a lot of stuff, going down and trying to figure things out in a less stressful place which was nice,” Sheehan said after his start on Sept. 7. “Just getting my delivery locked in and really just making sure I’m hammering it during the week so I can just go out there and compete which I felt I was doing tonight.”
"I’ve been optioned before," he added. "It’s always, 'See what we can do down there, and see what we can do to bring it back up here.'"
Now, he'll have to do that once more.
Dodgers Calling Up Paul Gervase
As for Gervase, the right-hander has made four appearances for the Dodgers at the big league level this season, allowing two runs over 7.2 innings for a 2.35 ERA with eight strikeouts.
Across 38 appearances at Triple-A Oklahoma City, he has a 4.56 ERA with 66 strikeouts over 47.1 innings.
